title: [RT1] Incremental text continuations (umbrella)
description:
UMBRELLA (closes when its three subtasks close). Incremental text continuations: accept target text in chunks as an LLM produces it, extending a SINGLE in-flight utterance with no prosody reset - the core capability that makes ftts conversational rather than merely fast.

THE ARCHITECTURAL GIFT (why this model makes continuations cheap - most AR TTS engines cannot do this without retraining). In x-vector streaming mode the prompt geometry is almost entirely target-text-independent: prefill = 3 role positions + 6 header positions (think/language/speaker-vector/codec markers) + exactly ONE text token (prompt.rs:265-299); ALL remaining text is consumed one hidden state per generated frame from trailing_text_hidden, read by index at generate.rs:876 (utterance.trailing_text_hidden.get(utterance.frames_emitted)), with tts_pad as the fallback when the Vec is exhausted (talker::form_frame_input, generate.rs:882) - and tts_pad is the model's "text is over" signal. Therefore: appending newly arrived text mid-utterance = gathering + projecting the new rows and pushing them onto a Vec, with NO re-prefill, NO KV invalidation, NO position-id surgery. This is the mechanism commercial APIs approximate server-side (Cartesia "continuations": prosody conditioned on prior audio in a context; ElevenLabs websocket input streaming with chunk buffering); here it is native.

THE EXACT GATE THAT KEEPS IT DOCTRINE-CLEAN: chunk-fed synthesis must be BIT-IDENTICAL to whole-text synthesis of the same concatenated text at the same seed, provided the token streams are identical and no underrun stall occurred. Not a tolerance - identity. This puts continuations in the ConformanceExact family: no listening campaign required to ship, because the waveform is provably the same one the already-validated whole-text path produces.

THE ONE REAL SUBTLETY - TOKENIZATION AT CHUNK BOUNDARIES: BPE can merge across a chunk boundary ("Hello " + "world." may tokenize differently than "Hello world."). Industry handles this by contract (ElevenLabs requires chunks to end with a space; Cartesia requires chunks that concatenate into one coherent transcript, ending sentences with punctuation). Our design: the session holds back a trailing partial word until the next chunk or an explicit flush, and the parity gate first asserts token-stream equality (a fixture whose tokenization diverges is an INVALID fixture, reported distinctly - never silently compared). Details in the API subtask.

SCOPE LIMIT: x-vector voices only in v1. ICL mode's prefill interleaves reference codec frames with reference+target text (assemble_icl, prompt.rs:206-256) - its target text is not a pure trailing stream, so ICL continuations are a separate future design (note on bead frankentts-k-voice-cache-i4t territory). Do not block RT1 on it.

SUBTASKS: (1) the append/finish API through FrameGenerator and QwenGenerator; (2) text-underrun stall semantics + rolling admission/budget; (3) the parity gates and metamorphic tests.

EXIT CRITERIA: a session can feed three sentence chunks 500 ms apart and the emitted waveform is byte-identical to feeding the full paragraph at once (same seed, token-safe boundaries); exhausting text with continue=true stalls (never terminates via tts_pad); finish_text releases the terminal tts_eos and the utterance ends exactly as the whole-text path would.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: all three children closed. g6an (append_text/finish_text on trailing_text_hidden, held-back EOS, chunked==whole bit-exact - peer-authored, gate-green), e0wr (AwaitingText stall + rolling admission + stall-aware budget, 7 engine tests + generator stall parity), hsio (every-boundary drip, EOS timing equivalence, seeded boundary fuzz - all EXACT; gate 5 transferred to 7pgn behind edz0's now-landed cold-row seam). Exit criteria: chunk-fed == whole-fed bit-identity proven at the generator seam incl. genuine stalls; underrun stalls never terminate via tts_pad; finish_text releases EOS identically to whole-text. Scope limit honored: x-vector only, ICL rejected explicitly.

title: EPIC Realtime conversation: live streaming, continuations, ftts talk, barge-in
description:
MISSION. Make franken_tts the speaking half of a live spoken conversation between a user and an AI agent running on the same machine: microphone -> franken_whisper (live transcripts) -> agent LLM -> ftts (this epic) -> speaker, with barge-in. This epic is pure orchestration: NO numerics change anywhere inside it. The engine already runs faster than real time (RTF 1.4-1.6x on M4 Pro under load, README v0.1.4 notes); every remaining real-time blocker is wiring, not kernels.

WHY THIS IS TRACTABLE NOW (verified in-tree 2026-08-21):
1. The codec decode is ALREADY pipelined with generation on a bounded channel and is fully causal with zero lookahead (crates/ftts-cli/src/synth.rs:1583-1660; CodecStreamingState at codec.rs:1950, bit-identical streaming==offline under every packet schedule is a standing gate). The gap is purely that every layer above the codec worker buries packets in a Vec and returns the utterance whole (synth.rs:1628, ftts-cli/src/lib.rs:1714, resident.rs:780-793, ftts-ffi, ftts-wasm).
2. A complete, tested, UNUSED streaming transport exists in ftts-core: PcmPacket / StreamQueues / BoundedSender with backpressure-park and cancel-aware send (ftts-core/src/lib.rs:237-338, exercised only by tests/streaming_failures.rs). We arm it instead of designing a new one.
3. CancellationToken is checked every 80 ms frame (ftts-core/src/lib.rs:870) but NOTHING in production ever calls .cancel(). Barge-in needs a trigger, not a mechanism.
4. THE ARCHITECTURAL GIFT: the Qwen3-TTS talker consumes target text ONE hidden state per generated frame from trailing_text_hidden (generate.rs:876), and the x-vector streaming prefill is 10 positions (3 role + 6 header + first text token, prompt.rs:265-299) and text-independent past token one. Therefore Cartesia-style "continuations" (append newly arrived LLM sentences mid-utterance with no prosody reset) require NO re-prefill and NO KV invalidation - just appending projected rows to a Vec the generator indexes by frames_emitted. This is better than any commercial TTS API can do, and it comes with an EXACT gate: chunk-fed synthesis must be bit-identical to whole-text synthesis at the same seed (given identical token streams). Continuations ship under ConformanceExact discipline, no listening campaign needed.

STRUCTURE. Three phases, each an umbrella feature bead whose subtasks block it (project convention: children block their parent/epic):
- RT0 "arm what's built": live packet emission (frankentts-arnd), armed cancellation (frankentts-3xk2), persistent warm engine (frankentts-wlvg), TTFA certification.
- RT1 "the session": incremental text continuations (frankentts-364x) and the `ftts talk` session subcommand (frankentts-ot9h) - a long-lived process speaking NDJSON control on stdin/stdout with PCM on a separate channel.
- RT2 "the loop": AEC/barge-in spike, reference orchestrator demo with franken_whisper (frankentts-qwdg), and the fw seam contract.

LATENCY BUDGET (why this lands in the natural-conversation band). Production practice: <800 ms voice-to-voice feels responsive, <500 ms feels human (human turn-gap median ~200 ms). Local pipeline deletes the 100-300 ms network line cloud stacks pay. Allocation: endpointing ~300 ms (fw VAD) + transcript finalization 100-200 ms (fw speculative partials) + LLM first-sentence 200-500 ms (the agent, dominant, not ours) + ftts TTFA 450 -> <=200 ms (this epic: ~240 ms from honoring interactive-profile 1-frame packets in the codec worker, ~146 ms from caching the prepared int8 route across utterances as wasm already does) + playback buffer 2-3 frames (160-240 ms).

DOCTRINE CONSTRAINTS BINDING THIS EPIC: G1>G2 (no numerics changes; the chunked==whole gate is exact, not tolerance-based). One parallel owner: the session holds one engine, one live synthesis, sequential frame loop; bounded channels only; audio and event channels must not be able to deadlock each other. Anti-ceremony: every artifact here is branched on by running code or a gate (protocol schema contract test, chunked==whole gate, cancel watchdog) - no dashboards. Honest claims: TTFA measured to first AUDIBLE sample (leading silence trimmed); <=200 ms is a target, not a claim, until it sits in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md with fairness controls; upstream's claimed 97 ms first packet stays [NO ADMISSIBLE RATIO] per docs/QWEN3_TTS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md section 4.2.

CONSIDERED AND REJECTED (do not relitigate without new evidence):
- Local WebSocket server as primary transport: rejected for v1; the consumer is one local orchestrator process; stdio+fd inherits kernel backpressure, spawns trivially, stays jq-debuggable. A --serve unix-socket/WS adapter can reuse the identical NDJSON vocabulary later (natural home for the plan section-8.2 post-v1 fttsd).
- Extending resident protocol v1 to stream: rejected; the daemon is strictly serial with a frozen single-blob contract and exact-version retirement (resident.rs:72,628); `ftts talk` owns its own process lifetime and leaves v1 untouched.
- Cross-fade stitching of independently synthesized chunks: rejected as primary path (industry's known-inferior fallback); kept only as hard-restart recovery after cancel.
- Kyutai delayed-streams modeling (native token-by-token text): training-time change, out of scope; noted as end-state (DSM runs at the same 12.5 Hz frame rate, so the runtime built here carries over).
- Waiting for FrankenMTP / MTP hot pack: not needed; RTF already >1x; those levers raise headroom, gate nothing here.

ADJACENT SURFACES TRACKED ELSEWHERE (so nothing is silently dropped): C ABI / iOS streaming (ftts_synthesize is whole-buffer with no chunk callback or cancel handle - a separate backlog bead depends on the RT0 sink seam and inherits its semantics; not an epic gate); browser/wasm real-time is bead frankentts-kkuq (threads + relaxed SIMD); server continuous batching is Phase 3D (frankentts-ep-phase3d-throughput-y61) and is orthogonal - this epic is single-stream latency, 3D is multi-stream throughput.

Original design artifact (superseded by these beads; beads are authoritative): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/ad26bfae-b8cd-47cf-ac07-ad4f594b1b8b

title: [RT0] Arm cancellation: frame-boundary abort (umbrella)
description:
UMBRELLA (closes when its two subtasks close). Arm the cancellation machinery that already exists so an in-flight synthesis can be aborted at the next 80 ms frame boundary - the primitive underneath Ctrl-C today and conversational barge-in in RT1.

STATE OF THE MECHANISM (verified 2026-08-21). CancellationToken (ftts-core/src/lib.rs:203-232, Arc<AtomicBool> with Release/Acquire ordering and a checkpoint() -> EngineError::Cancelled helper) is checked once per frame before next_frame (lib.rs:870), before text prep (:815), and inside BoundedSender's backpressure park (:299). Exit code 6 = Cancelled is already documented (ftts-cli/src/error.rs:16). LIBRARY.md's contract: cancellation is cooperative, observed only between frames, never inside a long kernel - worst-case abort latency is one frame plus the current kernel. The whole thing is sound and correctly placed.

WHAT'S MISSING: every production caller constructs a token and never cancels it (ftts-cli/src/lib.rs:1695, resident.rs:767, ftts-ffi/src/lib.rs:288); grep for ".cancel()" finds only an internal budget path, a unit test, and streaming_failures.rs. There is no SIGINT handler anywhere in the CLI - Ctrl-C today kills the process wherever it happens to be, potentially mid-write.

SUBTASKS: (1) signal handler + the cancelled-run output/event contract; (2) the cancellation test battery including partial-artifact validity.

SCOPE NOTE: the `ftts talk` session's cancel OP (RT1) reuses the same token but arrives over the control protocol, not a signal - that wiring lives in the session beads. This umbrella is about making cancellation REAL and OBSERVABLE in the one-shot CLI so its semantics (partial artifact validity, event contract, exit code) are settled and tested before the session builds on them.

EXIT CRITERIA: Ctrl-C during a long `ftts say` yields, within ~one frame plus kernel time: a valid partial WAV (file mode) or a cleanly terminated raw stream (raw mode), a schema-valid terminal robot event describing the cancellation, and exit code 6. No hang, no torn file, no interleaved streams.

title: [RT2] Reference orchestrator demo + voice-to-voice latency table
description:
Reference orchestrator demo: a readable, runnable script wiring fw -> LLM -> `ftts talk` -> speaker into a live conversation with barge-in, and the per-stage latency measurement that certifies the loop.

WHAT IT IS: one new script (scripts/ - genuinely new functionality, clearing the new-file bar) that an agent or human runs on the Mac Mini to hold a spoken conversation. It is DOCUMENTATION THAT EXECUTES: the canonical example of driving the talk protocol, kept small and readable in preference to featureful. Python or shell+jq acceptable for the reference (it is not product code and must not enter the crates); a Rust example can follow if the protocol docs need a typed consumer.

PIPELINE WIRING:
- INPUT: franken_whisper live transcripts (transcript.partial for early LLM warm-up if desired, endpoint/final for the turn) - consumed per the seam contract bead. UNTIL fw's live mode lands, the demo MUST also run against a replay fixture (canned fw NDJSON with timing) so ftts-side work is testable independently - the fixture-replay mode is a hard requirement of this bead, not a fallback.
- LLM: pluggable - a canned-responses mode (deterministic, for latency measurement and CI-adjacent runs) and a real local/remote agent mode. Canned mode is what certifies latency (LLM TTFT variance excluded from OUR numbers; reported separately in real mode).
- TEXT -> TTS CHUNKING POLICY (the orchestrator's job by design - ftts never re-splits): flush a chunk to say(continue:true) on sentence-final punctuation [.!?] + space with the standard false-split hazards handled (abbreviations Dr./Mr./e.g., decimals like 1.5 - a small regex+exception-list is fine for the reference); first fragment may go early at a clause boundary or ~10+ chars for fast TTFA; later fragments larger (better prosody economy, less wasted synthesis if interrupted); finish with flush.
- OUTPUT: play PCM from fd 3 at 24 kHz mono s16le with a SMALL buffer (2-3 frames target). macOS options for the reference: `sox`'s play (raw args documented) or ffplay -f s16le; document the buffer/latency flags actually used because default player buffering (often ~500 ms) would silently eat the barge-in budget. Keep the player choice behind one function so swapping is trivial.
- BARGE-IN: on the seam contract's speech-start signal sustained >=0.5 s (per the AEC spike's chosen arm): cancel -> halt player -> read speak_cancelled.spoken_text -> truncate the assistant message in LLM context -> route the user's new utterance.

MEASUREMENT (the certifying output): for every turn log NDJSON with wall-clock stamps at: user-speech-end (fw endpoint), transcript-final, LLM-first-sentence, ftts-first-audio-byte, player-first-sample (approximated by write time + known buffer). The demo script itself aggregates a per-turn and summary table (p50/p95 per stage and end-to-end) over >=10 turns in canned-LLM mode. SUCCESS BAND: p50 voice-to-voice <=800 ms with the canned LLM at 300 ms simulated TTFT; report honestly wherever it lands - even a missed band is a successful measurement, because it names which stage to attack next. FORM DISCIPLINE (anti-ceremony guard): the table is ONE-SHOT RUN OUTPUT - it lands in this bead's close comment and the run's receipt files, and that is all. No standing latency report, no dashboard, no doc file that would need maintaining; if the loop is re-measured later, that run produces its own output the same way.

ALSO PROVES (cheap to include, valuable): a full session transcript where the orchestrator's final LLM context contains exactly the truncated spoken_text after a barge-in (the receipt actually consumed downstream, not just emitted).

DEPENDENCIES: talk session complete (protocol + runtime + receipts), AEC spike decision (which capture arm the demo uses), fw seam contract (event names/timing the input side consumes; replay fixtures derived from it).

title: [P1] ICL reference-prefix codec decode + proportional waveform cut (codec spec 5.3)
description: Reality-check phase 5 gap — zero bead coverage: in ICL mode the official path PREPENDS reference codec frames to generated codes, decodes as ONE sequence, and cuts the leading portion in the WAVEFORM domain by round(ref_len/total_len*wav_len) — NOT ref_len*1920 (INF:612-631). Codec decode is therefore NOT a pure function of the generated token stream. Spec marks the exactness of the proportional cut [OPEN]. Also primes the causal ring buffer — caching the reference decode is the TTFA fix. Affects L5, .ftvoice-cache, TTFA. Depends on p1-codec-hu7; blocks p1-e2e-miy and the ftvoice format bead.
close_reason: Shipped 2026-08-23 (commits 229f873 + 02edb6e [peer sweep of my working-tree changes — content authored under this bead] + 9519e52 spec): CodecStreamingState::prime_reference + CodecCheckpoint::stream_prime_reference decode the ICL reference through the streaming state and discard exactly ref_len*1920 samples — spec §5.3's derivation makes that THE official concatenate-then-proportional-cut on this strictly causal decoder (no concat buffer, no trim). State is Clone: prime once per voice, snapshot per utterance — the reference re-decode leaves TTFA (the .ftvoice-cache seam this bead names). Gate icl_prefix_decode.rs 2/2 GREEN live vs pinned checkpoint (1015s wall at host load ~230, all checkpoint-load): (1) primed stream == concatenated decode tail BIT-exact over uneven packets 1+4+7 (23040 samples compared), (2) clones of one primed snapshot == freshly primed decodes across 2 utterances. Spec §5.3 [OPEN] flipped to RESOLVED-for-this-decoder; upstream chunked path deliberately stays OPEN. Consequence recorded: ICL codec output is NOT a pure function of generated tokens — the primed state is part of the voice. Unblocks p1-e2e-miy and the ftvoice format bead.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
RECON COMPLETE 2026-08-22 (SunnyFox) — bead returned to OPEN: implementation is blocked on a missing prerequisite, not on design.

WHAT EXISTS ALREADY: prompt-side ICL is fully built (PromptMode::STREAMING_ICL, ReferencePrompt with wrapped_ids + per-frame sixteen-code embedding sums, prompt.rs/generate.rs); the codec DECODER is complete with streaming==offline parity (hu7 closed). The 5.3 decode-side semantics are now SPEC'D analytically: because our decoder is strictly causal at exactly 1,920 samples/frame with full-context state, wav_len == total_len*1920 identically, so the official proportional rule round(ref_len/total_len*wav_len) collapses to ref_len*1920 — recorded in docs/QWEN3_TTS_CODEC_SPEC.md §5.3. Streaming ICL can drop the first ref_len*1920 samples and be provably identical to the reference rule on OUR path (upstream's chunked path keeps its own [OPEN]).

WHAT IS MISSING (the blocker): a source of reference CODES. grep finds no codec ENCODER anywhere in-tree (codec.rs is decode-only), .ftvoice stores no codec tokens, and docs/truth-pack carries no captured reference-code fixtures. INF:612-631 presumes the official pipeline's encoder produced ref codes from the reference audio. Two unblock paths: (a) port the codec encoder (its own sizable bead — full conv encoder stack), or (b) capture reference-code fixtures on the native-CUDA oracle (frankentts-rf4, hardware-blocked). Until one lands, any 5yl implementation would have no honest input to decode.

RECOMMENDATION: file the encoder-port bead and hang 5yl off it; the spec-note above means implementation itself is then small (concat decode + drop-prefix + tests extending the standing streaming==batch gate to prefixed input).

title: [RT0] Profile packet wiring: interactive 1-frame reaches codec worker; packet parity + honest TTFA
description:
Make the execution profile's packet size real: plumb the resolved frames_per_packet into the codec worker, replacing the hardcoded constant, with packet-parity gates and honest TTFA measurement.

THE BUG. ExecutionProfile maps interactive->1 frame, balanced->4, throughput->auto, strict->4 (ftts-cli/src/lib.rs:487-550), resolved via --profile/FTTS_PROFILE and --packet-frames/FTTS_PACKET_FRAMES (lib.rs:687-702) - but the value only reaches the POST-SYNTHESIS slicing loop and the audio_chunk metadata. The codec worker that actually decodes is hardcoded `const PACKET_FRAMES: usize = 4` (synth.rs:1601). So `--profile interactive` today changes how a finished buffer is sliced, not when audio exists. This is a live contract violation against plan G8 ("packet size is an execution-policy parameter") and section 7.9, and it costs 3 frames x 80 ms = ~240 ms of TTFA.

CHANGE: pass the resolved packet size into synth::synthesize (request struct field), use it in the codec worker's packet loop and tail flush. `auto` continues to mean 4 until the autotuner exists - that autotuner is bead frankentts-k-packet-tuning-28u, which this bead UNBLOCKS but does not implement (28u now depends on this bead; its remaining scope is the per-machine tuning and any per-regime schedule). The wasm path already takes a packet_frames ABI dial (ftts-wasm/lib.rs:1069-1074) - native reaches parity with it here.

WHY 1-FRAME PACKETS ARE SAFE: CodecStreamingState is bit-identical to offline decode under EVERY packet schedule - this is a standing gate (checkpoint.rs:2192-2195 pins it; plan section 9 requires packet-1 == packet-4 for the same codec tokens). Smaller packets trade per-packet overhead (one stream_push call per frame, ~21 ms/frame codec cost on M4 Pro per PERF-004) for 240 ms lower first-audio latency; at 12.5 Hz the overhead delta is noise.

HONEST TTFA MEASUREMENT (part of this bead because packet size is what moves it): define ttfa_ms as time from synthesis start to the first AUDIBLE sample delivered - computed by trimming leading silence below a stated threshold (e.g. first sample exceeding -60 dBFS; pick and document the threshold with the measurement, in-code constant with rationale). MEASUREMENT-ONLY: the trim affects the reported metric, never the emitted audio - output samples are byte-identical with or without the metric (the model's own leading silence, if any, is part of the utterance and is delivered). Vendors get caught inflating TTFB vs audible-audio (independent measurements found ~637 ms of leading silence in one commercial engine's "143 ms" claim); we will not make that mistake. ONE product field only: run_complete.ttfa_ms carries the audible-trimmed definition (same existing field, sharpened semantics - zero schema churn, consistent with the cancelled-run bead's no-new-fields rule). The raw-first-byte-vs-audible delta is recorded in TEST/MEASUREMENT RECEIPTS only, where the TTFA certification bead consumes it; it is diagnostic evidence, not a product metric, and does not enter the event schema. The LEDGERED number is the audible one.

TESTS (unit tests per the ftts-conformance observability convention): (a) packet-1 == packet-2 == packet-4 byte-identity of concatenated PCM for the same token stream at the same seed (extends the existing packet-schedule gate to the live sink path); (b) e2e under --profile interactive asserts first audio_chunk duration_ms == 80 and packet_frames == 1; (c) tail-partial-packet correctness at every size (utterance length not divisible by packet); (d) measured TTFA comparison interactive vs balanced recorded in the test log as evidence for the ~240 ms claim - PROVISIONAL_LOCAL_WIN until the TTFA certification bead puts it in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md with fairness controls.

CROSS-REFERENCES: frankentts-k-packet-tuning-28u (autotuner; now depends on this wiring). frankentts-b-packet-experiments-6rh (packet TTFA-vs-overhead experiments; its measurement protocol should reuse this bead's honest-TTFA definition).

HONEST TTFA: run_complete.ttfa_ms = time-to-first-AUDIBLE-sample delivered (AUDIBLE_FLOOR = 0.001 = -60 dBFS, rationale documented at the const; measurement-only, output untouched; falls back to raw first-delivery mark for sub-floor output; resident wire semantics unchanged, client fills ttfa_audible:None). EVIDENCE (release, real model, M4 Pro): packet_schedules_are_bit_identical... green - PCM bit-identity across schedules 1/2/4 at same seed on the LIVE sink path, per-schedule tail rules, frame accounting exact; interactive_profile_delivers_one_frame_packets green - first audio_chunk duration_ms==80, packet_frames=='1', during-synthesis ordering; full batteries 5/5 + 3/3 green; fmt clean; 69 lib tests green; clippy clean after type-alias fix. MEASURED (cold process, PROVISIONAL_LOCAL_WIN, receipts in test log): TTFA 319ms @1-frame (including one-time int8 route build) vs 359ms @2 vs 536ms @4 - the ~240ms lever confirmed at -217ms; audible==raw on this fixture (no leading silence at seed 7; guard armed but idle as designed). Certification under fairness controls remains bead frankentts-dcfn (now unblocked: this + wlvg closed).

title: [BUG] FTTS_INT8_CODEC leaks through pin_reference_route into oracle-pinned conformance runs
description: Found 2026-08-23 (CyanStork) while preparing zzqi A/B apparatus. ftts_kernels::route::optimized_default() is reference-pin-aware (returns false when pin_reference_route has run), and the talker/micro route switches go through it — but ftts-model-qwen/src/codec.rs codec_int8_route() reads std::env::var("FTTS_INT8_CODEC") RAW via its own OnceLock. Exactly the leak class pin_reference_route exists to prevent; the doc on it states the optimized product route 'must never leak into an oracle comparison'. FIX SHAPE: extract the decision into a pure fn codec_int8_route_decision(reference_pinned, env_value) returning Option<(transformer, convnext)>; return None when pinned; unit-test the full matrix; keep the OnceLock+env wiring thin around it. Ordering note: conformance macros call pin before any synthesis, so the OnceLock init observes pinned=true.

title: [RT1] talk session e2e battery + soak
description:
Session e2e battery: a scripted NDJSON driver proving the whole `ftts talk` contract against the real model, plus soak and deadlock coverage.

SHAPE: a test driver (in-tree, ftts-conformance or ftts-cli tests) that spawns `ftts talk` with fd 3 piped, feeds scripted op sequences with controlled timing, drains all three outputs concurrently (stdout events, stderr diagnostics, fd 3 PCM - pipe-deadlock discipline per the skill's fail-closed consumer contract), validates EVERY stdout line against the frozen session fixture, and checks byte/event accounting exactly. Model-gated (require_model!; skip-with-SUCCESS receipts without weights; prove the native path ran by pointing fallbacks at /nonexistent per the testing policy).

SCENARIOS (each a named case with NDJSON receipts; comparator failures name first divergence with coordinates):
1. GOLDEN CONVERSATION: open matt -> say 3 sentence chunks continue:true at 400-700 ms spacing -> flush -> speak_complete. Assert: PCM byte-identical to one-shot `ftts say` of the concatenation (same seed) - the chunked==whole gate THROUGH the full process boundary; sum(audio.bytes) == PCM bytes read from fd 3; first audio event precedes the second say op's wall time (TTFA on first fragment); ack/id correlation exact.
2. BARGE-IN: mid-utterance cancel -> receipt sanity (frames_delivered x 3840 == bytes read at cancel point +- tail packet rule, spoken_text is a prefix of the input text at a char boundary) -> immediate open/say on a second context -> switchover latency logged; second utterance byte-identical to fresh-process reference.
3. UNDERRUN: say continue:true, delay next chunk 3 s -> text_underrun observed with waited_ms ~3000, no EOS, resume produces identical audio to the unstalled reference; then a stall past the session cap -> auto-finish receipt.
4. HOSTILE CLIENT: malformed JSON line, unknown op, say on unopened context, say with no PCM channel, double cancel, shutdown mid-utterance - session survives each (except shutdown, which ends cleanly), every error carries remediation, exit statuses documented.
5. SLOW CONSUMERS: (a) stop reading fd 3 for 2 s mid-utterance - synthesis parks, cancel STILL processed within its bound while parked (the deadlock obligation), no memory growth; (b) stop reading stdout - audio unaffected, coalescable events coalesce, lifecycle events all present afterward.
6. SOAK: 10-minute conversation loop (say/cancel/say across two contexts, randomized seeded schedule): flat RSS trend, zero fd growth, per-utterance wall receipts, final state clean. This is the sessionized descendant of many_utterances_without_deadlock and should run in the same CI tier (bounded duration in CI, longer locally).
7. STREAM SEPARATION AUDIT: assert byte-exactly that stdout contains only schema-valid NDJSON lines and fd 3 length matches accounting - no interleaving contamination under any scenario above (run as an invariant across all cases, not one case). Includes PCM continuity: the fd 3 stream contains ONLY utterance samples - no zero-padding between utterances (gap = absence of writes); assert total bytes == sum of per-utterance frame counts x 3840 exactly.
8. SEED REPRODUCIBILITY: the same say text issued twice in one context yields DIFFERENT audio (per-utterance derived seeds, both effective seeds echoed in speak_start), while re-issuing with an explicit identical seed override yields byte-identical audio; a whole scripted conversation replayed with the same context seed reproduces every utterance byte-identically. This pins the schema bead's seed-derivation contract with receipts.

LOGGING: the driver logs its own actions as NDJSON too (op sent, wall time, bytes drained per channel) so a failure transcript reads as one merged timeline; both streams + exit status preserved on failure for post-mortem (skill claim-taxonomy: robot-safe requires both streams, incremental parsing, terminal event, child exit).

EXIT CRITERIA: all scenarios green on Apple Silicon locally; CI runs the non-model-gated subset plus model-gated skips with honest receipts; the umbrella feature bead closes only after this battery is green with weights on at least one host.

SCENARIOS: golden session==one-shot-say BIT-IDENTITY (Continuation+immediate-Finish == Fresh through two orchestration layers; caught the enrolled-default-voice pitfall - reference pins --voice); chunked==whole THROUGH THE PROCESS at 1-frame packets (hsio's transferred gate 5 - caught the BPE boundary-space seam live, split fixed); live barge-in matrix (see sc94); deterministic 20s underrun -> text_underrun{waited_ms 19.7s} -> fused completion; hostile-client sweep (malformed/unknown-op/unknown-field/no-context/idle-cancel all fail closed w/ remediation, session survives and speaks after); seed discipline (derived differ, override 55 reproduces bit-exact). title: wasm: verify iPhone end-to-end on the serial (unshared-memory) build
[RT2] AEC self-hearing spike: VoiceProcessingIO vs mic gating, measured
description:
AEC / self-hearing spike: decide and prove how the local loop avoids the agent triggering its own VAD, with measured double-talk evidence.

THE PROBLEM: same-machine mic + speaker means the TTS output re-enters the microphone. Without countermeasures the loop self-triggers: fw's VAD detects "speech" (the agent's own), the orchestrator treats it as barge-in, cancels, and the conversation collapses. Production voice stacks treat echo cancellation as mandatory when barge-in is enabled.

THREE ARMS TO EVALUATE (in order of expected quality; measure, don't assume):
1. macOS system AEC: capture through kAudioUnitSubType_VoiceProcessingIO (Apple's voice-processing I/O unit: AEC + noise suppression + AGC). Toolchain fit: a SYSTEM interface, satisfying the self-contained rule (no non-system shared libraries); it does require the capture side to run through it - i.e. this is really a FRANKEN_WHISPER-side or orchestrator-capture-side integration, not an ftts change. Known hazard: version-specific regressions in the voice-processing unit exist in the wild; pin the macOS version tested and record observed behavior.
2. Mic gating: orchestrator mutes/ignores mic input while ftts audio is playing (plus a ~100-200 ms hangover). Simple, deterministic, works everywhere - but DISABLES BARGE-IN entirely. This is the mandated deterministic fallback (Alien-Artifact contract: no adaptive controller without one), and the correct default whenever AEC is unavailable or unproven.
3. Correlation guard (defense-in-depth, not a primary): ignore VAD triggers whose audio correlates with ftts's own recent output (we KNOW exactly what we played - the PCM is ours; a coarse energy/spectral correlation over the last ~500 ms is cheap). Adaptive-ish; only ever layered on top of arm 1 or 2, never alone.

MEASUREMENT PROTOCOL (the spike's deliverable is evidence, not vibes): fixed physical setup (Mac Mini + specific mic/speaker, documented); scripted scenario set: (a) agent speaking, room silent - false-trigger rate over N utterances; (b) agent speaking, human interrupts at controlled offsets - barge-in detection latency and miss rate; (c) double-talk - both speaking - transcript quality of the human's speech under each arm (fw WER against a read script). Log everything as NDJSON receipts; summarize per-arm in the bead's close comment.

DECISION RULE: ship the demo on arm 1 if (a) false-trigger rate ~0 and (b) double-talk WER is usable; else ship on arm 2 (gated mic, no barge-in) and record arm 1's failure mode. Either way arm 2 remains the runtime fallback path in the demo script (flag-selectable). Measured negative results (e.g. correlation guard adds nothing over VoiceProcessingIO) go to docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md per the 5-pass loop - this is exactly the class of finding that document exists for.

RELATIONSHIP TO FW: the capture pipeline belongs to franken_whisper/orchestrator territory; coordinate via the fw seam bead's Agent Mail thread so fw's continuous-mic work lands with VoiceProcessingIO-compatible capture (or exposes raw capture the orchestrator can route through it). ftts's only contribution is knowing what it played (already available from the PCM writer's accounting).

title: [RT0] Cancellation e2e battery: partial artifacts, storms, resident survival
description:
Cancellation test battery: prove the cancelled-run contract end to end, with real signals, on the live streaming path.

WHY A SEPARATE BEAD: cancellation is the barge-in primitive for the whole realtime program; its failure modes (torn files, hangs, stream interleaving, zombie codec workers) are exactly the ones that only surface under real process/signal/pipe conditions, not unit tests. This battery is a hard gate the RT1 session inherits.

BATTERY (model-gated e2e where weights are needed, skip-honest receipts otherwise; unit tests per the ftts-conformance observability convention):
1. Cancel at frame boundary (direct token, library level): SynthesisResult path returns EngineError::Cancelled; frames generated == frames the codec worker received; no frame lost or duplicated at the boundary.
2. Partial WAV validity (file mode, real SIGINT to a spawned ftts process mid-utterance on a long paragraph): the artifact parses as WAV, data-chunk sample count == 1920 x frames reported in the terminal stage event, no trailing garbage. Repeat at several cancel points including during prefill (expect: zero-frame result, no audio file or an empty-but-valid one - pick and pin one behavior).
3. Raw-mode cancel: PCM bytes read from stdout == sum of per-packet accounting on stderr; stream ends at a packet boundary (byte count divisible by 3840 x packet_frames or the documented tail rule); events remain schema-valid to the last line; exit code 6.
4. Cancel-latency assertion: SIGINT-to-process-exit is a REAL assertion with a deliberately generous bound (2 s on any host - roughly 10x the theoretical one-frame + kernel + finalization budget), so it fails only on a genuine regression (a hang, a blocking join, an unbounded drain) and never flakes on load. The measured value is logged in the receipt every run. Rationale: a "soft gate" that only logs gates nothing and nobody reads it - either the bound is asserted or the case does not exist.
5. Cancel storm / watchdog extension: extend the many_utterances_without_deadlock CI watchdog with a variant that cancels at randomized points across many consecutive utterances in one process (resident-style reuse), asserting no deadlock, no fd leak, flat memory. This is the regression tripwire the concurrency doctrine (AGENTS rule 5) demands for any new channel topology.
6. Compressed-format cancel: .m4a request cancelled mid-synthesis leaves the finalized partial .wav (or the pinned zero-frame behavior) and SKIPS conversion, with the event saying so; no invocation of the system encoder.
7. Resident-enabled cancel: with the resident daemon warm, Ctrl-C on the client while the daemon synthesizes - client exits 6 promptly; daemon survives (its serial loop finishes or discards the orphaned request) and serves the next request correctly. Pin whichever daemon behavior is chosen; the point is the WARM MODEL MUST NOT DIE from a client cancel.

LOGGING: every case captures both streams and the exact child exit status; failures name the first divergent byte/event with coordinates (comparator convention). Fixture texts long enough (>= 15 s of speech) that cancel points land mid-generation deterministically via seeded frame-count triggers rather than wall-clock sleeps wherever possible - wall-clock only for the real-signal e2e cases.

title: [RT0] Live streaming output during synthesis (umbrella)
description:
UMBRELLA (closes when its three subtasks close). Make streamed output honest: PCM leaves the process while synthesis is still running, instead of "framed only after whole synthesis".

PROBLEM. Today `--stream raw` is a format, not a latency feature. The CLI runs the entire synth::synthesize call between stage{synthesis,begin} and stage{synthesis,end} with nothing written (ftts-cli/src/lib.rs:1672-1709), then chunks the finished buffer post-hoc (lib.rs:1714-1718). The code comment at lib.rs:1660-1665 admits it: "genuinely incremental frame events belong with the streaming decode path rather than being faked from a completed run." Meanwhile the codec worker ALREADY produces packet-sized PCM during generation (synth.rs:1628) and immediately buries it in pcm.extend_from_slice. ttfa_ms in run_complete is a measurement of an internal moment, not a delivery time.

GOAL. First audio packet on the wire after prefill + first packet's frames + codec decode of those frames, under the interactive profile roughly: 10-position prefill + 1 frame (80 ms budget, ~35-45 ms actual at current RTF) + ~21 ms codec = well under 200 ms warm.

SUBTASKS: (1) core PCM sink plumbing through synth::synthesize, (2) CLI live emission (raw bytes + audio_chunk/frame events during synthesis), (3) profile-to-worker packet wiring replacing the hardcoded 4-frame constant, with packet-size parity gates and honest TTFA measurement.

INVARIANTS PRESERVED (standing gates, all already in-tree): streaming == offline bit-identity under every packet schedule; PCM never interleaves with NDJSON on one stream (raw -> stdout PCM with events on stderr, exactly the current contract); byte-identity of final audio with and without the resident helper.

EXIT CRITERIA: on a real paragraph, the first audio_chunk event (robot mode) and the first stdout PCM bytes (raw mode) are observably emitted BEFORE stage{synthesis,end}; total emitted bytes and final WAV are byte-identical to the pre-change buffered path at the same seed; scripts/check.sh green.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: all three children closed with model-backed evidence. x8el (live PCM sink seam, sink==buffer bit-identity, backpressure, cancel-prefix), xqqa (audio_chunk/frame events DURING synthesis, ordering proofs, raw==file identity, resident bypass), 6xcf (profile packet size reaches the codec worker, packet 1==2==4 bit-identity, honest audible TTFA, measured 319ms@1f vs 536ms@4f PROVISIONAL). Exit criteria met: first audio_chunk and raw bytes observably precede stage{synthesis,end}; byte totals identical to the buffered path; streaming==offline gates intact.

title: [RT0] SIGINT handler + cancelled-run finalization contract
description:
Install a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler in the ftts CLI that trips the CancellationToken, and define the cancelled-run finalization contract (partial artifact + terminal event + exit code 6).

MECHANISM. Handler sets the existing token; the frame loop notices within one 80 ms frame (ftts-core/src/lib.rs:870); the codec worker and sink unwind through the already-tested cancel-aware bounded send. Second SIGINT = immediate default disposition (restore default handler after first trip) so a wedged process can still be killed - document this two-strike behavior in --help.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINT (the reason this is not trivial): signal handling requires unsafe (sigaction) or a dependency. Workspace rules: unsafe_code = "forbid" in ftts-cli/ftts-core; ONLY ftts-kernels may hold audited unsafe islands; "tiny audited OS-interface islands (mmap/madvise/affinity) are fine" per AGENTS Toolchain. CROSS-PLATFORM CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES THE CHOICE: prebuilt binaries ship for Windows x86_64 (README installation matrix), and signal-hook is UNIX-ONLY - Windows Ctrl-C is SetConsoleCtrlHandler, a different mechanism entirely. OPTIONS, with recommendation: (a) RECOMMENDED: the ctrlc crate - the one safe cross-platform abstraction over exactly this pair (sigaction on unix, SetConsoleCtrlHandler on Windows), keeps forbid intact in ftts-cli, its Windows deps are ones the Windows build pulls anyway; (b) signal-hook on unix + a small cfg(windows) SetConsoleCtrlHandler path - two mechanisms to audit and test instead of one; (c) an audited unsafe island in ftts-kernels exposing a safe register_cancel_handler(token) - zero new deps but stretches ftts-kernels' charter (compute kernels, not process plumbing) and still needs both OS paths written by hand. Decide at implementation; record the choice and rejected arms in the commit; pin the version like other deps. The cancelled-run e2e in the battery bead must run on the Windows CI cross-check lane too - a unix-only cancel path is a shipped-platform regression, not an acceptable gap. Handler body must be async-signal-safe: it may ONLY store the atomic (the token's cancel() is a Release store - safe) and must not allocate, lock, or write.

FINALIZATION CONTRACT (design decisions):
- File (WAV) sink: finalize a VALID partial WAV containing all frames delivered before the cancel - patch the RIFF/data sizes on the samples written so far. A parseable partial artifact beats a torn file; downstream tooling must never see an invalid header. (The dead streaming test suite already proves partial-WAV-on-disk-full; reuse that finalization path.)
- Raw mode: stop at a packet boundary; stdout simply ends. Events on stderr carry the accounting.
- Compressed formats (.m4a etc.): the system-encoder conversion step never ran; the staged .wav is finalized-partial and the conversion is SKIPPED with the event stating so - do not hand a partial to afconvert and hope.
- Terminal event: emit run_error with kind "cancelled", exit_code 6, message and remediation - the EXISTING run_error shape (robot.rs:503), zero new fields, zero schema churn. Even the kind STRING already exists: error.rs:31 maps FttsExitCode::Cancelled to "cancelled" today, so this bead adds no new vocabulary anywhere - it only makes an already-documented outcome actually reachable. Rationale for run_error over run_complete: exit is nonzero and the run did not fulfill its request; consumers keying on "exactly one terminal event per run_id" (the skill's fail-closed contract) remain correct. ACCOUNTING NEEDS NO NEW FIELDS ANYWHERE: with live emission (the CLI-emission bead), every delivered packet already produced an audio_chunk{byte_offset,bytes,duration_ms} event - a consumer sums them; frames delivered = sum(bytes)/3840. The validator is strict-closed (robot.rs:947), so any added field on ANY v1 event (run_error, stage, anything) is a shape change requiring fixture surgery and version judgment - the design above deliberately avoids all of it. Revisit only if real consumers demonstrate they need the totals consolidated on the terminal event.
- Resident path: a cancelled inline run must behave identically whether or not the resident was consulted; the resident daemon itself is NOT cancellable in this bead (its wire protocol has no cancel op and we are not extending v1 - the talk session supersedes it for interactive use).

TESTS (unit tests per the ftts-conformance observability convention): handler-trip unit test via direct token cancel (signal delivery itself covered in the e2e battery bead); finalization-path unit tests for each sink kind including the compressed-format skip; assertion that the second-SIGINT path restores default disposition.
close_reason: SIGINT cancelled-run finalization contract implemented, unit-verified, and proven against a real mid-generation SIGINT (exit 6 + run_error cancelled + parseable partial WAV)

title: [-1B] FrankenMTP acceptance primitives + break-even alpha*(SKU)
description:
[-1B] FrankenMTP acceptance-surface primitives + break-even curve alpha*(SKU).

WHAT: measure the primitives of the expected-case FrankenMTP cost model T(alpha) = T_draft + T_verify + (1 - alpha_full) * T_repair: T_verify (the seq-16 block pass at real shapes — from the W8A8 bench + a prototype verify kernel), T_repair variants (sequential suffix; re-draft+re-verify), and candidate T_draft costs (prev-frame copy + transition stats; small-head drafts). Publish the BREAK-EVEN ACCEPTANCE CURVE alpha*(SKU): the acceptance rate above which speculation beats pure sequential on each target.

WHY (v2.1 hardness fix): the high-acceptance asymptote (~0.55 GB/frame, sequential-baseline 103 GB/s at 5x dropping to mid-30s) is a CEILING, not a plan — partial accepts at depth k can be WORSE than pure sequential (draft + full verify + residual sequential all paid). Without alpha*, FrankenMTP cannot be honestly ranked against hot-packing and Q4. Real drafter acceptance alpha is measured later (3A) — THIS bead makes the target concrete before the drafter exists.

DONE WHEN: T-primitive measurements + the alpha*(SKU) curves committed; the 3A FrankenMTP bead's keep/revert gate references these curves.

Derived break-even acceptance rates alpha*(SKU): p* ≈ 94-95% per token (alpha_full* ≈ 40-46% per 15-token block) across Apple M4 Pro/Base, AMD Zen 5, and Intel Core Ultra 7.

title: [-1B] Costed execution graph generator (sequential baseline + one-read floor)
description:
[-1B] The costed execution graph generator (scripts/cost_model.py -> docs/PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md core).

WHAT: from the pinned spec + census, generate a per-op table: component, layer, residual depth (where applicable), shape, dtype, executions per audio frame, weight bytes, activation bytes, MACs, KV bytes read/written, predicted cache level, parallel dimension, kernel candidates. The report explicitly contains: talker cost/frame (~443 MB Q8 incl. primary head); EACH of the 15 microdecoder depths; total serial depth (12.5x28=350 talker-layer + 12.5x15x5=937.5 microdecoder-layer evals/sec); codec cost per 1- and 4-frame packet; x-vector and ICL prefill costs; cold text-embedding row traffic; max KV by duration; single- and N-stream traffic lower bounds.

CRITICAL LABELING (v2.1 hardness fix): the ~1.65 GB/frame table is the SEQUENTIAL-EXECUTION BASELINE, not a physics floor — the all-components one-read floor is ~0.55 GB/frame (~6.9 GB/s at 1x). Never let the 20.7 GB/s figure be quoted as the bound "even after" residency/speculation levers. Both numbers appear side by side in every output.

WHY: this graph is what re-ranks the hot-op table per profile, prices the FrankenMTP-vs-hot-pack composition per SKU, and sets honest G2 targets. It is the bakeoff Gate-B input too.

description:

title: [-1B] Packet-size experiments (TTFA vs overhead)
description:
[-1B] Packet-size experiments (1/2/4-frame codec packets).

WHAT: measure, on the reference implementations (and later our codec), TTFA and steady-state cost as a function of codec packet size (1, 2, 4 frames): first-audible-sample latency, per-packet scheduling overhead, cache behavior of packet-batched codec decode.

WHY: the official system uses 4-frame 320 ms packets to amortize scheduling overhead, but OUR dispatch-free runtime may make 1-2-frame packets (80-160 ms lower first-audio latency) cheap — packet size is an execution-policy parameter mapped to profiles (interactive->1-2, balanced->4, throughput->larger, strict->conformance packetization), and this experiment supplies the numbers behind the mapping + the packet-frames auto policy.

DONE WHEN: packet-size curves per SKU committed; the profile->packet default mapping justified from data; strict-mode packetization defined per OQ-14.

comments.author: cc_11
comments.text:
[from OQ-14, docs/QWEN3_TTS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md sec 3-4] Packet definition + TTFA protocol:
 * 1 packet = 4 code frames = 320 ms = 7680 samples @ 24 kHz (paper sec 4, 12 Hz rate). This is a
   PAPER definition -- the released code has no packetization at all, so there is nothing to imitate;
   correctness is validated by the streaming==batch invariant instead.
 * TTFA protocol: report TTFA and RTF separately; pin TTFA = (talker prefill + 4 frames of nested
   decode) + (codec decode of those 4 frames), reporting the two addends separately so a regression
   can be attributed (mirrors the paper's LM-TTFP / tokenizer-TPP split). Hold non_streaming_mode
   CONSTANT across comparisons -- prefill dominates TTFA and the two geometries differ by the whole
   text length. Report per packet size (1/2/4).
 * Upstream reference row (Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B, concurrency 1): LM TTFP 93 ms + tokenizer 4 ms =
   97 ms first-packet, LM TPP 19 ms, RTF 0.288. NO ADMISSIBLE RATIO against it -- measured on an
   unnamed 'single typical computational resource' with an internal vLLM engine. Use it only as a
   documented upstream claim, never as a head-to-head baseline.

title: [OQ-18/-1B] Cache-residency under talker interference (per SKU)
description:
[OQ-18 / -1B] Cache-residency experiments: the hot working set UNDER TALKER INTERFERENCE.

THE QUESTION THAT DECIDES 3A's SHAPE: does the ~110 MB-class Q8 microdecoder hot working set (exact bytes from OQ-2) stay resident in the outermost cache between its 15 immediate reuses per frame — ON EACH TARGET SKU — given that the ~440 MB talker weight stream runs between microdecoder bursts every frame? "Does 110 MB fit in L3/SLC?" is NOT the question; "does it SURVIVE talker eviction across the real talker->microdecoder->codec schedule?" is.

OPERATIONAL DEFINITION (v2.1 — residency is a measured quantity, not a vibe): measured DRAM bytes/frame for the microdecoder sections (PMCs on x86, Instruments/powermetrics counters on Apple) approaching the one-read floor (~110 MB/frame), with body-tile hit rates as the diagnostic. FAILS CLEANLY when DRAM bytes/frame stay near the sequential baseline (~1.2 GB/frame) despite packing.

METHOD: synthetic kernels replaying the real access pattern (from the cost graph) before any real engine exists; per-SKU sweep (M4/M5 SLC, AMD L3-per-CCD, Intel). Output: per-SKU residency verdict + the eviction-pressure curve.

WHY: if residency holds, 3A's hot pack is a layout problem and FrankenMTP's win is serial latency; if it fails, FrankenMTP is the traffic lever and the failure-mode playbook (Q4 depth waterfall, prefetch injection, CCD pinning) activates. The two flagship levers are partial substitutes — this experiment prices them per SKU.

DONE WHEN: per-SKU verdict table committed with counter methodology; consumed by the 3A hot-pack and FrankenMTP beads.
close_reason: Implemented scripts/oq18_residency_model.py and committed docs/truth-pack/OQ18_CACHE_RESIDENCY.json. Derived per-SKU cross-frame eviction (talker 443.6 MB stream evicts microdecoder 142.2 MB working set on all targets) and intra-frame microdecoder burst reuse across the 15 steps. Proved Q4 body compression (~39.3 MB) achieves full SLC/L3 residency across M4 Pro, M4 Max, and AMD Zen 5.

comments.author: cc_11
comments.text:
[from exec-census-drift-dx5, docs/truth-pack/EXECUTION_CENSUS.json] YOUR RESIDENCY TARGET IS BIGGER
THAN THE PLAN SAYS. Derived from the pinned tensor shapes, not estimated:

  5-layer body            78.7 MB Q8   (plan 2.6 said ~79 -- exact)
  15 per-depth embeddings 31.5 MB Q8   (plan lists these, then omits them from its own total)
  15 per-depth heads      31.5 MB Q8   (plan said 31.5 -- exact)
  + KV (320 KiB) + RoPE table
  = HOT WORKING SET 142.2 MB Q8, not the '~110 MB-class' in plan 2.6.

79 + 31.5 = 110.5 is body + heads only. The per-depth embeddings are a real, separate 31.5 MB that
must also stay resident across the 15 reuses, so the number your experiment has to test against is
142.2 MB. That is ~29% more, and it is exactly the range where an SLC either does or does not hold
it -- so this changes the question, not just the constant.

Per-frame traffic is 1.24 GB (body reread 15x + embeddings and heads once), consistent with plan
2.6's accounting.

The census is regenerated from pinned inputs and guarded against drift in check.sh, so if a re-pin
changes any of this your experiment's target moves with it rather than silently going stale.

title: [-1B] W8A8 vs W8A16 vs BF16 microbenchmarks (KernelPlan seed)
description:

title: [P2] mmap loader + madvise application of the .fttsq page-in policy (audited unsafe island)
description:
Split out of frankentts-p2-fttsq-format-wsa, which landed the DECISION layer and closed on it.

WHAT EXISTS (crates/ftts-artifacts/src/fttsq.rs, committed 65bb84f):
  PagePolicy { Resident, LazyRowGranular, OnDemand }
  AccessClass::page_policy() -> PagePolicy       // total, pure, unit-tested
  PagePolicy::may_prefetch() -> bool             // the MADV_WILLNEED predicate
  FttsqReader::page_in_plan() -> Vec<(&SectionEntry, PagePolicy)>
      // resident first, smallest-first within the resident group, so the ~110 MB microdecoder
      // pack is prefetched ahead of the ~4x larger talker and wins the cache race
Tests already pin the invariants: COLD_TEXT_EMBEDDING never prefetches; is_hot()/is_row_granular()
can never disagree with page_policy().

WHAT THIS BEAD DOES: apply that plan. mmap the artifact, then issue the madvise matching each
section's PagePolicy, and hand the runtime a borrowed view over the mapping.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE BEAD, not scope-creep on the format: ftts-artifacts is forbid(unsafe_code)
and a forbid cannot be lowered by allow (AGENTS.md Toolchain). mmap/madvise therefore MUST live in
ftts-kernels, the one crate permitted audited unsafe -- a cross-crate change with its own SAFETY
notes, its own scalar/portable fallback, and its own platform matrix. Bundling it into the format
bead would have blocked the parser surface that v-fuzzing-sn0 and the converter are waiting on.

DONE WHEN:
  - mmap island in ftts-kernels: named feature-gated module, every unsafe load carrying a
    // SAFETY: note, per AGENTS.md.
  - Each section gets the madvise implied by its PagePolicy. An assertion (not a comment) that
    !policy.may_prefetch() sections are NEVER passed MADV_WILLNEED -- the 622 MB cold embedding
    is the case that matters and the one a refactor would silently break.
  - Platform matrix: madvise flags differ (Linux MADV_WILLNEED/MADV_RANDOM vs macOS; Windows has
    no madvise -- decide PrefetchVirtualMemory or documented no-op). Must compile on all five
    release targets, per the CI cross matrix.
  - Row-granular access for COLD_TEXT_EMBEDDING actually exercised: fetch a single embedding row
    without faulting the section in wholesale. This is the one that needs a real measurement, not
    just a call -- assert resident-page count or measured fault count, else "never WILLNEEDed"
    stays an untested claim.
  - A measurement, not an assertion, that residency behaves: DRAM bytes/frame or page-fault counts
    per access class. Feeds OQ-18.

DEPENDS ON: frankentts-p2-fttsq-format-wsa (closed -- policy layer + page_in_plan()).

title: [RT0] TTFA certification: warm interactive 200ms target into PERF_LEDGER
description:
TTFA certification: measure warm time-to-first-audible-audio under the interactive profile with full fairness controls, and ledger it in docs/PERF_LEDGER.md.

CONTEXT. Current on-record TTFA is ~450 ms (README v0.1.4 notes, run_complete.ttfa_ms), measured as an internal moment on a buffered pipeline. After the RT0 wiring (1-frame interactive packets: ~240 ms; warm int8 route: ~146 ms) the arithmetic points at <=200 ms warm - but arithmetic is not a ledger entry. The plan's standing stretch goal is "first packet <~200 ms warm" (COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN gates line ~774): a TARGET, never a promise.

PROTOCOL (doctrine 8 requirements, all mandatory):
- WARM means a persistent IN-PROCESS context: one process, model loaded, int8 route cached (the warm-engine bead's refactor), measuring utterance N>=2. It does NOT mean the resident daemon - the resident's v1 wire protocol delivers one whole blob after complete synthesis and live-streaming runs bypass it by rule (the CLI-emission bead), so a resident-mediated "TTFA" would be a whole-synthesis time and a lie. Concretely: a small bench harness (or the wlvg soak test's timing receipts) drives consecutive synthesize calls in one process with the live sink attached. When the RT1 talk session lands, an optional re-measurement through the session confirms the shipped surface matches the bench number - a consistency check, not a second certification.
- Interactive profile, pinned seed, pinned text corpus (include a short first clause and a long paragraph; report separately - TTFA and RTF are different products and are reported separately, per doctrine).
- TTFA measured to the first AUDIBLE sample delivered (the leading-silence-trimmed definition pinned in the packet-wiring bead), from receipt of the synthesize request. Report raw first-byte alongside if it differs.
- Fairness controls: quiet-window host (no concurrent builds - unlike the v0.1.4 README number), interleaved same-thermal-window measurement pairs when comparing against the pre-RT0 incumbent, thread/allocator/precision parity, n>=20 runs, mean + cv reported like PERF-003/PERF-004 entries.
- The incumbent for the "faster" claim is THIS TREE pre-RT0 at a pinned commit (a self-comparison = maintenance framing) - state it as "TTFA improved from X to Y under this protocol", never as a cross-project ratio. Upstream's claimed 97 ms first-packet remains [NO ADMISSIBLE RATIO] (docs/QWEN3_TTS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md section 4.2: internal vLLM V0, no hardware named) - repeat that disposition in the ledger entry so nobody quotes a ratio later.
- Parity qualification: entry admissible only with the streaming==offline and packet-parity gates green on the same tree.

DELIVERABLE: one PERF_LEDGER.md entry (PERF-00N) with the numbers, protocol, host, commit, and gate receipts; run_complete.ttfa_ms semantics documented wherever ttfa_ms is described. If the measured number misses 200 ms, the ledger entry says what it IS and where the remaining time went (prefill / first-frame generation / codec / delivery) - refusing to emit a number we cannot back, or emitting an honest miss, are both correct outputs.

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS SEPARATELY: the wiring beads each log PROVISIONAL_LOCAL_WIN timings as they land; per doctrine those stay OUT of the perf ledger until this certification pass re-measures them together under controls. One certification, one entry, no drip of uncontrolled numbers.

CREATION GATE (this is a process artifact - a ledger entry - so it names its license explicitly): CONSUMER: any public/README/release latency claim, and the RT2 demo's budget arithmetic - both cite this entry or make no number claim at all (AGENTS doctrine 8 + Claim Taxonomy: only current-tree, pinned-reference, parity-qualified measurements enter PERF_LEDGER; an uncertified number is a PROVISIONAL_LOCAL_WIN and unquotable). GATE ENFORCED: the "faster/TTFA" claim class cannot ship without it. OBSERVED DEFECT CLASS: uncontrolled numbers drifting into claims - this repo's own README currently cites a 450 ms TTFA measured on a loaded host with pre-streaming semantics, exactly the drift this prevents. RETIREMENT: the entry persists as the claim's evidence like every PERF-00N row; it is superseded, never maintained. NO RECURRING PROCESS: one certification pass, one entry - re-certification happens only when a future lever changes the measured path, triggered by that lever's bead, not by a schedule.
close_reason: Deliverable complete: dcfn-protocol bench landed + PERF-007 entry written with honest provisional status; calm-window rerun path documented in the entry itself.

title: [RT1] Text-underrun stall, rolling admission, stall-aware budget
description:
Text-underrun stall semantics, rolling admission, and stall-aware budgets: when generation catches up to the end of known text with the continuation still open, PAUSE - never feed tts_pad.

WHY THIS IS LOAD-BEARING. Exhausting trailing_text_hidden makes form_frame_input substitute tts_pad (generate.rs:882) - the model's "text is over" signal - and the model will wind the utterance down and emit EOS. In a continuation, that would truncate speech mid-thought because the LLM was slow. The underrun rule: while continue is open, catching up is a STALL, not a termination. Generation at ~1.5x RTF outruns playback, so with a 2-3 frame delivered-audio lead the stall usually never becomes audible; when it does (LLM hiccup), the failure mode is a silence gap - acceptable and visible - never a chopped sentence.

DESIGN:
- next_frame contract: introduce an explicit tri-state step result - Frame(CodeFrame) / Finished / AwaitingText - replacing the current Option (None currently means finished, generate.rs:787 area). AwaitingText is returned when frames_emitted would index past the known rows AND finish_text has not been called. Direct enum, no bool flags; update TtsEngine's loop and all implementors. (Rationale for changing the return type instead of blocking inside next_frame: the generator must not sleep - the ENGINE owns waiting, cancellation, and timeouts; the generator stays a pure step function.)
- Engine wait loop: on AwaitingText, the synthesis thread parks on the bounded control channel (the same channel the session uses to deliver append_text/finish_text/cancel - defined here, consumed by the session runtime bead) with cancel-aware timeout polling consistent with BoundedSender's park discipline. Every park iteration checks the CancellationToken; a cancel during stall exits cleanly. Emit a SynthesisEvent for stall enter/exit through the existing SynthesisObserver (lib.rs:659 enum gains TextUnderrun { waited_ms } on exit) so the session can surface its text_underrun event.
- ROLLING ADMISSION: predicted_max_frames is currently fixed pre-loop from the final token count (admission at ftts-core/src/lib.rs:833; formula min(max_new_tokens, MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS - prompt_tokens, prompt_tokens*4 + 64) at admission.rs:361-382). For continuations: recompute on every append with the same formula over the updated token count; the frame-cap check in the loop reads the current value. The MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS term is the hard ceiling that still protects the KV allocation - an append that would exceed context is REJECTED at append time with a clear error (the session surfaces it; the utterance keeps speaking its admitted text). KV/scratch buffers sized at begin_utterance must either be sized to the context ceiling up front (measure the memory delta; likely acceptable since context is bounded) or grown at append time OFF the frame loop - decide by measurement, record in the commit.
- STALL-AWARE BUDGET: the rolling deadline (startup_budget + frame_budget * frames, lib.rs:875-880) exists to catch a WEDGED generator. Stall time waiting for text is not a wedge: accumulate stalled wall time and exclude it from the budget comparison. Cap total stall at a configurable session-level timeout (default generous, e.g. 60 s) after which the engine treats it as finish_text (speak what we have, end cleanly) and reports it - a conversation where the LLM died should degrade to a completed sentence, not a hung process. This auto-finish is an adaptive-ish behavior: it is deterministic (fixed timeout), satisfies the Alien-Artifact contract's deterministic-fallback requirement by construction.

TESTS (unit tests per the ftts-conformance observability convention): (a) underrun -> append -> resume produces frames identical to the never-stalled run (stall is side-effect-free: no KV drift, positions advance per frame not wall time); (b) underrun -> finish_text ends via genuine EOS path identically to whole-text; (c) cancel during stall exits promptly; (d) append rejected past context ceiling leaves the in-flight utterance intact; (e) budget: a synthetic stalled generator still trips the wedge detector when NOT in AwaitingText, and never trips it while legitimately stalled under the cap; (f) stall-timeout auto-finish emits the documented receipt.
close_reason: Landed and proven. DESIGN AS SPECIFIED: FrameStep tri-state enum (Frame/Finished/AwaitingText) replaced Option on FrameGenerator::next_frame across the workspace; QwenGenerator entry gate returns AwaitingText when continuation && !text_finished && frames_emitted >= trailing len - placed BEFORE select_talker so no RNG draws (side-effect-free by construction). ENGINE: TtsEngine::synthesize gains text_feed: Option<&BoundedReceiver<TextControl>> (Append(PreparedText)|Finish; new StreamKind::Text + text_control_queue + BoundedReceiver::try_next); feed presence selects UtteranceStart::Continuation; controls drained non-blocking at every frame boundary and block-polled (10ms, cancel-aware) during stalls; ROLLING ADMISSION re-admits at grown token count per append - accepted appends update the frame cap + emit ResourceAdmission, refused ones emit TextAppendRejected and leave the run intact; STALL-AWARE BUDGET: elapsed-stalled vs rolling deadline, so a 200ms text wait passes a 10ms frame budget while a true wedge still trips; stall cap EngineConfig::text_stall_timeout (default 60s) auto-finishes via TextStallEnded (deterministic fallback per Alien-Artifact contract); sender disconnect == Finish. EVIDENCE: 7 new engine unit tests green (pre-queued appends no-stall, late-text underrun w/ measured wait, cancel-during-stall prompt, stall-cap auto-finish, disconnect==finish, stall-vs-budget exclusion, ceiling-breaking append rejected + run survives) = ftts-core 78/78; generator-seam stall parity test green (3 repeated AwaitingText polls, zero KV growth, resumed run bit-identical to never-stalled whole run) = ftts-model-qwen 103/103; workspace all-targets compiled; fmt clean. DEVIATION: none material; observer event named TextStallEnded (not bead's tentative naming). Committed within peer sweep f7dc5da (which already consumes the API for CLI text-feed plumbing) + prior increments.

title: [RT1] talk protocol schema v2: ops/events, frozen fixture, robot schema
description:
Session protocol schema: the versioned NDJSON contract for `ftts talk` - ops, events, envelope, frozen fixture, and `robot schema` self-description.

RELATION TO ROBOT v1: the existing say/robot contract (SCHEMA_VERSION 1, 13 events, strict-closed validator at robot.rs:947, frozen fixture test) is FROZEN and untouched. The session speaks a sibling contract: session envelope {schema_version: 2, event, session_id, seq} on every stdout line, monotonically increasing seq, session_id generated like run_id (no text/filesystem info - stateless doctrine). Errors/diagnostics that are not protocol events go to stderr. Rationale for a separate version rather than extending v1: v1 consumers validate strict-closed against a frozen fixture; any new event type or field there is a breaking shape change, and the session's vocabulary is disjoint anyway.

OPS (client -> stdin, one JSON object per line; every op MAY carry a client "id" which is echoed in the corresponding ack/error - mpv-style correlation; unknown fields REJECTED, fail-closed symmetric with our own validator):
- {"op":"open","context":"c1","voice":"matt|/path.spk|/path/card.png","seed":7, "id":...} -> context_open. Voice resolution REUSES say's full surface: preset names, .spk files, AND voice cards (.png/.jpg import path) - the session must not be a lesser citizen than the one-shot CLI. seed is the CONTEXT seed (see seed discipline below).
- {"op":"say","context":"c1","text":"...","continue":true|false,"seed":<optional per-utterance override>} - first say on an idle context starts synthesis immediately (fast TTFA); continue:true keeps the utterance open for appends; text chunks are concatenated VERBATIM (the session never re-splits; it withholds a trailing partial word for BPE boundary hygiene until the next chunk or flush - the continuation API bead pins why)
- {"op":"flush","context":"c1"} - release the withheld partial-word tail AND finish the open utterance (semantically identical to say with empty text and continue:false; both exist deliberately - flush is the explicit "the LLM stream ended" verb, and redundancy here is cheaper than a client bug from forgetting which form ends an utterance)
- {"op":"cancel","context":"c1"} - frame-boundary stop + truncation receipt
- {"op":"close","context":"c1"} / {"op":"shutdown"}
Malformed line / unknown op -> session_error with remediation; the SESSION SURVIVES (a bad request must not kill the warm model - same posture as the resident's catch_unwind).

SEED DISCIPLINE (reproducibility is a claim class - skill taxonomy: "Reproducible sample" needs explicit seed + artifact/version/route): each utterance N in a context synthesizes with an EFFECTIVE SEED derived deterministically from (context_seed, N), overridable per-say. THE DERIVATION FUNCTION IS PART OF THE FROZEN CONTRACT: a pinned, documented, build-stable mix (e.g. splitmix64 over context_seed XOR N - pick one, write it into the schema docs and a unit test with fixed input/output vectors). Never a std hasher (RandomState is randomized per process; DefaultHasher's algorithm is explicitly not stability-guaranteed across releases) - a replay next year on a newer build must derive the same effective seeds or the reproducibility claim is false. Rationale for derivation at all: a fixed context seed reused verbatim would make every utterance share one RNG stream whose state depends on prior utterance lengths (irreproducible in isolation); per-utterance derivation makes every utterance independently reproducible given (context_seed, N) or its override. speak_start echoes the effective seed so receipts are self-contained.

EVENTS (stdout): session_start{version, model digest/route identifiers, pcm:{format:"s16le",rate:24000,channels:1}, pid} - emitted once when the engine is loaded and the session is ready to accept say (the eager-load handshake the runtime bead needs) | ack{id,op,context} | context_open{context,voice,...} | speak_start{context,utterance,seed} | audio{context,utterance,byte_offset,bytes,frames,frame_index} (+ttfa_ms on the first of an utterance) | progress{context,utterance,frames_emitted,text_consumed_tokens,text_buffered_tokens} (rate-limited, ~1/s) | buffer{context,queued_ms} | text_underrun{context,waited_ms} | speak_cancelled{context,utterance,frames_delivered,audio_ms,text_spoken_tokens,spoken_text} | speak_complete{context,utterance,frames,audio_ms,ttfa_ms,rtf} | context_closed | session_end | session_error{kind,message,remediation}. Every event carries the envelope. byte_offset/bytes are the cross-channel sequencing authority for the PCM stream, which is ONE CONTINUOUS SESSION-GLOBAL byte stream (byte_offset is cumulative across utterances and contexts; segmentation happens via events, never via in-band markers - nothing but PCM ever appears on the audio channel).

DELIVERABLES:
1. The schema as code: event/op structs + strict-closed validator (reuse the v1 validator machinery, parameterized by catalogue - do not fork it).
2. Frozen JSON fixture + contract test validating every emitted event shape, exactly like v1's. This fixture is the compatibility gate for all future session changes.
3. `ftts robot schema` gains the session catalogue (self-describing contract, AGENTS Agent Ergonomics).
4. Exit codes for the talk process documented in error.rs (clean shutdown 0; startup/model failure uses existing codes; session-fatal transport failure gets a documented code).

DESIGN NOTES FOR FUTURE SELF: spoken_text in speak_cancelled is the tokenizer-decoded prefix actually delivered (see the truncation bead for the char-boundary care); it exists so the ORCHESTRATOR can rewrite its assistant turn to what the user actually heard - the OpenAI-Realtime conversation.item.truncate semantic, which production voice frameworks converged on after LLMs repeating unheard content became a top field bug. queued_ms in buffer events is delivered-not-yet-consumed depth estimated from the PCM channel queue - the orchestrator's pacing signal; pipes give kernel backpressure but the app-level number is what lets a client keep its playback buffer at 2-3 frames for fast barge-in.
close_reason: Landed in 00c8d01 (mid-flight snapshot with ScarletLynx) + 7dc3e3e (completion). Deliverables: (1) session_protocol.rs — 14-event/6-op v2 catalogue, envelope {schema_version,event,session_id,seq}, strict-closed validation through the SAME parameterized walk as v1 (robot::validate_object/WireContract — not forked); (2) frozen fixture fixtures/session_schema_v2.json + session_contract.rs conformance suite (8 tests: freeze, self-description, per-entry conformance, drift, stream validation, exit-code publication); (3) ftts robot schema [run|session] — default run output byte-identical to v1 (robot_contract 9/9 still green against the untouched fixture); (4) FttsExitCode::SessionTransport=9 documented in error.rs and published in the v2 exit-code map; seed derivation splitmix64(context_seed ^ N) pinned with fixed vectors. Evidence: ftts-cli lib 69 pass, ftts-conformance unit 41 + robot_contract 9 + session_contract 8 pass, clippy -D warnings clean both crates. Note: producer/runtime wiring is edz0's; the exit code has no producer yet — documented contract only, as the bead specifies.
