title: [RT1] talk session runtime: control loop, engine ownership, PCM channel
description:
Session runtime: the `ftts talk` process - control loop, engine ownership, PCM delivery, and flow control.

THREAD TOPOLOGY (three threads, all channels bounded, honoring one-parallel-owner):
1. STDIN READER: line-oriented reads, parses/validates ops, forwards onto a bounded control channel. Never blocks on anything but stdin and the bounded send (a full control queue backpressures the client through the pipe - correct).
2. SYNTHESIS THREAD (the single parallel owner): owns TtsEngine + the persistent QwenGenerator + prepared int8 route + reused CodecStreamingState (this IS the warm-engine bead's persistent context - that refactor is a hard dependency, not a nice-to-have). Drives the frame loop; between frames drains the control channel non-blockingly for append/finish/cancel targeting the active utterance; on AwaitingText parks on that channel (the stall bead's design). Model load happens lazily on first open or eagerly at spawn behind a flag - default EAGER, announced by the session_start event (the schema bead defines it), because a conversation's first turn should not pay 3.7 s (document the flag for memory-sensitive callers). PROFILE DEFAULT: talk runs the INTERACTIVE profile (1-frame packets) unless overridden - a conversation session that waited 4 frames for first audio would defeat its own purpose; this makes the profile-packet-wiring bead a hard dependency too.
3. PCM WRITER: consumes the StreamQueues pcm queue, writes to fd 3 or --pcm-out, emits audio events (via a bounded event channel back to the stdout writer - stdout is owned by ONE writer to keep NDJSON lines atomic). Byte accounting lives here: byte_offset is the authoritative cumulative count of bytes WRITTEN to the channel.

PCM CHANNEL RULES: fd 3 when inherited open (spawn contract documented with an example; detect via a cheap fcntl F_GETFD probe at startup), else --pcm-out path (regular file or FIFO; FIFO is the streaming case - document that the session blocks until a reader opens it, and that a reader disappearing = broken pipe = session_error + context cancel, session survives). WINDOWS: fd-3 inheritance is a unixism and does not exist there - on Windows the PCM channel is --pcm-out only (regular file or a named pipe path the client creates); document this in --help and return a clear session_error if fd mode is requested on Windows. The event vocabulary is identical on both platforms. Refuse `say` with no PCM channel configured - fail-closed at open time with remediation text, not at first audio. STREAM SEMANTICS: the channel carries ONE continuous session-global byte stream; silence between utterances is the ABSENCE of writes, never zero-padding - the session must not manufacture silence bytes (a player consuming the fd handles underflow by playing silence itself; padding in-band would corrupt byte accounting and make gaps unskippable). byte_offset in audio events is the cumulative session count; utterance/context segmentation is event-side only.

FLOW CONTROL AND THE DEADLOCK OBLIGATION (AGENTS rule 5: audio and event channels must not be able to deadlock each other): audio flows stdin-reader-independent; the event channel to stdout is bounded but events are droppable-by-class under pressure (progress/buffer are coalescable - keep latest; lifecycle events speak_start/complete/cancelled/error are NEVER dropped and their channel capacity is sized for worst-case lifecycle burst). A stalled stdout consumer therefore cannot stall audio; a stalled PCM consumer parks synthesis via the tested backpressure chain (sink -> codec worker -> frame channel -> generator) WITHOUT stalling control processing (cancel must remain deliverable while audio is parked - the synthesis thread's park is on the control channel OR the sink send; verify cancel unparks both: BoundedSender's send loop checks the token each poll, and the control park wakes on any op).

CONTEXT LIFECYCLE: open validates voice (preset name or .spk path - reuse say's resolution; NOTE the skill's warning that preset resolution can write staging state: the session resolves ONCE at open, and open is the mutation point, documented); one utterance active at a time; say on a context while another context is speaking = queued or rejected - DECISION: rejected with session_error kind "busy" in v1 (the orchestrator owns turn-taking; queueing hides latency bugs). Multiple contexts open concurrently is fine (they hold only voice/seed config + any withheld text tail, not engine state).

IDLE/EXIT: no idle timeout by default (a conversation can pause; the orchestrator owns the process lifetime); FTTS_TALK_IDLE_SECS optional. stdin EOF == shutdown. SIGTERM/SIGINT -> cancel active utterance, emit session_end, exit 0 (clean, since the operator asked). Do NOT spawn or consult the resident daemon from talk (--no-resident semantics implicit: the session IS the warm engine; two warm models on one host is a footgun and a memory surprise).

TESTS (unit tests per the ftts-conformance observability convention): control-loop unit tests with a fake generator (op ordering, busy rejection, malformed-line survival, EOF shutdown); channel-topology tests: slow stdout consumer does not delay audio bytes; slow PCM consumer does not delay cancel processing (the two obligations above, each with a receipts-logged latency bound); FIFO reader-vanishes case; eager-load ready event. Full-model e2e lives in the session e2e bead.
close_reason: Landed and proven LIVE on this machine (release binary, real model, M4 Pro under swarm load). RUNTIME (crates/ftts-cli/src/talk.rs, commits 75faab4+e2469d0+f36b9d3): five-thread topology per the bead - stdin reader -> router (session state, fail-closed op validation via frozen v2 schema, every op acked/errored with id echo); synthesis thread as the single parallel owner driving synth::synthesize with the continuation text feed + INTERACTIVE 1-frame packets; PCM writer with session-global cumulative byte accounting (audio written+flushed BEFORE its event, silence = absence of writes, no in-band padding); one stdout owner for atomic NDJSON. Audio channel: /dev/fd/3 adoption via std (no unsafe) or --pcm-out; Windows --pcm-out only. Eager load announced by session_start{model,route,pcm,pid}. splitmix64 per-utterance seeds echoed in speak_start. BPE-hygienic tail withholding; verbatim concat. Cold-row re-gather seam (part 1) makes open-vocabulary appends work. Busy/idle/no-context/malformed all fail closed, session survives. EOF==shutdown; cancelled utterances SETTLE with their receipt even during shutdown (race found+fixed live). Resident never consulted; talk dispatches before cli_main's stdio locks (reentrant-guard deadlock found+fixed live). LIVE EVIDENCE (7 scripted sessions in /private/tmp/ftts-talk-smoke): golden run seed 7 -> 67x 1-frame audio events with exact offsets, 257,280 PCM bytes, BYTE-IDENTICAL across two separate processes (live reproducibility receipt); 3-chunk continuation + flush -> ONE 77-frame utterance; warm ttfa_ms 374 at load ~50; barge-in -> speak_cancelled{frames_delivered,audio_ms exact, wrapper-free spoken_text}; seq strictly contiguous; all event kinds from the frozen catalogue. DEVIATIONS/HONESTY: (1) receipt text fields are a documented UPPER BOUND - consumption outruns speech ~4x (live finding, schema+fixture amended through the reviewable-diff flow; exact alignment recorded as sc94 follow-on); (2) text_underrun event wired via engine observer but not yet observed live (generation under load absorbs multi-second gaps - the designed masking; deterministic stall proof lives in the 7pgn driver); (3) progress/buffer events defined but not yet emitted by the runtime (coalescable class, additive, 7pgn scope); (4) FIFO reader-vanishes and Windows paths compile-proven only. The 7pgn e2e battery formalizes the smoke scripts; sc94 carries alignment + cancel matrix.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: DISCOVERED GAP (2026-08-22, hsio work): appended chunks whose tokens fall outside the INITIAL utterance's gathered text-embedding rows fail closed in project_text_ids ('text token N was not gathered...', generate.rs:609) - correct fail-closed behavior, but it means the session runtime MUST re-gather cold rows at append time and extend the generator's compact table, exactly like wasm's cold-row injection (synthesize_with_text_rows). Concretely for this bead: on say(continue) appends, the session (a) tokenizes+wraps the chunk, (b) gathers missing rows via model.talker.gather_text_rows for the new ids, (c) extends the generator's TextEmbeddingWeights table (needs a small new generator/table API - extend_gathered_rows or similar, mirroring wasm), THEN sends TextControl::Append. Until that lands, synth-level continuations only work when appended ids are a subset of the initial gather - which is why hsio's gate 5 (chunked==whole through the full synth process at every packet size) is recorded as blocked-by-this rather than faked with an engineered fixture.

title: EPIC Bakeoff: three sequential gates (champion validation)
description:
EPIC — Bakeoff: three sequential gates validating the champion choice (Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base) against challenger Kyutai Pocket TTS 100M.

WHY THREE GATES: the original single kill rule ("Pocket wins if >=2x systems advantage after equivalent optimization") was CIRCULAR — it demanded optimization evidence before optimization exists. Fix: Gate A (upstream quality, official implementations only — Pocket eliminated if it fails a predeclared identity/naturalness floor vs Qwen; its published Elo deficit is -114 vs Chatterbox on speaker similarity, which is WHY it is challenger not champion); Gate B (architectural systems potential from the -1B cost model + microbenchmarks, organized around an explicit stage isomorphism map: text/prefill <-> text/prefill, talker backbone <-> Pocket backbone, microdecoder <-> consistency frame head, RVQ codec <-> causal VAE, streaming <-> streaming — so continuous-frame vs discrete-16-group comparison is structural, not rhetorical); Gate C (optimized confirmation ONLY if A and B pass: displacement requires BOTH >=~95% human-preference retention on identity+naturalness AND >=2x end-to-end systems advantage; failing either, Qwen stays champion).

IMPORTANT COMMITMENTS: Gate C's Pocket path is timeboxed/representative — the timebox bounds DECISION EVIDENCE only; a mixed verdict (Pocket wins some regimes) HARD-REQUIRES the dual-engine product (Pocket as ultra-edge profile in the same CLI) via the skill's full add-model recipe with complete certification. Qwen3-TTS 1.7B serves as upper-bound quality reference only. Artifacts live under docs/bakeoff/. Gates A+B verdicts are Phase-3 entry evidence.

title: EPIC Phase -1A: Exact Model Truth (truth pack + oracle)
description:
EPIC — Phase -1A: Exact Model Truth (truth pack + oracle). THE FOUNDATION: no kernel ships until its per-component gates are green.

CONTEXT: franken_tts is a pure-Rust, memory-safe, CPU-hyper-optimized library + single-binary CLI (ftts) running Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base (zero-shot voice-cloning TTS; Apache-2.0 pending OQ-1 verification) with NO general ML framework, per the /ai-model-into-rust-mega-fused-hyper-kernel doctrine. Project thesis: the model hides a 15-step autoregressive Residual-Code Microdecoder inside every 80 ms frame (28-layer talker once -> 5-layer microdecoder x15 SEQUENTIAL -> causal codec decode), ~1.65 GB Q8 weight traffic per frame on the sequential baseline (~20.7 GB/s at 1x real time). We turn that microdecoder from the model's largest CPU liability into its largest optimization advantage: cache-resident hot-packing, per-depth quantization, and FrankenMTP speculative block verification.

WHY THIS EPIC EXISTS: every architectural fact currently carries a [SOURCE] tag (read from the LIVE official repo/configs during plan review; URLs in plan v2.1 section 17) or [REPORTED]. Plan v1 shipped a load-bearing architecture error (missed the 15x microdecoder loop) precisely because facts were unpinned. This epic pins + hashes every source, promotes/corrects every fact, resolves OQ-1..OQ-17, extracts docs/QWEN3_TTS_EXECUTABLE_SPEC.md, and stands up the reference oracle + its measured nondeterminism floor (oracle BEFORE engine — the governing skill's Phase 0 lives here, assigned explicitly so it cannot fall through the cracks).

GATING POLICY (v2.1): truth gating is PER-COMPONENT — a kernel is blocked only by the unresolved OQs it depends on; a watermark question does not block a verified talker GEMV.

EXIT: per-component truth gates green for talker, microdecoder, codec, encoders, prompt builder; oracle fixtures + committed nondeterminism-floor envelope; executable spec committed.

title: EPIC Phase -1B: Cost and Feasibility Model
description:
EPIC — Phase -1B: Cost & Feasibility Model (the v2 centerpiece; runs after/alongside -1A, before ANY heroic kernel work).

WHY: v1 promised speed numbers before understanding the machine. The corrected traffic model shows ~1.65 GB/frame sequential baseline (~20.7 GB/s at 1x RT; the microdecoder body alone is ~1.18 GB/frame reread 15x). Whether targets like 5x-RT-on-M4 are even physically plausible depends on measurements nobody has yet: cache residency of the ~110 MB-class microdecoder hot working set UNDER talker interference, W8A8-vs-W8A16 winners at real shapes, packet-size behavior, and the FrankenMTP acceptance-surface primitives. Until this epic completes, ALL speed numbers are hypotheses, never promises (G2 policy).

CONTENT: a generated costed execution graph (per-op: component, layer, residual depth, shape, dtype, executions/frame, weight/activation/KV bytes, MACs, predicted cache level, parallel dim, kernel candidates); instrumentation of the official + MLX/GGML implementations per stage; per-SKU memory-hierarchy measurements; the Metal microdecoder spike; the seven feasibility questions incl. break-even acceptance alpha*(SKU); bakeoff Gate A concludes + Gate B runs here.

EXIT: all seven questions answered with measurements; docs/PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md committed; numeric G2 targets + roofline-efficiency factors set; the section-7.1 hot-op ranking re-ranked from data per profile.

title: EPIC Phase 1: Exact safe forward (ConformanceExact)
description:
EPIC — Phase 1: Exact safe forward (ConformanceExact green end-to-end, BF16/f32, zero optimization).

WHY FIRST: correctness outranks speed, always (G1 > G2). This phase lands the ENTIRE forward pipeline code-first in safe Rust — text/prompt path (verbatim mode), talker with mRoPE, the SEQUENTIAL 15-step microdecoder (the honest baseline every later lever must match bit-for-bit or distributionally), streaming+offline codec, both cloning paths (x-vector via ECAPA speaker encoder; ICL via codec encoder + transcript), two-level sampler with canonical greedy mode — then proves it seam-by-seam against oracle fixtures (teacher-forced per talker layer, per microdecoder depth, per codec block).

KEY RULES: implement from the extracted spec, never line-by-line from Python; weights stay ZERO-COPY BF16-resident (widen at the accessor — no whole-model f32 expansion; the text embedding alone is ~622 MB); rayon parallelism is fine here (KernelTeam comes in Phase 3); every module carries unit tests with detailed logging; streaming==batch is a standing gate from day one (chunked codec decode with ring buffers must equal offline decode of the same tokens).

EXIT: ConformanceExact ladder green end-to-end (L0 front-end exact -> L1 per-op -> L2 per-layer/depth/block -> L3 logits argmax-exact where oracle reproduces itself -> L4 codec-token stream exact under canonical greedy -> L5 audio per the pre-committed OQ-12 fork); WeightsManifest census passes; both clone modes produce reference-matching outputs.
close_reason: Closed EPIC Phase 1: Exact safe forward (ConformanceExact). All Phase 1 child tasks and exit gates completed: tokenizer (NFC byte-level BPE), zero-copy BF16 weights loader, prompt assembly (4 variants), talker forward (mRoPE/GQA/SwiGLU), 15-step sequential microdecoder, two-level sampler, streaming+offline codec decoder with ring buffers, ECAPA speaker encoder, codec encoder, audio core, audio diagnostics, STFT/mel front end, and full ConformanceExact end-to-end assembly exit gate.

comments.author: cc_1
comments.text:
TRUTH PACK CORRECTION C-1 (from frankentts-t-pin-sources-b2u) — LOAD-BEARING, changes the per-frame execution graph.

Plan §2.1's pseudocode ends at 'enqueue the 16-code frame for the codec'. The pinned source
(snapshots/gh/qwen_tts/core/models/modeling_qwen3_tts.py:1671-1692) does two more things per frame:

  1. All 16 code embeddings are SUMMED into the talker's NEXT-step input:
       inputs_embeds = cat([talker_emb(code0)] + [depth_emb[i](code_{i+1}) for i in 0..14]).sum(1)
  2. A text hidden state is ADDED on top, one per frame:
       + trailing_text_hidden[:, generation_step]   if generation_step < len(trailing_text_hidden)
       + tts_pad_embed                              otherwise

Consequence: the text stream is consumed ONE HIDDEN PER FRAME, interleaved with audio generation —
it is NOT a prefill-only prefix. Any forward that treats text as fully consumed at prefill desyncs
after frame 1. Also adds a 16-way embedding-sum + add to the hot loop op set.

Full detail + citations: docs/truth-pack/FACT_DISPOSITIONS.md (C-1).

title: EPIC Phase 2: Canonical Q8 artifact (.fttsq/.fttspack)
description:
EPIC — Phase 2: Canonical Q8 artifact (.fttsq + .fttspack + staged quantization).

STRATEGY (START WITH INT8, NOT Q4 — nominal bit width is not a performance metric): per-output-channel INT8 weights on talker + microdecoder GEMMs; dynamic INT8 activations where the hardware path is genuinely fast; INT32 accumulation with fused requant; HIGH PRECISION kept for all norms, sampling-logits boundaries, RVQ codec codebooks, speaker-conditioning path, codec-sensitive layers. Codec at Q8 with high-precision codebooks (the upstream GGML maintainer's converged policy — validate exact set via OQ-13). EMBEDDINGS ARE DIFFERENTIATED: the ~622 MB cold text embedding is a legitimate separately-gated Q8 experiment (row-wise cold access); acoustic RVQ codebooks stay high-precision. Per-depth precision on the 15 microdecoder depths is a first-class axis.

ARTIFACT SPLIT (load-bearing): .fttsq = immutable canonical portable model (logical tensors, recipe, manifest, per-section SHA-256, license/NOTICE, NO machine-specific tiling; ~1.6 GB-class with BF16 text embedding, ~1.3 GB if Q8-embedding experiment passes) vs .fttspack = regenerable per-machine execution cache (packed layouts, microdecoder hot pack, autotuned KernelPlan; keyed by model hash + kernel ABI + CPU + ISA + packing version + quant mode + autotune hash). Conversion is STREAMING and bounded-memory (never load whole BF16 model into RAM widened to f32). Runtime quantization ships FIRST; the converter reuses the identical quantizer function so artifact==runtime is byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION.

EXIT: staged levers (talker -> microdecoder -> heads gated -> codec Q8) each pass ConformanceExact + ProductionQuality gates; hardened parsers fuzzed; round-trip determinism proven.

title: EPIC Phase 3A: Microdecoder engine (ResidualCodeDecoder + FrankenMTP)
description:
EPIC — Phase 3A: The Microdecoder Engine (ResidualCodeDecoder + FrankenMTP). THE FLAGSHIP EPIC and the critical path of the whole project.

WHY IT IS THE FLAGSHIP: per 80 ms frame the 5-layer microdecoder runs 15 SEQUENTIAL times with per-depth embeddings and per-depth 2048-way heads — ~1.21 GB/frame of the ~1.65 GB sequential baseline (12.5 x 15 x 5 = 937.5 microdecoder-layer evaluations per second of speech vs 350 talker-layer evaluations). The official implementation runs this through full generic HF generation machinery; a fixed-topology zero-allocation engine is the single most model-specific thing this project builds.

CONTENT: the ResidualCodeDecoder (fixed 15-step loop, compile-time shapes, per-frame-reset tiny KV, precomputed 16-position RoPE table, direct per-depth embed/head indexing, no allocation, no generic machinery); the ~110 MB-class MTP hot pack in .fttspack (cache residency, operationally measured); the seq-16 verification kernel (a custom multi-head-per-position engine, NOT a stock LM pass); FrankenMTP drafter #1 (previous-frame residuals + transition stats — no training needed) with greedy-mode exactness by construction; the named speculative-sampling algorithm for sampled mode (OQ-19); the AF-3 e-value reliability monitor (kill-switch; NOT an exactness substitute); MTP-first Q4 experiments.

CLAIM TIERS (pre-written so a sour OQ-5 cannot collapse the epic): Tier 1 (training-mode forward mask/distribution-equivalent to the 15-step loop) = exact verifier, strict token identity + sampled distributional exactness claimable. Tier 2 (not equivalent) = approximate draft assistance, Contract-B-only claims, AF-3 always on, sequential path stays the only exact mode.

EXIT: sequential engine at/near its roofline per -1B; FrankenMTP verdict (keep with tier claim / revert with ledger entry); every lever behind FTTS_* kill-switches with parity receipts.

title: EPIC Phase 3B: Talker and prefill engine
description:
EPIC — Phase 3B: Talker & prefill engine.

SCOPE: the 28-layer talker on the KernelTeam as a persistent dispatch-free loop (per-layer fused pass 1: norm -> QKV -> QK-Norm(if OQ-3 confirms) -> mRoPE -> GQA attention -> O-proj -> residual; pass 2: norm -> gate||up -> SiLU-mul -> down -> residual with the corrected two-pass norm->quant fusion); exact-shape int8 GEMV kernels (1024/2048/3072/128 shapes all tile cleanly); the register-blocked tiled SMMLA/VNNI prefill GEMM (the "wedge" kernel frankentorch names but does not ship); the text projection MLP (2048->2048->1024 SiLU) in the prefill path; prompt partial evaluation + .ftvoice-cache static-prefix KV reuse (cache ONLY the maximal prefix proven independent of target text per OQ-10); long-context KV layout + admission integration.

KEY NUMBERS: talker body ~440 MB Q8/frame; q_proj 1024->2048, o_proj 2048->1024, MLP 1024->3072; worst-case i32 accumulation at K=3072 (U8S8 <= ~99.5M, >=21x headroom — proof obligation in shipped selftest). TTFA is dominated by this epic's prefill path plus the first codec packet — it is the interactive profile's critical path per the -1B ranking.

EXIT: fused talker loop bit-identical to the Phase-1 reference; prefill at/near roofline; norm->quant fusion proven byte-identity-preserving; voice-cache prefix reuse proven equal to full prefill (metamorphic gate).

title: EPIC Phase 3C: Codec and streaming engine
description:
EPIC — Phase 3C: Codec & streaming engine.

WHY CO-EQUAL: many local TTS ports optimize the language model then discover the codec dominates end-to-end latency. Our codec (speech tokenizer decoder) is ~291 MB Q8 community-measured: 8 transformer-like layers (hidden 512, 16 heads x head_dim 64 — attention width 1024 = 2x hidden, same wider-than-hidden signature as the talker; sliding window 72), causal convs, upsample rates [8,5,4,3] (product 480, x4 base hop = 1920 samples per 12.5 Hz frame at 24 kHz — exact hop math confirmed by OQ-7).

CONTENT: stateful causal-conv ring buffers (receptive-field-sized, preallocated, state across chunks); fused conv+bias+norm+activation; specialized small attention at the exact codec shape; NO im2col materialization (direct conv loops at small fixed shapes); streaming upsampling writing directly into the output PCM buffer; distinct encode/decode builds (synthesis artifacts need not carry encoder machinery); packet adaptivity (1/2/4/auto frames — official stack uses 4-frame 320 ms packets; packet size is an execution-policy parameter, never silently equated with the 80 ms model frame); cancellation still checked every talker frame regardless of packet size.

STANDING GATE: streaming == offline decode of the same token stream, bit-identical target (same ops, same order) — ring-buffer state correctness is an e-process invariant in the gauntlet, plus chunk-boundary fuzzing and sustained streaming tests with backpressure/cancellation semantics.

EXIT: codec at/near roofline; packet autotuning wired to profiles; streaming==offline proof green; sustained tests green.

title: EPIC Phase 3D: Server throughput (continuous batching)
description:
EPIC — Phase 3D: Server throughput (continuous batching on high-core AMD).

THE INSIGHT: N isolated per-stream engines reread the same weights N times. A central frame scheduler batches the talker step across all ready streams (GEMV -> GEMM, weights read once), then batches EACH microdecoder depth 0..14 across streams (valid because streams are independent; each stream's depth-d token depends only on its OWN depth-(d-1)), then batches/pipelines codec packets — preserving every utterance's autoregressive dependency while amortizing every matrix read. This is the primary throughput axis on Threadripper/EPYC.

CONTENT: the frame/depth batching scheduler; the RAGGED FrankenMTP x batching joint design (under speculation streams reject at different depths — candidate policies: pad-and-mask cohorts, cohort splitting by accept depth, dual-lane scheduler with verify lane + sequential-repair lane, per-cohort re-drafting; ONE scheduler design shared with Phase 3A, not two independent diagrams); NUMA-local weight packs + CCD-aware affinity; admission control + queueing policy + the capacity certificate; AF-5 USL sweeps feeding pool_sizing tables and N-bucket KernelTeam partition rebind rules.

OWNERSHIP INVARIANT: the batching scheduler IS the engine's single parallel owner — multi-stream inside ONE fan-out, never N concurrent fan-outs; fttsd admission rides the same capacity model.

METRICS (headline): aggregate RTF (generated-audio-seconds per wall-clock second per socket), streams/socket, p95 admission-to-first-packet queueing latency under load, joules per generated minute.

title: EPIC Phase 4: The voice compiler
description:
EPIC — Phase 4: The Voice Compiler (enrollment as the project's SECOND THESIS).

PITCH: ftts enroll compiles messy real-world recordings into a reproducible, scored, portable voice asset. Reference-preparation quality often buys more perceived clone quality than another 15 percent of kernel speed — continuation-style cloners reproduce defects in the prompt recording (documented by Pocket upstream; assume Qwen shares the failure mode), so the tool must say so BEFORE the user discovers it in output.

CONTENT: automatic reference-segment discovery (VAD -> reject overlap/multi-speaker -> score clipping/SNR/reverb/music/stationarity -> phonetic coverage from transcript -> select candidate 3-12 s segments -> synthesize a fixed audition set from each -> rank objectively + optional listener preference -> preserve chosen segment AND alternatives in the enrollment report); ICL as the quality default (modes: quality=transcript-backed ICL, quick=x-vector-only with upstream-documented possible quality reduction, auto=ICL when transcript verifies else x-vector WITH WARNING — never presented as interchangeable equals); transcript verification (duration consistency, alignment confidence, omission/repetition detection, external ASR plugin contract — the shipping binary contains NO ASR); multi-reference selection-BEFORE-averaging; AF-4 formal treatment (submodular segment/multi-ref selection + attribute->quality loss model calibrated on the audition benchmark; fallback whole-file enrollment).

ARTIFACTS: portable .ftvoice (identity data + provenance + CONSENT ATTESTATION + reproducible preprocessing recipe; profiles portable/private/minimal) vs derived .ftvoice-cache (recomputable prompt/KV caches keyed by voice-recipe hash + model hash + prompt-builder version + streaming mode + quant recipe + math mode + engine ABI).

ETHICS (doctrine 10): no acquisition features, consent recorded, upstream watermark preserved (OQ-8).

title: EPIC Phase 7: Certify + ship
description:
EPIC — Phase 7: Certify + ship.

CONTENT: release certification via the /running-the-gauntlet-on-your-rust-port machinery — three pillars (performance / conformance / surface parity), no victory-on-one-while-another-regresses; conformal lower-bound release ratchet (ship decisions use the LOWER bound, never point estimates); e-processes (anytime-valid) over the standing invariants: streaming==batch, admission-before-allocation, i32-overflow at census worst-case K, determinism scope, SIMD==scalar; >=10 convergence rounds with >=2-clean-round tail; skip-honest ladder receipts (a skipped rung is NEVER mistaken for green).

title: EPIC Verification infrastructure (contracts + listening + reliability)
description:
EPIC — Verification infrastructure (the two conformance contracts + listening protocol + reliability gates). Cross-cutting: this infra is INDEPENDENTLY REUSABLE, which is why it gets its own beads (per policy, implementation issues otherwise own their test criteria).

THE CENTRAL INSIGHT (v2): the official model SAMPLES at both autoregressive levels (talker T0.9/k50/rep1.05; residual T0.9/k50 — read from generation_config), so one ladder cannot serve two masters: a tiny legitimate logit perturbation can flip a token and diverge the whole sequence with zero perceptual harm. title: [RT1] Continuation API: FrameGenerator append_text/finish_text on trailing_text_hidden
description:
Continuation API: extend FrameGenerator with append_text/finish_text and implement them on QwenGenerator by appending projected rows to trailing_text_hidden.

TRAIT CHANGE. FrameGenerator (ftts-core/src/lib.rs:538-546) is today begin_utterance(&PreparedText) + next_frame(). Add: append_text(&PreparedText) -> Result<()> (extend the in-flight utterance's trailing text) and finish_text() -> Result<()> (no more text will arrive; the terminal tts_eos becomes reachable). Early development, no users, no compat shims (AGENTS Backwards Compatibility): change the trait directly and update the one production implementor (QwenGenerator) plus test fakes.

QWENGENERATOR IMPLEMENTATION:
- begin_utterance gains a continuation mode (an explicit flag on the utterance start, carried from the session's say op): in continuation mode, prompt assembly must NOT push the terminal tts_eos at the end of trailing_text_hidden (assemble_xvector currently does: target_text.push(tts_eos) at prompt.rs:~296-298). Hold tts_eos back; finish_text() appends it. The NON-continuation path is byte-for-byte unchanged - the parity gate depends on that.
- append_text: tokenize happened upstream (PreparedText); here: gather_text_rows from the cold embedding mmap + project_text_ids (generate.rs:600) for the new ids, push resulting hidden rows onto utterance.trailing_text_hidden. UtteranceState is private inside QwenGenerator (generate.rs:297 area) - this is a method on the generator, not external surgery.
- THREADING/HOT-LOOP RULE (doctrine 4: no second parallel owner; the generator needs no internal synchronization). Split the append work by what it needs: TOKENIZATION + NORMALIZATION need no model state - they run on the session CONTROL thread, producing PreparedText. GATHER (cold-embedding mmap rows) + PROJECTION (the 2048->2048->1024 SiLU MLP) read weights owned by the generator - they run on the SYNTHESIS thread, between frames, inside append_text called under &mut self: the PreparedText arrives via the bounded control channel the stall subtask defines, the synthesis thread drains it between next_frame calls and performs gather+project there. No lock is ever held across parallel work (AGENTS rule 5); the frame loop's exclusive ownership of the generator is untouched. COST BUDGET: projection is a small GEMM over a handful of tokens; at 12.5 Hz with ~1.5x RTF there is ~25-45 ms of slack per frame. The tests must include a receipt-logged measurement of append cost for a typical sentence (10-25 tokens) and assert no frame deadline miss; if a long paragraph append ever threatens the deadline, the fallback is chunked internal application (apply N tokens per inter-frame gap) - note it as the contingency, do not build it until measurement says so.
- Position semantics: appended rows are consumed at future frames_emitted indices; mRoPE position ids advance per frame exactly as today - appending changes NOTHING about positions. Assert in tests.

TOKENIZATION AT CHUNK BOUNDARIES (the correctness trap): BPE merges can span a naive chunk boundary. Contract pinned here: (a) append_text receives ALREADY-PREPARED tokens; the SESSION is responsible for boundary hygiene - it withholds a trailing partial word (no terminal whitespace/punctuation) until the next chunk or flush; (b) normalization runs per-chunk through the same TextPreparer as whole-text (normalization context does not cross chunks; if a divergence vs whole-text normalization is ever observed on realistic sentence chunks, that is a ledgered discrepancy to evaluate, not silently absorbed); (c) the parity fixtures assert token-stream equality BEFORE comparing audio, and report tokenization divergence as a distinct outcome (invalid fixture), never a comparison failure.

TESTS (unit tests per the ftts-conformance observability convention): (a) append-then-generate token/hidden bookkeeping: trailing_text_hidden length, consumption index, tts_eos position after finish_text; (b) non-continuation path unchanged: whole-text synthesis before/after this change is bit-identical (regression pin); (c) append after utterance finished / before begin_utterance / double finish_text are clean errors; (d) mRoPE position invariance assertion across an append; (e) ICL-mode begin_utterance with continuation flag = explicit unsupported error (scope limit, x-vector only in v1).
close_reason: Landed in 1b8b4c5. Trait: UtteranceStart {Fresh, Continuation} + append_text/finish_text on FrameGenerator; engine path stays Fresh (session wiring is edz0). QwenGenerator: continuation mode holds the terminal tts_eos out of the assembled stream via prompt::hold_tts_eos (streaming x-vector only — ICL/non-streaming rejected in validate_input AND at begin_utterance); append_text runs cold-table gather + projection on the synthesis thread between frames and only extends the trailing stream — positions/KV untouched by construction; finish_text releases the generator's own tts_eos row. THE exactness gate: chunked_appends_match_whole_text_bit_for_bit pins code-for-code identity plus position invariance across an append (tiny synthetic weights, greedy). Error cases are clean errors (before begin / after model EOS / fresh-append / double finish / post-finish append). Cost receipt printed and asserted < 80 ms frame budget at synthetic 25-token scale — real-weights receipt deferred to session e2e, noted honestly. Evidence: ftts-core 71, ftts-model-qwen 102 incl. 5 new, ftts-cli lib 69 pass; clippy -D warnings clean across all five touched crates. Chunk-boundary hygiene contract lives in the trait docs + bead text (caller withholds trailing partial words).

title: [RT1] Continuation parity gates: chunked==whole, stall metamorphics, boundary fuzz
description:
Continuation parity gates: chunked == whole bit-identity, stall metamorphics, and boundary fuzzing - the standing gates that let continuations ship without a listening campaign.

PRINCIPLE. Continuations touch zero numerics: same kernels, same sampler, same codec. The only new degrees of freedom are WHEN text rows become visible and WHERE tts_eos lands. Therefore every gate here is EXACT (bit-identity), in the ConformanceExact family, and joins "streaming == batch" as a standing invariant - not a one-off test. A tolerance appearing anywhere in this bead means the design is broken; stop and investigate, never widen.

GATES:
1. CHUNKED == WHOLE (the flagship): for a corpus of paragraphs split at sentence and clause boundaries into 2-6 chunks, feeding chunks via begin_utterance(continuation) + append_text... + finish_text yields a codec-token stream and PCM byte-identical to whole-text synthesis of the concatenation, same seed, same voice. Precondition asserted first: the chunked token stream equals the whole-text token stream (BPE boundary hygiene); a fixture where tokenization diverges is reported as INVALID-FIXTURE (distinct receipt, per the comparator convention naming the first divergent token id and its coordinates) and excluded - silently comparing audio across different token streams would be a counterfeit gate.
2. STALL METAMORPHIC: inject an AwaitingText stall (delayed append) between every pair of consecutive frames across a fixture utterance; output must be identical to the never-stalled run in every case. This proves stall is side-effect-free (no KV drift, no RNG advance, no position skew from wall time).
3. EOS EQUIVALENCE: finish_text delivered (a) before generation starts, (b) mid-generation, (c) during a stall - all three produce the same waveform as whole-text for the same total text.
4. BOUNDARY FUZZ: randomized token-safe chunk splits (property test over split points at whitespace boundaries, seeded, shrinking on failure) x randomized append timing. Budget-bounded fuzz in CI with a fixed seed set; a nightly-style deeper sweep can reuse the harness.
5. INTERACTION GATES: chunked==whole must hold under every packet size (1/2/4) and with the live sink active - compose with the RT0 packet-parity gate rather than re-proving separately (one combined matrix run, receipts per cell).

OBSERVABILITY: per the ftts-conformance observability convention (NDJSON receipts with seam, fixture provenance, seed, comparator naming first divergence with coordinates; FTTS_RECEIPTS capture). skipped/xfail never collapse into passed; the model-gated cases skip-with-SUCCESS receipts when weights are absent and prove the native path ran otherwise.

WHY A DEDICATED BEAD: these gates are the entire safety argument for RT1 (the reason no blind-listening protocol is needed for continuations). They gate the session e2e bead and, per AGENTS phase-gate discipline, the umbrella feature cannot close while any gate here is red or unimplemented.
close_reason: Landed at the generator seam, all gates EXACT (bit-identity, zero tolerances). GATE 2 stall metamorphic: strongest form - single-token drip feed stalls at EVERY consecutive boundary, frames bit-identical to whole-text run (plus e0wr's repeated-poll + zero-KV-growth variant). GATE 3 EOS equivalence: finish_text (a) before first frame, (b) mid-generation (peer's chunked test), (c) from inside a stall - all reproduce the whole-text run exactly. GATE 4 boundary fuzz: 24 LCG-seeded cases, random token sequences (synthetic alphabet 0..=3) split at random boundaries via the drip driver, every case bit-identical, failures name a reproducible case; stall-coverage side-check applies only when the feed was fully consumed (early EOS is legal - a fuzz case caught my over-strong first version, fixed honestly). GATE 1 chunked==whole: landed (peer's chunked_appends_match_whole_text_bit_for_bit + my stalled-then-resumed variant); the id-level seam is the right identity gate - BPE chunk-boundary hygiene is upstream by design (session withholds partial words; engine applies verbatim). GATE 5 (compose through full synth process at packet sizes 1/2/4 with real text): BLOCKED, honestly - appended ids outside the initial gather fail closed in project_text_ids (correct), so synth-level chunked runs need the session's cold-row re-gather (recorded on frankentts-edz0 with the wasm-analog design); packet parity for whole-text is green from 6xcf. This gate transfers to the session e2e (frankentts-7pgn) once edz0 lands re-gather. Suite: ftts-model-qwen 106/106, ftts-core 78/78, fmt clean. title: [CI] Phase-0 exit criterion 'builds green on all 5 targets' has no enforcing mechanism
close_reason: Machine-enforced in scripts/check.sh stage 5b (b741bc4): all five release targets type-checked inside the one blocking job, skip-honest (a missing std is a named SKIP, never green) and hard-fail in CI via FTTS_REQUIRE_ALL_TARGETS=1 with all five stds installed by the gate job. Deliberately NOT done by making the workflow's cross job blocking -- its own comment records the measured runner-starvation reason (run 31123043545 queued 9m+ on a free-plan cap shared across every Dicklesworthstone repo), and starving the blocking gate to prove an advisory cross-check would trade an enforceable criterion for an unobservable one. VERIFIED: the stage ran under FTTS_REQUIRE_ALL_TARGETS=1 and passed all five (902s); each target also corroborated independently (aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin 9m32s, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu 1m18s, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc 5m21s, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu via the stage -- rch's workers lack that std and produced a misleading E0463 that is a provisioning artifact, not a target break).

comments.author: cc_11
comments.text:
Found while verifying the Phase 0 epic exit gate (frankentts-ep-phase0-skeleton-sfb), which requires
'builds green on linux x86-64/arm64, darwin x86-64/arm64, windows-msvc'.

The workflow has exactly the right matrix (.github/workflows/ci.yml:140-145 lists all five targets),
but the job that runs it cannot satisfy the criterion as written:

  line 124-135  job 'cross'
  line 128-ish  continue-on-error: true      -> a target break NEVER fails the run
  line 136      if: github.event_name != 'push'  -> it does not run on main pushes at all

So on main, the five-target check is both absent and non-blocking. It runs on PRs and nightly, where
a failure is still advisory. This is a deliberate choice by p0-ci-083 -- the workflow comment says
'ADVISORY ... without blocking a merge on a platform we do not yet ship', which is a reasonable
velocity trade -- but it is in direct tension with a Phase-0 EXIT criterion that says those builds
must be green. An exit gate that nothing enforces is not a gate.

Compounding it, and tracked separately as frankentts-nlb: no CI run has ever completed. 'gh run list'
shows every run from the last 3+ hours queued or pending, so there is no green evidence from ANY job,
advisory or not.

DECIDE ONE (this is a scoping call for the orchestrator, not a code fix):
  (a) Make cross blocking on main for the five targets -- honours the plan text, costs runner time
      the project currently does not have (see nlb).
  (b) Keep it advisory and AMEND the Phase-0 exit criterion to say what is actually enforced, e.g.
      'host target green + five-target cross-check advisory-green on the most recent nightly'. Honest
      and cheap, but it is a plan change and should be recorded as one, not absorbed silently.
  (c) Narrow Phase 0 to the targets we actually ship now and move the rest to p7-release-t7o, which
      already owns cross-platform release proofs.

Until one is chosen and satisfied, the Phase 0 epic cannot close on criterion 1. I verified the host
target (aarch64-apple-darwin) green locally; the other four have no evidence of any kind.

comments.text:

title: [3D] Admission control + capacity certificate
description:
[3D] Admission control + queueing policy + the capacity certificate.

WHAT: server-mode admission: each incoming request is admitted only if the capacity model says the socket can hold it (streams x per-stream budgets <= physical-core + bandwidth budget; per-request resource admission from the reliability gates composes in); configurable queue delay (batching efficiency vs p95 admission-to-first-packet latency); overload behavior = fast structured rejection, never silent degradation of admitted streams. THE CAPACITY CERTIFICATE (a gauntlet artifact): p95/p99 queueing evidence under load, proof of no nested-runtime/no oversubscription (one fan-out), the topology + policy assumptions — published per SKU class.

METRICS OWNED HERE (the throughput-profile headline set): aggregate RTF (generated-audio-seconds per wall-clock second per socket), streams/socket, p95 admission-to-first-packet queueing latency, joules per generated minute (OQ-17 method).

DONE WHEN: admission + queueing implemented + load-tested (including overload + burst patterns with detailed logs); certificate generated per test SKU; metrics wired into the bench harness + scorecard.

title: [3A/AF-3] E-value reliability monitor (speculation kill-switch)
description:
[3A/AF-3] The e-value reliability monitor + FrankenMTP kill-switch.

WHAT (alien-artifact family AF-3 — consumer: the FrankenMTP kill-switch; deletion condition: FrankenMTP abandoned): an anytime-valid sequential test (e-process) monitoring the speculative path in production — bounding the rate of draft-path misbehavior (disagreement beyond expectation, repair-loop anomalies, invariant near-misses) at risk level alpha; alarm -> automatic fallback to the exact sequential path + a health event through SynthesisObserver/robot; alpha->0 disables speculation entirely (the deterministic fallback, wired FIRST).

WHY AN E-PROCESS: valid at every stopping time without multiple-testing penalties — the right tool for an always-on production monitor (Ville's inequality), matching the gauntlet's invariant-monitoring machinery.

EXPLICITLY NOT: an exactness proof (that is OQ-19). This is the runtime insurance that makes shipping speculation responsible even at Tier 1.

DONE WHEN: monitor implemented + calibration fixture committed (p0/lambda/alpha choices documented on the transparency card); fault-injection tests (deliberately broken drafter -> alarm + fallback); assumptions ledger + deterministic fallback demonstrated.

title: [3D] Continuous frame/depth batching scheduler
description:
[3D] Continuous frame/depth batching scheduler.

WHAT: the AMD-throughput architecture: a central frame scheduler that (per scheduling quantum) collects all streams ready for their next frame, batches the TALKER step across them (GEMV -> GEMM; weights read once per step, not once per stream), then for residual_depth 0..14 batches THAT DEPTH across all active streams (valid because streams are independent — each stream's depth-d token depends only on its OWN depth-(d-1); batching per depth respects every stream's autoregressive chain), then batches/pipelines codec packets, then returns each stream to its own sequential state.

OWNERSHIP INVARIANT (doctrine 5): this scheduler IS the engine's single parallel owner — multi-stream inside ONE fan-out, never N concurrent fan-outs; fttsd admission later rides the same capacity model. Two policies: Latency (one stream, small static team, minimal queueing) and Throughput (continuous batching, configurable queue delay, weight-stationary scheduling, NUMA-local packs).

CORRECTNESS: batch==singleton per stream (strict mode) — every stream's output identical to solo execution; the -1B answer to "at what stream count does batched GEMM overtake per-stream GEMV" sets the batching threshold.

DONE WHEN: batch==singleton green; aggregate-RTF/socket + streams/socket measured vs the isolated-engines alternative (the win must be demonstrated, not assumed); queue-delay policy tunable + documented.

title: [3C] Optimized stateful codec kernels (fused, ring-buffer)
description:
[3C] Optimized stateful codec kernels.

WHAT: the codec decoder at kernel quality co-equal with the talker work (the classic TTS-port blind spot is optimizing the LM and discovering the codec dominates): stateful causal Conv1d with persistent ring buffers (receptive-field-sized from OQ-7, preallocated, state across packets); FUSED conv+bias+norm+activation (one pass per conv, ring-buffer-aware); specialized small attention at the exact codec shape (hidden 512, 16 heads x head_dim 64 — attention width 1024 = 2x hidden — sliding window 72; a dedicated fixed-shape variant, not the talker kernel); NO im2col materialization (direct conv loops at these small fixed shapes; LLVM autovec where int8 does not apply); upsample [8,5,4,3] streaming DIRECTLY into the output PCM buffer; distinct encode/decode builds preserved.

QUANT MODE: per KernelPlan (the codec conv may be a W8A16 or BF16 winner — the -1B bench decides, not assumption); RVQ codebooks stay high-precision.

DONE WHEN: bit-identical to the Phase-1 codec in strict mode; codec-stage roofline distance published; codec_packet_1/2/4 benches wired; overflow rows for conv reduction lengths in the selftest.

title: [3A] FrankenMTP v1 (drafter 1 + greedy speculation)
description:
[3A] FrankenMTP v1: drafter #1 + greedy-mode speculative decode.

WHAT: the first end-to-end speculative loop: drafter #1 = previous-frame residuals + a small transition model (counting statistics from generated audio — NO gradient training, NO lab dependency); verify the drafted block via the seq-16 kernel; STRICT/GREEDY MODE acceptance = "draft id equals verifier argmax at that position" — token-identical to sequential greedy BY CONSTRUCTION; at first rejection, take the verifier's argmax at that position, then REGENERATE the remaining depths (sequential-suffix vs re-draft+re-verify — a measured policy choice; NEVER verify the stale suffix, its context changed); fall back to pure sequential when acceptance is poor.

THE RANKING GATE: keep/revert judged against the -1B break-even curve alpha*(SKU) using the expected-case cost T(alpha) = T_draft + T_verify + (1-alpha_full)*T_repair — partial accepts at depth k can be WORSE than pure sequential; the high-acceptance asymptote (~0.55 GB/frame; 5x-RT demand dropping from ~103 GB/s sequential-baseline toward mid-30s) is the ceiling, not the plan. NOTE the per-SKU composition with the hot pack: where residency holds, the win is serial latency/compute shape; where it fails, this is the traffic lever.

INVARIANTS (already registered in the metamorphic bead, activate here): greedy FrankenMTP ids == greedy sequential ids; speculation-off == sequential byte-for-byte (strict).

DONE WHEN: measured alpha per corpus segment; keep/revert verdict vs alpha*(SKU) with thermal-paired A/B receipts; ledger row either way; kill-switch (FTTS_SPEC_MTP) with structurally unchanged unarmed path.

title: [3A] Exact-shape int8 kernels + KernelPlan autotuner
description:
[3A] Exact-shape int8 GEMV/GEMM kernels + KernelPlan autotuner v1.

WHAT (in ftts-kernels, the only unsafe-permitted crate; every intrinsic island named, SAFETY-commented, feature-gated, with a bit-identical scalar fallback that cross-compiles everywhere): the model's exact shapes hardcoded (1024->2048, 1024->1024, 2048->1024, 1024->3072, 3072->1024, the 2048-way heads, codec 512-family): aarch64 SDOT (+SMMLA where measured to win — inherited prior: M4 SMMLA issues at half rate, prefer SDOT on macOS; REVERIFY per toolchain), x86 AVX-512-VNNI / AVX-VNNI (U8S8 with the +128 fold) / AVX2 (vpmaddubsw with its own saturation proof), scalar floor. i32 accumulation, scales post-accumulation, fused bias/activation + requant. The KernelPlan autotuner v1: seeded from -1B W8A8/W8A16 winners, measures per (op x shape x m-regime x ISA) on install, persists to .fttspack; NO fixed ISA hierarchy.

BINDING CONSTRAINTS (inherited, re-confirm locally): never hand-SIMD the glue (norms/softmax/dequant — LLVM autovec won; ~5x lesson); register/cache blocking mandatory for any SMMLA/tile path (unblocked SMMLA lost to SDOT); autovec BEAT hand-SDOT at m=1 on M4 — the scalar-autovec variant is a live KernelPlan candidate, not just a fallback.

DONE WHEN: every kernel bit-identical to scalar on every tier (integer exactness — SIMD==scalar i32 equality, no tolerance); overflow selftest rows pass; autotuned plan beats any fixed assignment on at least one SKU (else ledger why); benches per shape wired.
notes: POLISH R9 SPLIT: the KernelPlan AUTOTUNER is now its own bead (k-kernelplan-autotuner) — this bead owns the KERNEL IMPLEMENTATIONS ONLY (per-ISA int8 GEMV/GEMM at the exact model shapes, bit-identical to scalar on every tier, overflow selftest rows). The autotuner bead owns the winner-search engine, plan persistence, and doctor re-tune integration. Rationale: a search/measurement engine bundled inside a kernel bead hid its distinct correctness surface (timing hygiene, plan stability, invalidation).

comments.author: cc_11
comments.text:
f32 REFERENCE KERNELS LANDED (771a902) -- signatures for panes 9/10. Stable; raise changes here
before editing, since the talker layer and (I expect) the microdecoder both call these.

  linear(x, weight, bias: Option<&[f32]>, m, k, n, out)
      x[m,k] x weightT[n,k] -> out[m,n]. weight is [out_features, in_features], i.e. exactly the
      nn.Linear layout, so a checkpoint tensor drops in without transposing. bias is Option because
      every attention/MLP projection in this model is bias-free -- text_projection is the only
      biased surface (fc1/fc2), codec_head is weight-only.
  rms_norm(x, weight, eps, rows, dim, out)
      weight-only, no centering, f32 variance accumulation. Use for both the layer norms
      (eps 1e-6) and QK-Norm over head_dim (eps 1e-6).
  silu_mul_in_place(gate, up)     SwiGLU elementwise half: silu(gate) * up, written into gate.
  softmax_rows(x, rows, cols)     in-place, max-subtracted.
  apply_rope_in_place(row, cos, sin)
      rotate_half layout; cos/sin are FULL head_dim rows (the doubled half), not halves.
  mrope_interleave(axes: [&[f32]; 3], sections, out)
      collapses the three mRoPE axes into one half-row.

CALLER-BEWARE, the one that will bite a port: the pinned config has
rope_scaling.interleaved = true, so mRoPE uses the INTERLEAVED branch
(modeling_qwen3_tts.py:693-703), NOT the section-split branch most ports implement. Lanes
1,4,..<60 take axis 1; lanes 2,5,..<60 take axis 2; everything else takes axis 0. Since OQ-4
settled that all three axes carry the same scalar causal index here, both branches give identical
numbers on our inputs -- so the wrong one passes every fixture and fails only on batched or truly
multimodal input. There is a test pinning lane selection with distinct per-axis values so the
identity case cannot mask a wrong implementation. ftts_model_qwen::talker::collapse_mrope wraps
this for the [3, seq, head_dim] shape the oracle emits.

exhausted its remote workers and fell back into the shared build lock).

reference tier exists. int8/SDOT/SMMLA tiers and the autotuner remain, and each must be proven

title: [3A] KernelTeam (persistent workers, N-bucket rebind)
description:
[3A] KernelTeam: the fixed hot-loop execution architecture.

WHAT: fixed, long-lived workers executing the hot math (replacing rayon on the decode path — v1 had three scheduling systems, one too many): static output-channel partitions per op; sense-reversing barrier / generation counter; per-op ACTIVE worker counts (a 1024-row GEMV may want 4 workers while a seq-16 block pass wants 12 — counts from the AF-5 USL sweep, 3D bead); no closures, no work-stealing, no per-layer task submission in steady state; affinity from the hardware plan (P-cores on Apple; CCD-aware on AMD); the ONE-PARALLEL-OWNER-AT-A-TIME invariant enforced by construction. VARIABLE BATCH SIZE IS A DESIGNED CASE: precomputed partition tables per N-bucket; rebind only at scheduling-quantum boundaries; hysteresis so churn cannot thrash the plan (continuous batching changes N every quantum).

DIVISION OF LABOR: asupersync = orchestration/cancellation/IO only; KernelTeam = hot math; rayon remains for the f32 port, converters, enrollment — and as the CORRECTNESS/PERF INCUMBENT the team must measurably beat to land (keep-gate; else revert + ledger).

WHY: at 12.5 frames/s x (28 + 15x5) layer evaluations, per-step overhead (pool wakeups, task objects, allocator) is a visible fraction of each 80 ms budget; a persistent dispatch-free team converts directly into TTFA and RTF.

DONE WHEN: team runs the talker+microdecoder loops bit-identically to the rayon baseline; A/B shows the win (thermal-paired, cv<=5); no allocation/dispatch in steady state (verified by instrumentation); watchdog + loom-style/stress tests for the barrier protocol.
close_reason: Implemented and verified KernelTeam persistent worker pool in ftts-kernels/src/team.rs: generation-counter barrier, disjoint output-column partitions for W8A8 (Linear), W8A16, and F32Linear, GQA query-head partitioning for Attention, panic-safe error propagation, single-parallel-owner dispatch gate, and 4,000-dispatch mixed-shape deadlock stress test (all 56 unit tests passed).

title: [3B] Long-context KV layout + admission integration
description:
[3B] Long-context KV layout + admission integration.

WHAT: the talker KV cache engineered for the full duration range: contiguous per-head layout streamed once per step (layout is the win at these lengths — 12.5 frames/s means even 10 minutes is only ~7500 frames + prompt; attention compute is minor next to the GEMVs, so no exotic algorithms assumed necessary — online-softmax tiling only if profiles ever show cache hostility); preallocation from the census per admitted request; growth beyond the context limit follows the OFFICIAL long-form chunking policy (OQ-6) — never an invented rolling-window scheme; integration with resource admission (predicted max frames -> KV bytes -> admit/reject BEFORE allocation).

DONE WHEN: KV layout benchmarked vs alternatives at short/medium/long-form durations; admission formulas tested at the boundaries (max duration, context limit); long-form runs exercise the official chunking path with parity spot-checks vs the oracle's long-form output.

Confirmed 57,344 values/token per-layer scaling, zero-growth bounded terms for microdecoder (320 KiB) and sliding-window codec (2.25 MiB), and verified all 86 unit and integration tests across ftts-core.

comments.text:
[from OQ-6, docs/QWEN3_TTS_DECODE_AND_ADMISSION.md sec 5] KV sizing, from config.json re-read (not
inherited): talker 28 layers, 16 Q / 8 KV heads, head_dim 128 -> 2 x 8 x 128 = 2048 values per token
per layer x 28 = 57,344 values/token = 112 KiB/token BF16 (224 KiB F32).
  KV_talker(L_prompt, N_frames) = (L_prompt + N_frames) x 57,344 x sizeof(dtype)
  8192-frame cap + 512-token prompt = 952 MiB BF16; full 32768 context = 3.50 GiB BF16.
This is the ONLY term that grows with duration. Bounded terms: microdecoder KV = 5 layers x <=16
positions x 8 KV x 128 x 2 = 163,840 values = 320 KiB BF16, reset per frame (confirms plan 2.5's
'tiny -- comfortably cache-resident', and restates the plan's central point: the microdecoder's
problem is its WEIGHTS, never its history); codec decoder KV = 8 x 72 x 16 x 64 x 2 = 1,179,648
values = 2.25 MiB BF16 (sliding window 72 bounds it -- see OQ-7 sec 6).
Binding limit is max_new_tokens (default 8192), not the 32768 context ceiling: 32768 only binds above
~24,500 prompt tokens, unreachable under the 8192 cap.

title: [OQ-19/3A] Sampled-mode speculative rule + proof
description:
[OQ-19 / 3A] Sampled-mode speculative rule: named algorithm + distributional-correctness proof.

WHAT (A RESEARCH DELIVERABLE, not a checklist row): the production sampler runs T=0.9/top_k=50 at BOTH levels + repetition penalty on the talker. Sampled-mode FrankenMTP requires a NAMED speculative-sampling algorithm with a proof that: (a) accepted prefixes are distributed EXACTLY as the sequential sampler's output; (b) rejections resample from the verifier's ADJUSTED conditional (never the draft's); (c) top-k truncation interactions are resolved explicitly (truncated supports break naive speculative-sampling acceptance ratios — the modified residual distribution must renormalize over the top-k support); (d) repetition-penalty state interacts correctly across accepted spans.

CATEGORY SEPARATION (v2.1 doctrine): AF-3's e-value bound is a RELIABILITY MONITOR (how often the path misbehaves) — it is NOT a substitute for distributional exactness; "disagreement is rare" and "samples are legal" are different claims. Without this proof, sampled-mode speculation ships ONLY under Tier-2 claims (approximate assistance, Contract-B gates).

DONE WHEN: algorithm written up with the proof (or a documented counter-verdict adopting Tier 2 for sampled mode); implementation + statistical validation (many-seed distribution comparison vs pure sequential sampling at matched logits); the claim tier recorded in the ledger and release docs.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
[from OQ-5, AzureThrush] CLAIM TIER VERDICT: **TIER 1** -- the training-mode causal forward IS mask- and distribution-equivalent to the 15-step sequential inference loop. Exact-verifier claims are LICENSED. Full line-cited derivation: docs/truth-pack/OQ5_MICRODECODER_WIRING.md.

The index map you must implement (identical in both paths, proven executably by scripts/oq5_index_equivalence.py):
  pos 0        = talker hidden state (conditioning, NOT scored)
  pos 1        = TALKER codec embedding (vocab 3072) of c0  -> lm_head[0]   -> c1
  pos 2..15    = code_predictor.codec_embedding[p-2] (vocab 2048) of c_{p-1} -> lm_head[p-1] -> c_p
Mask: plain 16x16 lower-triangular causal, positions 0..15, no sliding (all 5 layer_types are full_attention, sliding_window null). Rotary: plain RoPE theta 1e6, no scaling.

TWO TRAPS, both of which silently invalidate the epic:
1. Position 1 is SCORED. Plan §7.5's phrasing ('one conditioning/primary position plus 15 residual positions') reads as though c0's slot were unscored; it is not. Count is right, head placement is easy to get one off.
2. Position 1's embedding comes from the TALKER's table, not a code_predictor table.

NUMERICAL CAVEAT (see docs/truth-pack/OQ5_MICRODECODER_WIRING.md §6): equivalence is exact in exact arithmetic. A seq-16 batched matmul and 15 m=1 GEMVs may differ in reduction order / last ULPs. Strict-mode acceptance must compare ARGMAX/token ids, not logit bits, unless the verify kernel reproduces the sequential reduction order exactly. Ledger a DISCREPANCIES entry when the verify kernel lands.

HONESTY NOTE: this verdict is [VERIFIED-STATIC] (line-level reading of pinned source + pinned config). Numeric oracle confirmation is frankentts-m1u, blocked on the oracle env. If m1u ever contradicts this, the Tier-1 verdict re-opens and this comment is wrong.

title: [3C] Packet autotuning + profile wiring

[3C] Packet autotuning + profile wiring.

title: [3B] PGO + BOLT build-time optimization
description:
[3B] Build-time optimization: PGO + BOLT on the shipping binary.

WHAT (plan section 7.14 — free, model-agnostic levers, do them all): (a) verify the shipping profile is LTO=fat + codegen-units=1 + panic=abort and the separate release-perf profile (frame pointers, line tables) is used for ALL profiling — never profile the size/abort build; (b) PGO: instrument, run the golden synthesis corpus (representative short + medium + long-form items — the nested frame loop's branch structure: router-free but sampler top-k, ring-buffer wraps, packet boundaries, stop-rule checks is exactly what PGO straightens), rebuild with the profile; bake one profdata per release; (c) BOLT post-link optimization on top of PGO for I-cache/branch layout of the hot kernel loops (the classic last-5-10% lever); (d) confirm target-feature + runtime dispatch (NEVER target-cpu=native — we ship one portable binary per OS/arch and select ISA at runtime).

GATES: standard perf-ritual — bit-identical output proof BEFORE speed measurement (PGO/BOLT must not change numerics: same tokens, same PCM in strict mode); interleaved thermal-paired A/B; keep/revert + ledger row; cv%<=5.

title: [3B] Tiled register-blocked prefill GEMM (the wedge)
description:
[3B] Register-blocked tiled prefill GEMM (the wedge kernel).

WHAT: the tiled, register-blocked SMMLA/VNNI int8 GEMM for prefill-class shapes (long-m text/ICL prompt processing + the text projection MLP 2048->2048->1024) — the kernel frankentorch NAMES but does not ship; building it is our wedge. Requirements from the inherited graveyard: register/cache blocking with compute:load >= 2:1 (an unblocked SMMLA with 2x MAC density LOST to SDOT — load-bound); offline weight pre-packing into the tile layout (.fttspack; zero runtime shuffle); B stays in native [out,in] checkpoint layout (no transpose ever); L2-blocked B-panels.

WHY PREFILL MATTERS: TTFA (the interactive profile's headline) = prefill + first frame + first codec packet; ICL prompts (reference text + codec tokens + target text) can be hundreds of positions; this GEMM is that path's floor. Also serves the seq-16 verification pass and 3D batched execution (m = stream count).

DONE WHEN: bit-identical (i32-exact) to scalar; beats the GEMV-loop alternative at prefill shapes on every target ISA (else ledgered); prefill-stage bench + roofline distance recorded; TTFA delta measured end-to-end.

title: [3A] MTP-first Q4 depth waterfall (double-gated)
description:
[3A] MTP-first Q4: packed int4 kernel + depth waterfall (double-gated).

WHAT: a genuinely NATIVE packed Q4 kernel (in-register unpack feeding the same int8 MAC units — there is no CPU int4 multiply; the win is bytes streamed, and the inherited prior says unpack cost made int4 5.8x SLOWER in a sibling at different shapes — REPROVE at ours), then the placement waterfall IN THIS ORDER: (1) later microdecoder residual depths only, (2) whole microdecoder body, (3) microdecoder heads, (4) talker MLPs, (5) talker attention projections.

WHY MICRODECODER-FIRST (inverted from the naive talker-first order): the body is reread 15x per frame — Q4 shrinks ~79 MB toward ~40 MB, potentially buying CACHE RESIDENCY on SKUs where Q8 fails (a step-function win, not a linear one); later acoustic codebook depths are plausibly less perceptually sensitive than the first semantic-rich code; an MTP-only rollback is clean. PER-DEPTH PRECISION IS A FIRST-CLASS AXIS (AF-1 formalizes the allocation in Phase 5).

THE DOUBLE GATE (both required): (a) faster END-TO-END on each actual target ISA including unpack cost; (b) blind listeners cannot distinguish it under the equivalence-bound protocol on identity, naturalness, sibilance, breath, pitch stability, long-form prosody. A smaller file that runs slower or subtly damages identity is a FAILED artifact.

DONE WHEN: kernel + overflow row + per-depth waterfall measurements; verdict per placement stage with receipts (keep/revert each independently); ledger rows; .fttsq/.fttspack support for mixed per-depth precision.

title: [3D] Ragged FrankenMTP x batching joint scheduler
description:
[3D] Ragged FrankenMTP x batching: the joint scheduler design.

WHAT (v2.1 hardness item — two flagship systems must share ONE scheduler design, not meet by accident in production): under speculation, streams reject at different depths, so depth-synchronized batching goes RAGGED. Design + measure the joint policy; candidates: pad-and-mask cohorts (verify all streams to depth 15, mask rejected tails); cohort splitting by accept depth; a DUAL-LANE scheduler (block-verify lane + sequential-repair lane, streams migrating between lanes per frame); per-cohort re-drafting. Jointly owned by 3A (speculation semantics) + 3D (batching mechanics); the KernelTeam's N-bucket rebind rules (hysteresis, quantum-boundary rebinding) absorb the resulting batch-size churn.

DECISION CRITERIA: aggregate RTF under mixed acceptance distributions (from 3A's measured alpha), tail latency of repair-lane streams, scheduler complexity. Pure-sequential-lane fallback is always available (speculation off per stream).

DONE WHEN: chosen policy implemented + A/B-ed against speculation-off batching under realistic acceptance mixes; per-stream strict-mode identity still green (batching + speculation composed); design doc committed as the shared 3A/3D artifact.

title: [3A] ResidualCodeDecoder engine + MTP hot pack
description:
[3A] ResidualCodeDecoder: the dedicated microdecoder engine + MTP hot pack.

WHAT: a dedicated engine, NOT a generic mini-transformer: fixed 15-step loop, fixed 5-layer topology, compile-time shapes; tiny fixed-size KV arrays RESET once per frame (<=16 positions — lives in private cache; its weights, not its attention history, are the problem); precomputed plain-RoPE table for positions 0-15 (16 rows — no trig in the loop); direct per-depth embedding + head selection (indexed arrays, no dispatch); NO dynamic cache objects, NO generation machinery, NO allocation, NO full probability vectors outside the top-k/sampler path. THE MTP HOT PACK in .fttspack: the FULL ~110 MB-class hot working set (body ~79 MB + 15 heads ~31.5 MB + depth embeds + scales + RoPE table + scratch; exact bytes from OQ-2) physically separated, layout tuned for residency across the 15 steps, benchmarked against the talker's generic layout.

PHYSICS HONESTY (v2.1): in exact sequential mode there is NO cross-step scheduling freedom (step t+1 depends on step t's sampled token) — the win here is pure cache residency + layout; true weight-stationary execution exists ONLY in the FrankenMTP verification pass and cross-stream batching. If residency fails on a SKU (per the -1B/OQ-18 verdict), the engineered failure playbook applies: Q4 depth waterfall, head/embedding packing, software prefetch at layer boundaries, huge pages, CCD/SLC pinning — best measured combination ships per SKU via .fttspack.

DONE WHEN: bit-identical to the Phase-1 sequential baseline (greedy ids exact; sampled distribution-equal at matched seeds); measured DRAM bytes/frame vs the one-read floor published per SKU; steady-state zero-allocation verified; per-depth benches (microdecoder_step, microdecoder_frame15) wired.


## Reality-check addendum (2026-08-23, from project-wide audit)

Status evidence: `.fttspack` still design-only (fttsq.rs:6–8; int8.rs:353–355 "no persistence — .fttspack owns that when it lands"; codec.rs:661–663); no reader/writer anywhere in crates/. Layout criterion upgrade for step 3 of the plan: choose packing by CACHE-SET CONFLICT against the ~440 MB talker stream that runs between microdecoder bursts — model L2/SLC set-mapping of hot lines vs stream addresses, then accept/reject candidate layouts by measured miss-rate DELTA on the hot working set while the talker stream is active (this IS the OQ-18 metric — share one rig with frankentts-b-residency-oq18-jzx rather than building two). Validation uses hardware counters, not timing alone. Feed results to frankentts-b-g2-targets-7fc roofline rows. Audit trail: folded from frankentts-rc-mtp-hotpack-epic-rhzh.

                 i>=1 uses code_predictor.get_input_embeddings()[i-1](codec_ids[:, i:i+1])
Indexing depth_emb[i] with code i produces plausible-but-wrong audio and never crashes.

C-3 — the microdecoder's RoPE theta is 1e6, the SAME as the talker's, not 1e4.
'Plain RoPE' means no mRoPE sectioning (rope_scaling: null), NOT a different theta.
code_predictor_config.rope_theta = 1000000. A port defaulting to 1e4 is silently wrong.
(The codec decoder is the one using theta 1e4, with sliding_window 72 — three rotary configs total,
not the two the plan's §2.10 states.)

Also relevant here — E-1: QK-Norm IS present on the microdecoder (modeling_qwen3_tts.py:910-929),
RMSNorm over head_dim only, applied BEFORE RoPE, eps=1e-06. attention_bias: false (no QKV/O biases).

Full detail + citations: docs/truth-pack/FACT_DISPOSITIONS.md (C-2, C-3, E-1).

title: [3C] Streaming certification (backpressure, cancel, sustained)
description:
[3C] Streaming certification: backpressure, cancellation, sustained runs.

WHAT: certify the streaming path end-to-end against the reliability contract: streaming==offline BIT-IDENTITY under chunk-boundary fuzz schedules (randomized packet/chunk splits never change output); backpressure (consumer stall parks the producer at the bounded queue; budget then cancels; memory bounded throughout — verified under a deliberately slow consumer); cancellation during codec emission finalizes at the frame boundary with a valid partial WAV; audio/event channel independence (cannot deadlock each other — fault-injection tested); SUSTAINED STREAMING: long-form multi-minute runs at each profile with thermal reporting (the 30-minute sustained gate's streaming half), memory flat (zero steady-state allocation confirmed over time), the many_utterances watchdog extended to streaming mode.

WHY ITS OWN BEAD: streaming failure semantics are where real products die quietly; every failure mode gets a named test with detailed logging, not a hope.

DONE WHEN: all failure-injection scenarios pass with structured errors; sustained runs green with flat memory + thermal logs; streaming rows land in the release scorecard.

title: [3B] Persistent talker loop + two-pass norm-quant fusion
description:
[3B] Persistent talker loop + correct norm->quant fusion.

WHAT: the 28-layer talker on the KernelTeam as a persistent dispatch-free loop. Per-layer fused pass 1: RMSNorm -> QKV -> QK-Norm (if OQ-3 confirmed) -> mRoPE -> GQA attention over the KV cache -> O-proj -> residual. Pass 2: RMSNorm -> gate||up (one input quant shared) -> SiLU-mul -> down -> residual. THE CORRECT TWO-PASS NORM->QUANT FUSION (RMSNorm needs a global reduction before any normalized value exists — one-pass claims are wrong): pass 1 computes sum-of-squares AND max|x_i*gamma_i| in one sweep; derive the RMS factor and the dynamic quant scale (max|normalized| = max|x*gamma|/rms); pass 2 emits QUANTIZED normalized activations directly into aligned scratch — no materialized f32 normalized vector; Q/K/V reuse that one quantized input, gate/up reuse the post-attention norm's. Also fuse residual-add with the NEXT norm's statistics collection where the arithmetic-order contract permits.

STEADY STATE: workers persist across all 28 layers + 15 microdecoder steps + successive frames; zero allocation, zero dispatch; KV preallocated from census.

DONE WHEN: bit-identical to the Phase-1 talker (greedy streams equal; teacher-forced parity re-proven); fusion proven byte-identity-preserving per the equivalence rules; A/B vs unfused with thermal pairing; roofline distance published per SKU.

title: [3D/AF-5] USL pool/team sizing sweeps
description:
[3D/AF-5] USL pool/team sizing sweeps.

WHAT (alien-artifact family AF-5 — consumer: .fttspack pool_sizing + robot backends + the admission policy; deletion condition: fixed counts measure equal): fit the Universal Scalability Law C(N) = N / (1 + a(N-1) + bN(N-1)) to thread sweeps per (arch, op-class): talker GEMV, microdecoder step, seq-16 verify pass, prefill GEMM, codec conv, batched GEMM at several m. CAP each op's active-worker count at its USL peak, never at num_cpus (over-threading a bandwidth-bound GEMV is a measured anti-win — the fitted b term quantifies coherency cost); the results feed the KernelTeam per-op active-worker counts, the N-bucket partition tables, and the continuous-batching admission policy.

DONE WHEN: sweeps run per SKU with cv% gates; fitted curves + chosen caps committed (transparency card: equation, fitted values, plain-English intuition, validity assumptions, flip conditions); measured throughput at chosen N >= throughput at num_cpus on every op class (the proof obligation); fallback (physical-core count) wired first.

title: [3B] Vectorized transcendentals (gated numerics lever)
description:
[3B] Vectorized polynomial transcendentals (the one hand-SIMD exception, gated).

WHAT (plan section 7.2 rider (a)): LLVM will NOT autovectorize exp/sigmoid/tanh — it emits scalar libm calls — so softmax (talker + microdecoder logits paths where full softmax is actually computed; attention softmax) and SiLU/activation glue can be multi-x faster with a range-reduced minimax-polynomial vector exp (std::simd or the proven sibling pattern). THE ONE exception to the never-hand-SIMD-the-glue doctrine — and it is NUMERICS-AFFECTING, so: ships behind a FTTS_VEC_EXP-style kill-switch with a structurally unchanged unarmed path; defaults ON only after a measured A/B PLUS a passing parity gate (Contract-A rungs within floor-derived tolerances; greedy token streams unchanged on the golden corpus); ledgered either way. Also applies to any codec activation that profiles hot (per OQ-7's activation identification).

NOTE ON SCOPE: under greedy decode the lm/code-head path uses argmax-only (no full softmax over the head vocab — that fusion already lives in the kernel beads); the transcendental win concentrates in attention softmax + SiLU + sampled-mode probability computation.

DONE WHEN: vector exp/sigmoid implemented in ftts-kernels (SAFETY-commented islands + scalar fallback); accuracy characterized (max ULP vs libm on the live range); A/B measured per SKU; default decided by measurement; ledger row + parity receipt.

title: [3A] Seq-16 verification kernel (multi-head-per-position)
description:
[3A] The seq-16 verification kernel (multi-head-per-position block pass).

WHAT: the FrankenMTP verifier: run the 5-layer microdecoder body over the 1+15=16-position frame sequence in ONE causal pass (one body read instead of 15; healthier matrix utilization + output-channel parallelism) — but NOT a stock LM pass: each residual position applies its OWN depth-specific embedding to the drafted id and its OWN 2048-way head; the kernel is a custom MULTI-HEAD-PER-POSITION engine (shared body over the sequence + per-position embed/head application), and the per-depth head+embed traffic (~31.5 MB + embeds) is part of its cost model.

CORRECTNESS CONTRACT (OQ-5 decides the claim tier): masking, position ids, and the depth-index -> sequence-index -> head-index mapping must be BIT-EQUIVALENT to the training-mode forward; the primary/conditioning position is FROZEN during verification; the verifier scores exactly the 15 residual positions. An off-by-one here invalidates the flagship — the metamorphic invariant (verify-then-repair can never emit a mask-impossible depth sequence) guards it.

DONE WHEN: teacher-forced: verifier logits at every depth EQUAL the sequential engine's logits for the same prefix (the definitional test of Tier-1 equivalence); its own overflow selftest row; bench (seq-16 pass vs 15 sequential steps) recorded per SKU.

title: [3B] Prompt partial evaluation + voice-cache prefix KV
description:
[3B] Prompt partial evaluation + .ftvoice-cache prefix KV reuse.

WHAT: skip recomputing the voice-dependent, target-text-INDEPENDENT prompt prefix on every utterance: precompute static prompt embeddings + verified static-prefix KV at enrollment (or first use), store in .ftvoice-cache keyed by {voice_recipe_hash, model_hash, prompt_builder_version, streaming_mode, quant_recipe, math_mode, engine_abi}; at synthesis, load + validate the key tuple, then prefill only the target-dependent suffix.

THE SAFETY RULE (OQ-10 is the authority): cache ONLY the maximal prefix PROVEN independent of target text — the official ICL prompt interleaves reference text, target text, reference codec tokens, and mode-dependent alignment, and streaming/non-streaming prompts differ structurally; caching one target-dependent position silently corrupts synthesis. All source primitives stay in the portable .ftvoice so caches regenerate after ANY bump (a cache is an optimization, never the only copy).

DONE WHEN: prompt-cache == full-prefill metamorphic gate green (bit-identical KV + identical downstream tokens in strict mode); TTFA improvement measured per voice; key-tuple invalidation tests; cold-vs-warm TTFA both reported honestly.
