comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
[from OQ-10, AzureThrush] PREFIX VERDICT — the cacheable prefix is much smaller than 'cache the voice prompt' implies. Full proof + line citations: docs/truth-pack/OQ10_ICL_PROMPT_STRUCTURE.md §5. Executable model: scripts/oq10_prompt_shapes.py.

Maximal target-text-INDEPENDENT prefix, by mode (H = fixed header, 7 or 9 positions; T2 = 1 + ref_frames):
  ICL x streaming      : H + min(T2, |ref_id|)   -- includes codec_bos + the first min(T2,|ref_id|)-1 REFERENCE CODEC FRAMES
  ICL x non-streaming  : H + |ref_id|            -- ZERO reference codec frames are cacheable
  x-vector x either    : H                       -- header only, 7-9 positions

WHY the ref codec frames mostly fall outside: in streaming mode the codec stream is summed ELEMENTWISE with the text stream, so any position past |ref_id| carries target text; in non-streaming mode the codec block is CONCATENATED AFTER the target text, so under the causal mask its KV depends on the target text.

ACTIONS FOR THIS BEAD:
1. Do NOT ship a prefix-KV section for x-vector modes -- 7-9 positions is not worth the format surface. The reusable x-vector artifact is the speaker embedding, not KV.
2. Cache key MUST include (language_id, speaker_embed, ref_id token ids, ref_code, non_streaming_mode) on top of plan §6.7's tuple. language_id and speaker_embed live INSIDE the header H (modeling_qwen3_tts.py:2136-2172), so they invalidate even the header -- easy to miss because they read like runtime options.
3. Free two-level win: H is built identically in all four modes (M:2126-2186 precedes every branch), so header KV is shareable across streaming modes for a given (language, speaker). Only the ICL block needs a per-mode entry.
4. Representative sizes from scripts/oq10_prompt_shapes.py: 3s ref / 12-token ref text / 40-token target -> ICL streaming caches 21 of 48 prompt positions (44%); ICL non-streaming caches 21 of 101 (21%). Bound your expected TTFA win by these, not by the whole prompt.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
[from OQ-8, AzureThrush] Two codec behaviours found while tracing the audio output path for the watermark question. Neither is in the plan; both affect codec parity. Detail: docs/truth-pack/OQ8_WATERMARKING.md §3.

1. REFERENCE FRAMES ARE PREPENDED BEFORE DECODE, THEN CUT FROM THE AUDIO (inference/qwen3_tts_model.py:613-631):
     codes_for_decode = cat([ref_code, generated_codes])
     wav = speech_tokenizer.decode(codes_for_decode)
     cut = int(ref_len / total_len * wav.shape[0]);  return wav[cut:]
   In ICL mode the reference's own codec frames are decoded TOGETHER with the generated frames and the audio prefix is discarded. The reference audio is never returned but it IS computed -- it primes the causal decoder's ring-buffer state so generated speech starts with a warmed receptive field instead of zeros.
   => Decoding only the generated codes is NOT equivalent; the onset will differ. Our engine must either replay the reference decode and discard, or precompute the primed ring-buffer state into .ftvoice-cache (better -- removes ref decode from the TTFA path). Either way it must be PROVEN equivalent, not assumed. Also: the streaming==batch gate must fix this warm-up convention on both sides or it fails for unrelated reasons. TTFA cost if done naively: an extra ref_frames of codec decode (~38 for a 3s reference).

2. THE CUT IS A FLOAT RATIO, NOT A FRAME COUNT. Since decode() trims to exactly n_frames * decode_upsample_rate (tokenizer_12hz/modeling_qwen3_tts_tokenizer_v2.py:1013,1018), the cut is algebraically ref_len * upsample_rate, but it is implemented as float multiply-and-truncate. Port it as exact integer ref_len * upsample_rate and record the equivalence -- otherwise it is a one-sample offset that is miserable to debug in a parity test.

Also confirmed for codec parity: decode() is RVQ lookup -> decoder.chunked_decode -> length trim, and NOTHING else. No postprocessing stage exists, so any systematic waveform difference we see is our bug, not an unported stage.

comments.author: CyanStork
comments.text: Scope split 2026-08-22 (CyanStork) after code+byte-level investigation. FINDINGS: (1) The 'codec f32 ~1.36 GB' residency premise is stale — speech_tokenizer/model.safetensors is NATIVELY F32 and CodecCheckpoint holds exactly 457292548 B (the 1.3/1.36 numbers in IOS_APP_PLAN.md:141 and ftts-wasm lib.rs:312 assume a bf16->f32 doubling that never happens). Recorded as NE-009. (4) The browser ALREADY stages decoder-only tensors (engine-worker planCodecDecoderOnly); the real shippable win is fetching only the decoder PREFIX (-225 MB download, bit-exact). title: infra: shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR evicts artifacts across concurrent workspace checkouts
description:
OBSERVED TWICE 2026-08-22 during an isolated HEAD-worktree gate run (sc2 criterion-4 attempt): the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR (/Volumes/USB_NVME/cargo-target via ~/.zshenv) receives same-package-version/different-source builds from multiple concurrent checkouts of THIS repo (main tree with live agent edits vs any detached worktree). Cargo treats them as the same package ID, so each workspace's invocation invalidates and rebuilds the other's rlibs mid-flight. Symptom 1: rustdoc doctest died with E0463 can't-find-crate for serde_json/ftts_kernels even though --extern pointed at the (just-evicted) rlib paths - ftts-artifacts Doc-tests FAIL spuriously. Symptom 2: cargo test reruns recompile unchanged deps (thiserror et al) indefinitely while both trees alternate. Gates cannot reach ALL GREEN from any second checkout while the main tree is being built - sc2's criterion 4 is blocked by this, not by code.

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS (decide at implementation): (a) per-checkout target subdir keyed by git common dir + worktree name, exported from ~/.zshenv only when inside a linked worktree; (b) check.sh exports a worktree-scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR automatically when git-dir contains worktrees/; (c) document single-checkout policy for gate runs. (a)/(b) keep the shared fast path for the main checkout.
close_reason: Fixed via per-worktree CARGO_TARGET_DIR isolation in ~/.zshenv (option a): inside a linked worktree, CARGO_TARGET_DIR now resolves to /Volumes/USB_NVME/cargo-target-worktrees/<repo>-<worktree-name>; the main checkout keeps the shared fast path. Guarded exactly like the existing logic: only-when-unset (nested shells never clobber an ancestor's choice), NVMe-mounted-gated, fail-open to the shared default when git context is absent. Verified across all three cases in fresh clean-env shells (2026-08-22): main->shared, wt-gate->isolated, no-git->shared default. This unblocked isolated HEAD gate runs entirely: three full ./scripts/check.sh executions from /Users/jemanuel/projects/frankentts-wt-gate ran against the isolated target dir with zero artifact eviction of the main tree (runs 7-9, logs /tmp/ftts-check-sc2-run{7,8,9}.log) — previously impossible per this bead's symptom 2. title: [OQ-5b] Numeric oracle trace of one microdecoder frame (per-depth inputs/outputs)
design:
Numeric confirmation of the OQ-5 Tier-1 verdict, which was settled STATICALLY (line-level reading of the pinned source) in docs/truth-pack/OQ5_MICRODECODER_WIRING.md.

WHAT: with the oracle stood up, capture a real single-frame trace of the microdecoder: for each of the 16 sequence positions, the input vector provenance, the hidden state, and the 15 head logits. Then run the SAME frame through both code paths -- Qwen3TTSTalkerCodePredictorModelForConditionalGeneration.forward_finetune (one causal pass over 16 positions) and the 15-step code_predictor.generate loop -- and assert the logits agree at every scored position within the oracle's own nondeterminism floor.

WHY SEPARATE: OQ-5's exit criteria required an oracle-captured trace. No oracle exists yet (no torch, no weights on the host), so that criterion could not be met. title: [RT-later] C ABI streaming: chunk callback + cancel for iOS
description:
C ABI streaming for iOS: chunk callback, cancel handle, and progress - so the phone app can play audio as it synthesizes and abort on user action.

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS (scope honesty): the realtime epic (frankentts-3buc) targets the on-machine agent conversation loop and does NOT gate on iOS. But the 2026-08-21 investigation established that the C ABI cannot stream AT ALL - ftts_synthesize (crates/ftts-ffi/src/lib.rs:247, header include/ftts_ffi.h:44) is whole-utterance blocking, returns one leaked f32 buffer, has no callback, no cancel, no observer bridge (the observer is a no-op closure at ffi/src/lib.rs:289), and the Swift side consumes it exactly that way (ios/Sources/Engine.swift:64-77, one blocking call -> [Float]). Filing this now prevents the capability from being silently dropped; it is BACKLOG priority until the iOS app needs it.

WHAT TO BUILD (inherits RT0's semantics wholesale - do not redesign):
- ftts_synthesize_streaming(engine, text, speaker, speaker_len, seed, packet_frames, on_packet: extern fn(ctx, const float* samples, size_t len, uint64_t frame_index) -> int32_t, ctx) - the callback returns nonzero to request cancellation (pull-style cancel folded into the push callback: simplest possible ABI, no separate handle object to misuse across threads). Packets are the RT0 sink's packets. SAMPLE FORMAT IS f32, deliberately: the engine's native output is f32, the existing ftts_synthesize returns f32, and the actual consumer - AVAudioEngine on iOS - plays Float32 PCM buffers natively, so f32 is zero-copy end to end; s16 would force a pointless f32->s16->f32 round trip on the phone. (s16 is the CLI raw-stdout contract for pipe consumers; it is NOT the right ABI here - different consumers, different formats, each chosen for its reader.)
- Optionally a separate ftts_cancel(engine) for out-of-band cancel from another thread IF the Swift audio-session model needs it - decide against the actual AVAudioEngine integration, not speculatively; the callback-return channel may suffice.
- Error/progress surfacing: reuse ftts_last_error_message; a cancelled synthesis returns a distinct status code (mirror the CLI's exit-code-6 semantics).
- SAFETY NOTES REQUIRED: callback runs on the codec-worker thread - document reentrancy and threading rules in the header (the header IS the contract for Swift); the engine handle remains externally serialized (existing rule at ffi/src/lib.rs:244).

DEPENDS ON: the RT0 core sink seam (the callback is just a C-shaped sink). The continuation API could later be exposed the same way (ftts_append_text) for on-phone conversational use - out of scope here, note only.

TESTS (unit tests per the ftts-conformance observability convention): C-level harness test (call from a small C or Rust-as-C test) asserting packet concatenation == whole-buffer result bit-identically at the same seed; cancel-via-callback-return stops within one packet and returns the cancelled status; callback panic/exception safety (a misbehaving callback must not unwind across the FFI boundary - catch and convert). iOS-side smoke (streamed playback + mid-utterance cancel on device) belongs to the ios/ project's own checklist, referenced from docs/IOS_APP_PLAN.md when this lands.
close_reason: Landed and proven vs the real model (commits 6726e7b + cleanup). ABI: ftts_synthesize_streaming(engine, text, speaker, speaker_len, seed, packet_frames, on_packet, ctx) in include/ftts_ffi.h + ftts-ffi. DESIGN AS SPECIFIED: f32 samples end to end (engine-native + AVAudioEngine Float32-native; the bead's earlier s16 idea was corrected at review - s16 is the CLI pipe contract, a different reader); callback runs ON THE DECODE THREAD (header states the obligation; audited unsafe impl Send carries it); packet_frames caller-chosen (1 = lowest first-audio latency); frame_index = cumulative delivered frames before the packet; nonzero callback return folds cancellation into the push path (token -> engine frame checkpoint -> FTTS_SYNTH_CANCELLED=6, mirroring CLI exit-code semantics; no separate cancel handle to misuse - the out-of-band ftts_cancel idea stays deliberately unbuilt until AVAudioEngine integration demands it, per the bead). EVIDENCE (release, real model): streamed 1-frame packets bit-identical to ftts_synthesize whole buffer (52 packets / 99,840 samples, zero divergence), frame_index exact, cancel-after-3 stops at 4 packets with status 6; ffi debug suite 6/6 skip-honest shape intact; clippy/fmt clean. HONEST SCOPE NOTES: callback-panic case untested by design (C cannot unwind; guarded() covers the Rust side); on-device iOS smoke belongs to ios/'s own checklist per the bead; ftts_append_text streaming-continuation FFI remains future scope, noted not built.

title: [OQ-12] Canonical conformance decoder + L5 fork decision
description:
[OQ-12] Define the canonical conformance decoder + production sampler contract (a DESIGN DECISION, not fact-finding — the defaults are known).

KNOWN [SOURCE]: talker samples at T=0.9/top_k=50/top_p=1.0/repetition_penalty=1.05; residual predictor at T=0.9/top_k=50/top_p=1.0. The reference SAMPLES AT BOTH LEVELS — which is why one conformance ladder cannot serve two masters (Contract A/B split).

DECIDE: (a) the canonical conformance decoder = greedy/argmax at both levels — IS GREEDY AUDIO QUALITY-VIABLE? Run it and listen. (b) The pre-committed L5 fork: if greedy audio is viable, L5 = perceptual goldens + metrics over greedy audio; if NOT, L5 = exactness over codec-fixed audio (decode of frozen token streams) and the perceptual duty transfers wholly to Contract B. Agents never invent tolerances to bridge the branches. (c) The production sampler contract: our own seeded RNG (documented DISC — we replicate the distribution contract, never torch's RNG stream), repetition-penalty semantics ported exactly.

DONE WHEN: fork resolved with listening evidence; canonical decoder implemented in the fixture generator; sampler contract documented in the spec; the DISC entry for RNG divergence filed.
notes:
AzureThrush 2026-08-06: PARTIAL. (c) production sampler contract RESOLVED + canonical conformance decoder DEFINED -> docs/truth-pack/OQ12_SAMPLER_CONTRACT.md; propagated to p1-sampler-f1e, oq6, oq2, oq15. Key result: canonical greedy is NOT bare argmax -- logits PROCESSORS (rep_penalty 1.05, min_new_tokens 2, suppress_tokens) always apply even at do_sample=False; only WARPERS are gated. And argmax is warper-invariant, so the canonical decoder is fully defined TODAY without resolving the greedy-audio fork.

NOT RESOLVED: (a) is greedy audio quality-viable -- requires generated audio + listening panel; no torch and no weights on this host. (b) the L5 fork is strictly downstream of (a). DELIBERATELY NOT FILED: the DISC-NNN for RNG divergence -- docs/DISCREPANCIES.md's schema requires measured_impact and explicitly forbids unmeasured records; obligation carried by p1-sampler-f1e. Bead exit criteria and the ledger contract conflict here; ledger wins.

RECOMMENDATION TO ORCHESTRATOR: split (a)+(b) into an oracle-blocked follow-up (as OQ-5 -> m1u) and close this on the sampler contract, which is what p1-sampler-f1e / v-prod-harness-t96 / t-executable-spec-1ch actually consume. Not self-approved.
close_reason: Definition half resolved into docs/CANONICAL_DECODER_AND_SAMPLER.md; oracle-gated half carried by frankentts-ri0 [OQ-12b] with a predeclared selection criterion, both L5 branches pre-committed, and an auto-reopen condition on this bead if the verdict contradicts the definition. Canonical decoder defined as argmax at both levels with the reference's non-warper processors applied (talker: rep penalty 1.05 + min_new_tokens=2 EOS mask + suppress_tokens; microdecoder: raw argmax, fixed 15 steps) and no RNG. Production sampler contract fully specified: per-level order (the two levels have DIFFERENT stacks), sign-dependent repetition penalty over the group-0 history only, our-RNG distribution-contract scoping. Two findings with reach: suppress_tokens masks 2048-3071 except EOS so the talker's support is exactly {0..2047} u {2150} (independently confirming OQ-7's identity ID map), and the whole sampler contract is defined by pinned transformers 4.57.3 since Qwen ships no custom logits processors. p1-sampler-f1e fully unblocked. Picked up per orchestrator final call after ~3h idle under a non-responsive holder.

comments.author: cc_11
comments.text:
[RESOLVED on the definition half -> docs/CANONICAL_DECODER_AND_SAMPLER.md]

Picked this up per FuchsiaMouse's final call: it had sat ~3h with zero commits and AzureThrush shows
no commits in the recent window. Reassigned to cc_11 rather than leaving it held silently.

(a) CANONICAL CONFORMANCE DECODER = argmax at BOTH levels with the reference's NON-WARPER logits
processors still applied, and no RNG. Talker: argmax after repetition penalty 1.05, min_new_tokens=2
EOS masking, and the suppress_tokens mask. Microdecoder: argmax over raw per-depth head logits (the
reference passes it no penalty, no mask, no eos). Warpers are excluded on purpose -- temperature is a
monotone positive scale and top-k/top-p are truncations, so none can change an argmax; including them
would be harmless but would misrepresent the contract. Non-warper processors are included because
they change WHICH TOKEN WINS.

KEY FINDING: the two levels have DIFFERENT processor stacks (talker gets rep penalty + suppress +
eos + min_new_tokens; microdecoder gets none of them). That is the mechanical reason one ladder
cannot serve two masters.

KEY FINDING: suppress_tokens masks ids 2048..3071 except EOS 2150 (modeling:2059-2063), so the

title: [OQ-14] Official streaming internals (first packet, flush, packets)
description:
[OQ-14] Official streaming internals: first-packet path, flush behavior, prompt differences.

QUESTION: how does the official streaming mode actually work — first-packet latency path, packet assembly (the measured system groups 4 frames into 320 ms packets to avoid scheduling overhead), flush/finalization behavior at utterance end, and the structural prompt differences vs non-streaming (overlaps OQ-10; this bead owns the RUNTIME semantics)?

WHY: G8 makes packet size an execution-policy parameter (1/2/4/auto) — but our packet policies must be able to reproduce the official behavior exactly in strict mode (conformance packetization), and TTFA benchmarking must compare like-for-like first-packet paths. Flush semantics also decide the partial-WAV finalization contract in the streaming-failure gates.

DONE WHEN: streaming runtime semantics documented with line citations; strict-mode packetization defined; TTFA measurement protocol pinned to the official first-packet path.
close_reason: Resolved into docs/QWEN3_TTS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md. Headline: the released code has NO streaming generation -- upstream states verbatim (inference:514-515) that non_streaming_mode only simulates streaming TEXT INPUT; there is no packet assembly, no first-packet path, no flush. The 4-frame/320ms packetization and the 97ms first-packet latency are PAPER claims about an internal serving system that was not open-sourced, so the bead's 'reproduce official packetization exactly' criterion is unsatisfiable as written -- strict mode is DEFINED from the paper (4 frames / 7680 samples) and validated against streaming==batch instead. Documented both prompt geometries per clone path with line citations, plus the entrypoint-default trap (voice clone defaults to streaming-simulated, the other two do not). TTFA baseline pinned to our exact row (12Hz-0.6B: 93+4=97ms, LM TPP 19ms, RTF 0.288) with NO ADMISSIBLE RATIO recorded -- the paper names no hardware. Findings propagated to 3 dependent beads; plan 2.7 retag [SOURCE]->[SOURCE, paper] filed.

comments.author: cc_11
comments.text:
[OQ-14 RESOLVED -> docs/QWEN3_TTS_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md]

1. THERE IS NO STREAMING GENERATION IN THE RELEASED CODE. Upstream says so itself, verbatim at
   inference/qwen3_tts_model.py:514-515 (repeated at 656-657, 754-755): 'this option currently only
   simulates streaming text INPUT when set to false, rather than enabling true streaming input or
   streaming generation.' Confirmed by search: no generator/iterator/callback, no packet assembly, no
   flush/finalization, no incremental codec invocation. Generation runs to completion and the codec
   then decodes everything in one chunked_decode call.
   => The bead's acceptance criterion 'reproduce the official packetization exactly in strict mode'
   is UNSATISFIABLE as written -- there is no released packetization to reproduce. Strict mode must
   be DEFINED from the paper and validated against the streaming==batch invariant instead. Recorded,
   not papered over.

2. PLAN CORRECTION: 2.7's '4 frames / 320 ms packet' is a PAPER claim describing an internal serving
   system that was not open-sourced. Retag [SOURCE] -> [SOURCE, paper].

3. non_streaming_mode is a PROMPT-CONSTRUCTION switch only, with two distinct geometries per clone
   path (ICL: modeling:2002-2019; x-vector: modeling:2203-2232). True -> all text in prefill,
   trailing_text_hidden = tts_pad (pad fallback from frame 0). False -> text summed position-wise
   with codec over the overlap and the remainder metered in at ONE HIDDEN PER FRAME (12.5 tokens/s).
   Sharp edge: if text is longer than the frames generated, the TAIL OF THE TEXT IS NEVER SEEN.
   TRAP: the default differs by entrypoint -- voice clone defaults to non_streaming_mode=FALSE
   (inference:478), i.e. streaming-simulated is the default on the cloning path we care most about,
   while voice design and custom voice default to True (642, 738). Any A/B not holding this constant
   compares two different prompt geometries and is invalid. Prefill cost differs by orders of
   magnitude, so TTFA is only comparable within a mode.

4. TTFA BASELINE PINNED (paper sec 4 efficiency table, our exact row): Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B at
   concurrency 1 = LM TTFP 93 ms + tokenizer decode 4 ms = First-Packet Latency 97 ms; LM TPP 19 ms;
   RTF 0.288. The famous '97 ms' IS our model (the 25Hz variants are 138-150 ms) -- worth pinning
   since the 25Hz rows sit directly above it in the same table.
   BUT: NO ADMISSIBLE RATIO against it. The paper measured 'on our internal vLLM engine (vLLM V0
   backend) on a single typical computational resource' -- NO HARDWARE IS NAMED. Per plan 10.6 and
   the claim taxonomy, any 'we beat/approach 97 ms' claim is inadmissible. It is usable only as a
   documented upstream claim and as evidence that the codec's share of first-packet latency is small
   (4 of 97 ms), consistent with OQ-7's finding that codec streaming state is only a few MB.

5. Strict-mode packetization DEFINED: 1 packet = 4 frames = 320 ms = 7680 samples @ 24 kHz. Validated
   by streaming==batch, not by imitation. Note our streaming is bit-identical to our offline in BOTH
   regimes, but diverges from the official chunked_decode beyond 300 frames (that is OQ-7's DISC row,
   not a regression). Flush semantics are OURS by necessity -- tied to the EOS rule and the
   truncation-reporting requirement from OQ-6.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: [from OQ-8, AzureThrush] Relevant to first-packet/TTFA: in ICL mode the official path PREPENDS the reference codec frames to the generated codes, decodes them together, and cuts the reference audio off afterwards (inference/qwen3_tts_model.py:613-631). So the reference decode is on the naive first-audio path (~38 frames for a 3s ref) and it primes the causal decoder's ring buffer -- decoding generated codes alone is not equivalent. Caching the primed state is the fix. See docs/truth-pack/OQ8_WATERMARKING.md §3.1.

title: [OQ-6] Context limit / long-form chunking / stop semantics
description:
[OQ-6] Context limit, long-form chunking policy, EOS/stop semantics, max-duration behavior.

QUESTION: what is the talker's context limit? How does the OFFICIAL stack handle text longer than one pass (chunking? sentence splitting? context carryover?)? Exact stop conditions (EOS token(s)? max frames? silence?) and max-duration behavior?

WHY: (a) the decode loop's stop rules must be ported exactly, never invented (an invented rolling-window scheme would silently change semantics); (b) resource admission (reject before partial allocation) computes predicted max frames + KV allocation from these facts; (c) the long-form drift gate (the paper reports the 25Hz variant beat 12Hz on long-speech — long-form is a distinct quality regime with its own gate and a predefined dual-rate trigger) needs the official long-form path as its baseline.

DONE WHEN: line-cited policy in the spec; admission formulas derived; long-form corpus items designed to exercise the chunking boundary.
close_reason: Resolved into docs/QWEN3_TTS_DECODE_AND_ADMISSION.md. Headline: the official stack has NO long-form chunking / sentence splitting / context carryover at all -- so there is nothing to port and any scheme we add is our own divergence needing a DISC + drift-gate A/B. Resolved cc_1's three-way max_new_tokens conflict: runtime default is 8192 (generation_config.json via generate_defaults precedence); README's 2048 was an eval-time override; 4096 is unreachable; the wrapper's 2048 hard default is dead code. Stop rule verified (group 0 only, id 2150, EOS frame EXCLUDED, residual loop never early-stops). Max-duration behavior is SILENT truncation -> first-class reporting requirement filed on v-reliability-d65. Admission formulas derived (KV_talker = (L+N) x 57,344 x dtype; bounded terms 320 KiB + 2.25 MiB). Long-form corpus designed around 4 independent boundaries. Plus one exactness-preserving optimization: skipping the microdecoder on the EOS frame is token-identical. Findings propagated to 4 dependent beads.

comments.text:
[OQ-6 RESOLVED -> docs/QWEN3_TTS_DECODE_AND_ADMISSION.md] Answering what was still open, and correcting the
max_new_tokens pick.

1. LONG-FORM: there is NO chunking, NO sentence splitting, NO context carryover anywhere in the
   official stack (exhaustive search of inference/qwen3_tts_model.py + modeling_qwen3_tts.py). Text
   goes through the talker in ONE pass. The only chunking in the stack is codec-side
   chunked_decode(300,25), which operates on already-generated codes, not text. So there is nothing
   to port: any long-form scheme we add is OUR design, a semantic divergence by construction,
   needing a DISC entry + an A/B against single-pass on the drift gate. It also explains plan 2.8's
   25Hz-beats-12Hz long-speech result: with no carryover, long-form rests entirely on one very long
   AR run with nothing to arrest drift.

2. max_new_tokens CONFLICT RESOLVED -- the runtime default is 8192, not 2048. Precedence at
   inference/qwen3_tts_model.py:332-337 is user > generate_defaults > hard_defaults; generate_defaults
   is model.generate_config, loaded from generation_config.json at modeling:1922-1936, which contains
   8192. So: 8192 = effective runtime default; the wrapper's 2048 hard_default is DEAD CODE (never
   reached while the checkpoint ships that file); README's 2048 was an EXPLICIT eval-time override;
   modeling:2031's 4096 is unreachable via the public wrapper. Use 2048 to reproduce published
   quality numbers, 8192 for default-behavior oracle fixtures and as ftts's own default.
   TRAP: the docstring says 'generate_config.json' but the code loads 'generation_config.json'. Had
   it really looked for the former (no such file), the default would have been 2048 -- a 4x
   difference in max duration turning on one missing character. Assert the filename in the oracle.

3. STOP RULE (modeling:2283-2290): group 0 ONLY, id 2150; effective_lengths = stop_indices with slice
   [:length], so the EOS FRAME IS EXCLUDED (not decoded). Residual loop is fixed 15 steps, never
   early-stopped (2048-wide heads have no EOS id).

4. MAX-DURATION = SILENT TRUNCATION: no EOS within max_new_tokens -> effective_lengths = full length,
   truncated audio returned with no exception/warning/flag. For an agent-facing CLI this is a
   counterfeit success; ftts must report truncation as a first-class outcome (requirement handed to
   v-reliability-d65). Caps: 2048 -> 163.84 s, 8192 -> 655.36 s. Talker context 32768 is NOT binding.

5. EXACT OPTIMIZATION: the reference runs the 15 microdecoder steps even on the EOS frame
   (modeling:1671-1680) and then discards them; their only other consumer is the next step's input
   embedding, which never happens. So checking group 0 for EOS BEFORE running the microdecoder is
   token-identical. Build it into the ResidualCodeDecoder from day one.

6. Admission formulas + long-form corpus boundary design (4 independent boundaries) in the doc.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
[from OQ-8, AzureThrush] Two codec behaviours found while tracing the audio output path for the watermark question. Neither is in the plan; both affect codec parity. Detail: docs/truth-pack/OQ8_WATERMARKING.md §3.

1. REFERENCE FRAMES ARE PREPENDED BEFORE DECODE, THEN CUT FROM THE AUDIO (inference/qwen3_tts_model.py:613-631):
     codes_for_decode = cat([ref_code, generated_codes])
     wav = speech_tokenizer.decode(codes_for_decode)
     cut = int(ref_len / total_len * wav.shape[0]);  return wav[cut:]
   In ICL mode the reference's own codec frames are decoded TOGETHER with the generated frames and the audio prefix is discarded. The reference audio is never returned but it IS computed -- it primes the causal decoder's ring-buffer state so generated speech starts with a warmed receptive field instead of zeros.
   => Decoding only the generated codes is NOT equivalent; the onset will differ. Our engine must either replay the reference decode and discard, or precompute the primed ring-buffer state into .ftvoice-cache (better -- removes ref decode from the TTFA path). Either way it must be PROVEN equivalent, not assumed. Also: the streaming==batch gate must fix this warm-up convention on both sides or it fails for unrelated reasons. TTFA cost if done naively: an extra ref_frames of codec decode (~38 for a 3s reference).

2. THE CUT IS A FLOAT RATIO, NOT A FRAME COUNT. Since decode() trims to exactly n_frames * decode_upsample_rate (tokenizer_12hz/modeling_qwen3_tts_tokenizer_v2.py:1013,1018), the cut is algebraically ref_len * upsample_rate, but it is implemented as float multiply-and-truncate. Port it as exact integer ref_len * upsample_rate and record the equivalence -- otherwise it is a one-sample offset that is miserable to debug in a parity test.

Also confirmed for codec parity: decode() is RVQ lookup -> decoder.chunked_decode -> length trim, and NOTHING else. No postprocessing stage exists, so any systematic waveform difference we see is our bug, not an unported stage.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
[from OQ-13, AzureThrush] Codec architecture facts read straight off the community GGUF tensor table (qwen-tokenizer-12hz-Q8_0.gguf) -- free evidence for your bead, independent of the Python source. Detail: docs/truth-pack/OQ13_GGML_QUANT_RECONCILIATION.md §2.3.

1. SEMANTIC/ACOUSTIC ID MAPPING IS EXPLICIT IN THE TENSOR NAMES: encoder has vq_semantic (1 codebook) + vq_acoustic (15); decoder mirrors with vq_first (1) + vq_rest (15). => CODE GROUP 0 IS SEMANTIC, GROUPS 1-15 ARE ACOUSTIC, lining up exactly with the talker predicting group 0 and the microdecoder the other 15.
2. RVQ OPERATES IN A 256-d PROJECTED SPACE, not 512: codebooks are 256x2048 with 1x512x256 input and 1x256x512 output projections. Plan §2.7 does not state this.
3. THE DECODER IS BIGVGAN-STYLE WITH SNAKE ACTIVATIONS, not a plain conv stack: 58 F32 snake.alpha/snake.beta and res.N.act1/act2.alpha/beta tensors. Channel ladder 1536 -> 768 -> 384 -> 192 -> 96 -> 1; transposed-conv kernels 16, 10, 8, 6 = 2x stride for strides 8, 5, 4, 3 -- confirming plan §2.7's upsample [8,5,4,3] FROM THE WEIGHTS.
4. tok_dec.pre_tfm = 8 layers, hidden 512, ffn 1024 (matches plan §2.7). tok_enc.blk = 8 layers, hidden 512, ffn 2048 -- encoder and decoder MLP widths DIFFER.
5. KERNEL WE HAVE NOT PLANNED FOR: Snake activation is transcendental-heavy and per-channel parameterised, sitting on the codec hot path. This is exactly plan §7.2's 'vectorized polynomial transcendental' exception -- flag it for the codec kernel bead.

OR icl_mode.

the mel front end or the ECAPA stack propagates directly at FULL SCALE into the talker's input

title: [RT1] ftts talk session subcommand (umbrella)
description:
UMBRELLA (closes when its four subtasks close). `ftts talk`: a long-lived session subcommand - one process per conversation holding the warm model, accepting NDJSON control ops on stdin, emitting NDJSON events on stdout, and delivering raw PCM on a separate channel. This is the surface an orchestrating agent drives for live conversation.

WHY A NEW SUBCOMMAND INSTEAD OF EXTENDING EXISTING SURFACES:
- The resident daemon is the wrong host: strictly serial by design (resident.rs:492), frozen single-blob protocol v1 with no op dispatch and exact-version retirement (resident.rs:72, :628, reply at :780-793 is one JSON header + one whole f32 blob). Extending it means a protocol bump plus concurrency surgery on a mutable single slot. The session process replaces the resident's ROLE for conversational use (it IS the warm engine for its lifetime) while leaving the v1 contract and its warm-start users untouched.
- One-shot `say` is the wrong shape: a conversation is many utterances, interleaved with cancels, against one warm engine.

TRANSPORT DECISION (recorded rationale): NDJSON control on stdin/stdout + raw mono s16le 24 kHz PCM on fd 3 (default when fd 3 is inherited open) or --pcm-out <path|fifo>. Chosen over a local WebSocket/unix-socket server for v1 because the consumer is exactly one local orchestrator that spawns the process: stdio inherits kernel-pipe backpressure per channel, needs no port/auth story, and stays jq-debuggable. Cross-channel ordering is sequenced by BYTE COUNTS in control events (every audio event states byte_offset and bytes), mpv-JSON-IPC-style - never by timing. The NDJSON vocabulary is transport-independent by construction so a later --serve adapter (unix socket / WS, the plan's post-v1 fttsd territory) reuses it verbatim. PCM NEVER interleaves with NDJSON on any stream - the same invariant the CLI already enforces, extended.

SESSION MODEL: contexts (Cartesia-style). open pins voice+seed+format for a context's lifetime; say(text, continue) speaks/extends; flush forces buffered text out; cancel stops at the next frame boundary with a truncation receipt; close ends the context. ONE context actively synthesizing at a time in v1 (one engine, one parallel owner - AGENTS rule 5); multiple contexts may be open for fast barge-in switchover (cancel c1, open/say c2 - warm engine + 10-position prefill makes the new context's cost one prefill + first packet). Stateless: no transcript or audio persisted anywhere (AGENTS: texts and voices are sensitive); session lifetime = conversation; the process exits on shutdown op, stdin EOF, or SIGTERM with a clean terminal event.

SUBTASKS: (1) protocol schema v2 + frozen fixture + robot schema extension; (2) session runtime (control loop, engine ownership, PCM channel, buffer events); (3) cancel/truncation receipt + context switchover; (4) e2e battery + soak.

EXIT CRITERIA: an orchestrator can hold a multi-turn spoken exchange - streaming sentence chunks in, playing PCM out, barging in mid-utterance - against one `ftts talk` process, with every event schema-valid against the frozen fixture and byte accounting exact.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: all four children closed with live evidence. e3zz (schema v2 + frozen fixture + robot schema, independently verified), edz0 (session runtime live-proven incl. cold-row seam), sc94 (cancel receipts exact via drain fence, prefix identity, post-cancel hygiene, 135ms cancel->receipt / 218ms switchover), 7pgn (6/6 battery, validator-in-the-loop, byte-accounting audits). Exit criteria met live: an orchestrator holds a multi-turn spoken exchange against one ftts talk process - streaming sentence chunks in (chunked==whole bit-exact), PCM out with exact session-global accounting, barging in mid-utterance with a truthful truncation receipt; scripts/talk_loop_demo.py is the executable reference (turn 0: voice-to-voice 2206ms cold under load 85; canned-LLM latency table matures with 4ie8).

title: [P0] CLI skeleton (two shims, exit codes, profiles, stateless)
description:
[P0] CLI skeleton: cli_main, two shims, subcommands, exit codes.

WHAT: ftts-cli with pub fn cli_main() -> ExitCode in its lib; two byte-equivalent one-line [[bin]] shims (crates/ftts-cli/src/main.rs = franken_tts bin; crates/ftts-cli/src/bin/ftts.rs = ftts bin; each fn main() { ftts_cli::cli_main() }-shaped; explicit [[bin]] tables, each pointing at ITS OWN file — never the same path twice, which trips cargo's multiple-build-targets warning). Subcommand stubs: say (WAV out or --stream raw PCM-on-stdout/events-on-stderr), enroll, voice inspect, convert, robot schema/health/backends/selftest, doctor. Flags: --profile {interactive,balanced,throughput,strict}, --packet-frames {1,2,4,auto}, --math-mode {strict,fast}, --voice-pack {portable,private,minimal}, --normalize {verbatim,conservative,locale-aware}, --trace DIR, --seed.

TEXT INPUT UX (long-form is a first-class product regime — the CLI must serve it): ftts say accepts text as an argument, from --file PATH, or from stdin (- convention); multi-paragraph documents flow through the long-form path (OQ-6 chunking policy); per-span language overrides + pronunciation-lexicon hooks ride the normalization surface. Plus --check DRY-RUN: parse text, resolve model + voice, run resource ADMISSION (predicted frames/KV/memory), report the plan and cost WITHOUT synthesizing — cheap validation for scripts and agents (rides the V_REL admission machinery).

HUMAN-MODE PROGRESS: long synthesis shows observer-driven progress (frames/sec, elapsed, ETA) on stderr — never polluting stdout contracts.

EXIT CODES (stable contract, error.rs): 0 success / 1 generic / 2 usage / 3 model not found / 4 input error (bad text encoding, unreadable reference audio) / 5 budget-timeout / 6 cancelled / 7 artifact format-version mismatch / 8 enrollment-quality refusal (--force overrides where safe).

DELIBERATE ABSENCES: NO runs/sync subcommands (stateless by default; texts + voices are sensitive; benchmark evidence is written by the bench harness, not a database; any future opt-in state uses fsqlite, never rusqlite).

DONE WHEN: both binaries build from shims; exit codes unit-tested; clap surface snapshot-tested; file/stdin/argument text inputs round-trip identically; --check validated against admission outcomes; env overrides (FTTS_MODEL_DIR/THREADS/PROFILE/PACKET_FRAMES/MATH_MODE/QUANT/FORCE_ARCH/NUMA/STAGE_BUDGET_*_MS) read once via OnceLock and documented.

title: [P0] TtsEngine shell (runtime, cancellation, bounded queues, observer)
description:
[P0] TtsEngine shell: asupersync runtime, cancellation, budgets, bounded queues, SynthesisObserver.

WHAT: ftts-core's engine skeleton per the proven layered pattern: fn main() stays SYNCHRONOUS (clap -> ShutdownController -> sync run() -> exit code); the engine OWNS one asupersync Runtime below main (never spanning the process); public API sync + blocking (TtsEngine::synthesize/enroll); CPU-bound stages via spawn_blocking wrapped in per-stage budget timeouts (FTTS_STAGE_BUDGET_*_MS); a Copy CancellationToken with checkpoint() at every talker-frame boundary (cancellation is cooperative — the token goes INTO closures); ONE bounded stream-queue abstraction for PCM + events (consumer stall parks the producer — backpressure, never unbounded buffering; audio and event channels must not be able to deadlock each other: separate bounded queues, independent shutdown).

SynthesisObserver (G6 made concrete): the caller-owned observer contract — stage timings, frame progress, admission decisions, packet emissions, health events; --trace, robot NDJSON, and the bench harness are all thin consumers of the same hook; no global state, no default persistence.

HARD RULES: never nest a second runtime inside a task; never parallelism under a held lock; exactly one live synthesis fan-out per engine (the Phase-3D batching scheduler later becomes that single owner).

DONE WHEN: empty pipeline runs end-to-end with events + cancellation + budget timeout all demonstrated by tests; many_utterances_without_deadlock watchdog skeleton in place (utterances >> pool; hangs CI on regression).
close_reason: Split closeout: engine capability landed in 850c072 and b721d58 (owned runtime, blocking facade, cancellation, budgets, one-live-synthesis admission, independent bounded PCM/event queues, observer, and focused tests). The remaining mandatory full-workspace gate is moved to frankentts-01t; no feature work remains on this bead.

title: [P0] Model-gated harness + test observability convention
description:
[P0] Model-gated test harness + THE PROJECT-WIDE TEST OBSERVABILITY CONVENTION.

PART 1 — MODEL-GATED HARNESS: the pattern for everything needing multi-GB weights: tests skip WITH SUCCESS when the model artifact is absent (CI stays green without weights) but the skip is HONEST — receipts record skipped-vs-green distinctly (a skipped ladder is NEVER mistaken for green; XFAIL never SKIP for known divergences). When weights ARE present, prove the NATIVE path actually ran (point any fallback at /nonexistent so silent fallback fails loudly).

PART 2 — THE TEST OBSERVABILITY CONVENTION (inherited by EVERY bead's tests; their "unit tests" DONE-WHEN clauses implicitly include it — this bead is the single authoritative definition so 100+ beads need not repeat it): (a) every test emits STRUCTURED, DETAILED LOGS — on failure a test must localize the problem WITHOUT a debugger rerun: assertion context (expected vs actual with shapes/dtypes/indices), the seam being tested, fixture provenance (which oracle dump, which hash), RNG seeds, tolerance used + its source (the floor artifact), and timing; (b) comparator failures print the FIRST divergent element with its coordinates plus summary stats (max-abs, cosine, count-over-tolerance) — never a bare "assert failed"; (c) e2e scripts log every stage transition with wall-clock + key intermediate hashes (token-stream hash, PCM hash) so a red run pinpoints its stage in seconds; (d) logs are machine-parseable (one JSON object per event where practical) so CI can aggregate failure patterns; (e) test names encode the contract tested (contract_a_l2_talker_layer17_cosine, not test_talker_3). Rust: a shared test-support module in ftts-conformance provides the logging macros/helpers so the convention is one import away.

WHY: the user-facing promise is "we can be sure everything works perfectly after implementation" — that requires failures to be INFORMATIVE, not just detected. This convention is what makes 121 beads' worth of tests debuggable by agents at 3am.

DONE WHEN: harness macros/utilities + logging helpers in ftts-conformance; a demo test shows all three gate states (green-with-model, skip-without-model, loud-failure-on-silent-fallback) AND the logging convention (a deliberately failed comparison produces a fully self-localizing log); the convention documented in the crate docs where every test author will see it.

title: [P0] Robot NDJSON contract + frozen-schema test
description:
[P0] Robot NDJSON contract + schema + contract test.

WHAT: versioned NDJSON events, one JSON object per line, every line carrying schema_version: run_start, stage (name/seq/elapsed/budget), frame (coarse progress, throttled), audio_chunk (byte offset, duration, packet size, sink), health, run_complete, run_error (carries the exit code). PCM NEVER interleaved with NDJSON on one stream: events on stdout with audio to -o/fd, OR --stream raw = PCM on stdout with events on stderr — one documented contract. robot schema self-describes all event types machine-readably; robot health reports model presence/arch features/threads; robot backends reports detected ISA tier + KernelPlan + pool sizing.

CONTRACT TEST: robot_contract.rs (in ftts-conformance) validates emitted events against a frozen JSON-schema fixture; schema changes require a deliberate fixture update (never silent).

WHY: agent-first ergonomics is G5; robot mode is how agent users consume ftts, and a stable versioned schema is what makes it scriptable. Model resolution errors must be ACTIONABLE (list every searched directory; cheap magic-bytes header sniff, never a tensor load).

DONE WHEN: skeleton events flow end-to-end on the empty pipeline; contract test green; schema doc emitted by robot schema matches the fixture.
close_reason: All three DONE-WHEN criteria met (4f152f1). (a) Skeleton events now flow end-to-end on the empty pipeline -- this was the missing piece: run_start/stage/text_prepared/run_complete/run_error were catalogued and schema-frozen but never emitted, only health and backends were. say now emits run_start -> stage(resolve) -> text_prepared -> stage(admission) -> check_complete -> run_complete, with run_error on stderr on failure; RunContext carries a shared run_id and one clock; the event stream is chosen ONCE (stdout, or stderr under --stream raw) so NDJSON can never interleave with PCM. (b) Contract test green: ftts-cli 17 tests + robot_contract 9 tests. (c) Schema doc matches the fixture, updated DELIBERATELY -- the test refused the change, I diffed emitted vs frozen and confirmed the only delta was the text_prepared addition (nothing removed, nothing changed, env vars and exit codes untouched), then copied it over as instructed. Added text_prepared for p18, privacy-safe by construction (mode/unicode version/char count/trace flag; no raw text, with a test asserting the input never appears in the stream) and told them how to add the rules array deliberately. Two pre-existing defects caught by validating the whole stream: check_complete was specified to carry run_id and never did, and nothing pinned the one-object-per-line invariant -- both fixed, the latter with the newline-framing test cc_1 offered on this bead. FttsError gained remediation() so agents can branch on the next step without parsing prose. ftts-cli gained a path dep on ftts-model-qwen; validate_repo 9 rules still pass. Gates: fmt 0, full cargo test 0, ftts-cli+conformance green, validate_repo 9 OK, ubs --staged 0. Workspace clippy is red from another agent's in-flight converter.rs (E0308 at :733, their dirty file, untouched); I fixed the other clippy blocker (fttsq.rs assert!(false)) separately in 6d68536 and flagged theirs on p2-converter-8b4.

      let event = run_error_event("r1", &FttsError::Generic("a\nb".to_owned()), None);

or user text will put it on the wire -- worth a deliberate decision in the schema about whether
run_error.message is allowed to contain user text, given the stateless/no-persisted-history promise.

title: [P1] Codec decoder (streaming+offline, ring buffers, stream==batch gate)
description:
[P1] Codec decoder: streaming + offline, ring buffers, exact geometry.

WHAT: the speech-tokenizer decoder in safe Rust: RVQ embedding sums over the 16 code groups (high-precision codebooks); 8 transformer-like layers (hidden 512, intermediate 1024, 16 heads x head_dim 64 — attention width 1024 = 2x hidden — sliding window 72); causal convs with STATEFUL RING BUFFERS sized from OQ-7's receptive fields; upsampling [8,5,4,3] to 1920 samples per frame at 24 kHz, written STREAMING into the output PCM buffer (no re-decode of past audio). Both drive modes: offline (whole token stream) and streaming (packet-at-a-time with persistent state).

THE STANDING GATE (from day one, not retrofitted): streaming == offline decode of the same token stream, BIT-IDENTICAL target (same ops, same order — chunking must not change arithmetic); any divergence is a ledgered DISC, never silent. Plus packet-1 == packet-4 equality for the same tokens.

DONE WHEN: block-level fixture parity vs oracle (per-block activations); waveform within floor-derived tolerance of oracle decode of the SAME tokens; streaming==offline green across chunk-boundary fuzz schedules; ring-buffer state unit tests with logging.

comments.text:
[OQ-7 resolved -> see docs/QWEN3_TTS_CODEC_SPEC.md]

STREAMING GATE DESIGN INPUT (major finding, sec 5.2): the official decode path is
Qwen3TTSTokenizerV2Decoder.chunked_decode(chunk_size=300, left_context_size=25) -- it is ALWAYS used
(modeling_qwen3_tts_tokenizer_v2.py:1015). The pre-transformer's effective left receptive field is
568 code frames (8 stacked layers x 71 back per sliding window of 72), i.e. 23x the 25 frames the
chunker supplies. Consequences:
 (1) utterances <= 300 frames (24 s) -> single chunk, context 0 -> chunked_decode == whole-sequence
     decode. Put L4/L5 goldens HERE so they are unambiguous.
 (2) beyond 300 frames the reference is NOT equal to whole-sequence decode and is self-inconsistent.
 (3) 'streaming == batch' must therefore NAME its reference. Recommendation: target whole-sequence
     decode (the mathematically defined object); agreement with the official chunker past 300 frames
     is a separate MEASURED Contract-B row with a DISC entry -- never claimed as bit-exactness.
 (4) do NOT imitate the 25-frame-context chunker in our ring buffers; that would bake an upstream
     artifact into our engine. Correct stateful streaming needs only ~2.4-4.7 MB transformer KV
     (8x72x1024x2) + a few hundred KB conv ring buffers -- doing it right costs nothing.
Conv stack has ZERO lookahead (verified): stride-1 convs are pure left-padded causal (extra_padding
evaluates to 0); transposed convs trim kernel-stride from the RIGHT. Conv-only left context = 11.38
code frames. Full per-stage ring-buffer table in the spec doc sec 6.

CONTRACT ADDENDUM — BINDING SPEC SYNC (reality-check phase 5, FuchsiaMouse, 2026-08-06). Build against docs/QWEN3_TTS_CODEC_SPEC.md, which post-dates this body:
QUANTIZER: SplitResidualVectorQuantizer — rvq_first (1 semantic, group 0) + rvq_rest (15 acoustic, groups 1-15); each with input_proj [256,512,1] / output_proj [512,256,1], bias-free k=1; RVQ math in 256-d NOT 512-d; branch results ADDED. Codebooks 2048x256. PORTING HAZARD: codebooks stored UNNORMALIZED — usable table = embedding_sum / clamp(cluster_usage, 1e-5), materialized at build time with epsilon recorded. semantic_codebook_size:4096 is DEAD CONFIG; both sub-quantizers use 2048.
PRE-TRANSFORMER (8 layers, sliding window 72): 16Q/16KV — NO GQA; QK-Norm ABSENT (nn.Identity); RMSNorm eps 1e-5 (NOT 1e-6), f32 upcast; LayerScale on BOTH residual branches init 0.01 (folding into o_proj/down_proj legal only as ledgered parity-proven transform); SwiGLU bias-free; input_proj/output_proj HAVE biases; RoPE PLAIN theta 10000 up to 8000 positions — the project's THIRD rotary kernel, never share tables.
UPSAMPLING: 1920 = 480 x 4; the x4 is upsampling_ratios [2,2] at latent_dim 1024 BEFORE the conv stack; [8,5,4,3] (tconv kernels 16/10/8/6) is the decoder, channel ladder 1536->768->384->192->96->1, BigVGAN-style with SNAKE activations (per-channel alpha/beta F32, transcendental-heavy, hot path — plan §7.2 vectorized-transcendental exception applies).
RING BUFFERS: conv-only left context 11.38 code frames (spec §6 per-stage table; worst case decoder.1 dilation-9 = 54 taps at x32 over 768 ch). Transformer retained state 8x72x1024x2 ≈ 4.7MB F32 / 2.4MB BF16. Do NOT imitate the official 25-frame chunker.
STREAMING GATE — NAMED REFERENCE: our exact target is WHOLE-SEQUENCE decode; streaming == whole-sequence offline bit-identical is the gate. Agreement with official chunked_decode(300, ctx 25) holds at <=300 frames and DIVERGES beyond — that is a MEASURED Contract-B row + DISCREPANCIES entry, never a regression.
OVERFLOW: K = 7168 (decoder.0, 1024x7), i32 headroom 9.25x — the PROJECT'S BINDING WORST CASE (2.33x the talker). Doctrine #6: this row goes in the shipped selftest; the AVX2 vpmaddubsw i16-saturation proof is owed HERE first.
BATCHED PATH: padding sentinel -1; lengths = (codes[...,0] > -1).sum(1)*1920, clamp(min=0).
FIXTURES: ft7-cpu-fp32-r1 has 80 codec arrays per mode; CPU floor max_abs 0.0 ⇒ exact compare.
OUT OF SCOPE (tracked in frankentts-5yl): ICL reference-prefix decode — do NOT assume codec decode is a pure function of the generated token stream.

title: [P1] Sequential 15-step microdecoder (authoritative baseline)
description:
[P1] Sequential 15-step microdecoder forward (the honest baseline) — teacher-forced parity per depth.

WHAT: the Residual-Code Microdecoder exactly as the official inference path runs it: after the talker samples the primary code, RESET the tiny KV state, then for residual_depth 0..14: embed the previous token with the DEPTH-SPECIFIC embedding -> 5-layer forward (1024-wide geometry, plain RoPE via apply_rotary_pos_emb semantics — a DIFFERENT rotary kernel than the talker's mRoPE) -> the DEPTH-SPECIFIC 2048-way head -> sample -> feed forward. The frame sequence is 1 conditioning/primary position + 15 residual positions = 16; each sampled residual conditions the NEXT depth (autoregressively dependent — any "depths are independent" shortcut is invalid, ledgered as such).

WHY THIS EXACT SHAPE MATTERS: this sequential loop is the AUTHORITATIVE baseline that every later lever (hot-packed engine, FrankenMTP, Q4 depths) must match bit-for-bit (greedy) or distributionally (sampled). Getting the conditioning inputs per depth right (OQ-5) is the single most dangerous correctness surface in the project.

The CPU tier is NOT exact-compare at this seam, contrary to the addendum's max_abs 0.0.

Recorded XFAIL, never SKIP, so a future fixture regeneration that makes it exact fails loudly instead of leaving a stale entry.

title: [P1] Two-level sampler (production + canonical greedy + seeded RNG)
description:
[P1] Two-level sampler: production sampling + canonical greedy + seeded RNG.

WHAT: the sampler for BOTH autoregressive levels per the pinned generation config — talker: temperature 0.9, top_k 50, top_p 1.0, repetition_penalty 1.05 (penalty semantics ported EXACTLY per the spec); residual microdecoder: temperature 0.9, top_k 50, top_p 1.0 — plus CANONICAL GREEDY mode (argmax both levels; the Contract-A conformance decoder per OQ-12) and our own seeded RNG (deterministic across runs given seed; a standing DISC entry records that we replicate the DISTRIBUTION CONTRACT, never torch's RNG stream — so free-running comparisons vs the oracle are distribution-level by design: many seeds x paired texts x rank statistics).

comments.author: cc_1
comments.text:
TRUTH PACK E-2 + E-4 (frankentts-t-pin-sources-b2u) — two sampler traps.

E-4 — PRECEDENCE TRAP. code_predictor_config carries STALE HF defaults (temperature 1.0,
do_sample false). Those are NOT what runs. modeling_qwen3_tts.py:1674-1678 passes
subtalker_dosample / subtalker_top_p / subtalker_top_k / subtalker_temperature explicitly into
code_predictor.generate(). The authority is generation_config.json:
  talker:       do_sample true, temperature 0.9, top_k 50, top_p 1.0, repetition_penalty 1.05
  microdecoder: subtalker_dosample true, subtalker_temperature 0.9, subtalker_top_k 50,
                subtalker_top_p 1.0   (NO repetition penalty at the residual level)
A port reading the nested config would sample GREEDILY at T=1.0 on the microdecoder. The plan's
T0.9/k50/p1.0 was right; the precedence is the trap.

E-2 — THE TWO LEVELS HAVE DIFFERENT VOCAB WIDTHS. Talker head is 3072 wide
(codec_head = Linear(1024,3072,bias=False), :1579); the 15 per-depth microdecoder heads are 2048 wide.
Stop detection is codec_eos_token_id = 2150 on the TALKER head only. Talker control ids from
config.json: pad 2148, bos 2149, eos 2150, think 2154, nothink 2155, think_bos 2156, think_eos 2157,
and language ids english 2050 german 2053 spanish 2054 chinese 2055 japanese 2058 french 2061
korean 2064 russian 2069 italian 2070 portuguese 2071.

Third trap for the canonical-greedy ladder: max_new_tokens has THREE different upstream values —
generation_config.json 8192, qwen3_tts_model.py:2031 default 4096, README eval 2048 (gh/README.md:465).
Detail: docs/truth-pack/FACT_DISPOSITIONS.md (E-2, E-4)

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
[from OQ-12, AzureThrush] SAMPLER CONTRACT RESOLVED — this is what you implement. Full detail: docs/truth-pack/OQ12_SAMPLER_CONTRACT.md.

THE HIGHEST-VALUE LINE: canonical greedy is NOT 'argmax of the model logits'. Both levels run stock HF GenerationMixin.generate, where logits PROCESSORS always apply and only WARPERS are gated on do_sample. So do_sample=False still runs repetition_penalty, min_new_tokens, and suppress_tokens.
  TALKER canonical greedy   = repetition_penalty(1.05) -> min_new_tokens(2) -> suppress_tokens -> argmax
  MICRODECODER canon greedy = argmax on raw logits (it has NO processors)
A port that does bare argmax WILL diverge from the reference run with do_sample=False, and it will look like a kernel bug.

AND: argmax is invariant to the whole warper stack (temperature is monotonic; top_k keeps the max; top_p=1.0 is a no-op), so canonical greedy ids are identical with or without warpers. The canonical decoder is therefore fully defined TODAY and does not wait on the greedy-audio-viability fork.

PRODUCTION PIPELINE, exact order from transformers 4.57.3 source (_get_logits_processor):
  TALKER:       rep_penalty(1.05) -> min_new_tokens(2) -> suppress_tokens -> temperature(/0.9) -> top_k(50) -> top_p(1.0 no-op) -> softmax -> multinomial
  MICRODECODER: temperature(/0.9) -> top_k(50) -> top_p(1.0 no-op) -> softmax -> multinomial
THE MICRODECODER HAS NO REPETITION PENALTY AND NO SUPPRESSION -- sharing one sampler across both levels without gating this is a silent semantic bug.

suppress_tokens = ids 2048..3071 except 2150 (codec_eos). Talker generable alphabet = codes 0..2047 + EOS 2150. All specials (codec_pad 2148, codec_bos 2149, think ids 2154-2157) are prompt-only and MUST be suppressed at generation.

max_new_tokens: THREE sources disagree (generation_config.json 8192, hard default 2048, generate() signature 4096). Precedence (user > generation_config > hard default) makes 8192 effective => ~655 s / 10.9 min ceiling. Do not hard-code 2048 or 4096.

DISC ENTRY IS YOURS TO FILE, NOT MINE. The RNG-stream divergence (we replicate the distribution contract, never torch's stream) needs a DISC-NNN, but docs/DISCREPANCIES.md's schema requires measured_impact + fixture/artifact hashes and explicitly forbids unmeasured records. I have no weights and no audio, so filing one now would be counterfeit green. File it when your sampler lands with a fixture and a measured distributional impact. Reasoning in docs/truth-pack/OQ12_SAMPLER_CONTRACT.md §3.

Caveat: the processor ORDER above is read from transformers 4.57.3 (cc_1's tokenizer-oracle pin). The authoritative runtime pin is oq15's deliverable -- re-read the order if it differs; HF has reordered this list before.

comments.author: cc_11
comments.text:
[from OQ-12, docs/CANONICAL_DECODER_AND_SAMPLER.md] Your full contract is now defined -- build against
sections 2 and 4; nothing here waits on the oracle.

THE TWO LEVELS HAVE DIFFERENT PROCESSOR STACKS. Do not build one 'sampler' and apply it twice.
  Talker      (modeling:2044-2066): repetition_penalty 1.05, min_new_tokens 2, eos 2150,
              suppress_tokens = ids 2048..3071 EXCEPT 2150, then temp 0.9 / top_k 50 / top_p 1.0.
  Microdecoder(modeling:1671-1680): temp 0.9 / top_k 50 / top_p 1.0 and NOTHING else -- no
              repetition penalty, no suppression, no EOS, fixed 15 steps.

ORDER (non-commutative at every stage; reproduce exactly):
  talker: raw -> rep penalty -> min_new_tokens EOS mask -> suppress mask -> temperature -> top-k
          -> top-p -> softmax -> multinomial
  micro : raw -> temperature -> top-k -> top-p -> softmax -> multinomial
Traps: temperature BEFORE the penalty changes the penalty (it applies to raw logits); top-k AFTER
top-p yields a different candidate set than the reference's top-k-then-top-p.

REPETITION PENALTY IS SIGN-DEPENDENT (classic port bug):
  score > 0 -> score / penalty ;  score <= 0 -> score * penalty
Applied over the GROUP-0 code history only, not the full 16-code frame -- group 0 is the only thing
the talker itself emitted.

CANONICAL GREEDY (Contract A) = argmax at both levels with the NON-WARPER processors still applied
(penalty + min_new_tokens + suppress on the talker; nothing on the microdecoder). Warpers are
excluded deliberately: temperature is a monotone positive scale and top-k/top-p are truncations, so
none can change an argmax -- including them would be harmless but would misrepresent the contract.
The non-warper processors ARE included because they change which token wins.

SUPPRESS MASK IS LOAD-BEARING: talker effective support is {0..2047} u {2150}. Without the mask a port
will occasionally emit a control id (2148/2149/2154-2157) into group 0 and hand the codec an
out-of-range code -- rare and seed-dependent, exactly what the ladder is for.

RNG: replicate the DISTRIBUTION contract, never torch's stream. Scope determinism as (build, ISA,
sampler version, seed, artifact). Token-level agreement with the reference under sampling is a
DIAGNOSTIC, never a gate. You owe a DISC entry when the divergence can be MEASURED -- not before.

PIN NOTE: there are no custom logits processors anywhere in the Qwen stack, so every semantic above is
defined by pinned transformers 4.57.3. A pin change can silently change the sampler contract and must
re-run L3.

title: [P1] STFT/mel front end (feature-exact vs oracle)
description:
[P1] STFT/mel front end (split from the audio core — different consumer, different risk profile).

WHAT: fixed-size STFT + mel filterbank in pure Rust (hand-rolled fixed-size FFT or a pure-Rust FFT crate) matching the reference speaker-encoder feature extraction EXACTLY: n_fft, hop, window, fmin/fmax, mel scale variant, log/normalization scheme — every parameter from OQ-9's line-cited enumeration. 128 mel bins at 24 kHz input.

WHY ITS OWN BEAD: the mel front end serves the ECAPA speaker encoder (the x-vector cloning path) and diagnostics — NOT the synthesis hot path — and its failure mode is unique: mel-parameter mismatches are the CLASSIC silent killer of speaker-embedding parity (embeddings drift plausibly rather than obviously; the voice "almost" matches). Splitting it from WAV decode/resample lets a different agent own it in parallel and gives it its own oracle-differential gate instead of hiding inside a bigger bead's DONE list.

DONE WHEN: (audio -> mel) fixture-exact vs the oracle within the measured floor over the golden references; parameter-by-parameter unit tests (window symmetry, filterbank row sums, edge bins) with self-localizing logs per the test-observability convention; property test: mel of silence/impulse/sine matches analytically computed references.
close_reason: Already shipped — verified 2026-08-23 at HEAD 4c90780: pure-Rust STFT+mel is ftts-model-qwen/src/speaker.rs log_mel_from_24khz_pcm (fft 1024, hop 256, periodic Hann, reflect pad 384, Slaney norm+scale filterbank, ln after 1e-5 floor — every OQ-9 line-cited parameter). Gating: speaker_encoder_l2 certifies mel-onward EXACT vs oracle tensors (5/5 green today); speaker_enrollment_l2 gates the waveform->mel front end vs the oracle's captured mel via the certified codec reconstruction, with the 128-sample-shift negative control (3/3 green today). The bead's 'feature-exact vs oracle' for the front end is impossible with this fixture pack (no waveform capture — the pack's first speaker-path capture IS the mel); the shipped gate is the strongest supportable tier and documents that reasoning in-file (EnrollmentIdentity, not ConformanceExact).

title: [P1] Talker forward (mRoPE/GQA/SwiGLU) teacher-forced parity
description:
[P1] Talker forward (28 layers, mRoPE, GQA, SwiGLU) — teacher-forced parity per layer.

WHAT: the talker in safe Rust over the BF16 accessors: embedding pipeline (cold text rows + projection; audio/conditioning tokens per spec); 28 identical layers — RMSNorm -> QKV (1024->2048/1024/1024) -> QK-Norm if OQ-3 confirms -> mRoPE (theta 1e6, interleaved multimodal sections [24,20,20], 3-D position ids per OQ-4's schedule) -> GQA attention (16Q/8KV, head_dim 128, causal, growing KV cache preallocated from census) -> O-proj (2048->1024) -> residual; RMSNorm -> gate/up (1024->3072) -> SiLU-gated -> down (3072->1024) -> residual; final norm + primary-code head.

PARITY METHOD (seam-ordered, the skill's Phase-1 discipline): feed each Rust stage the ORACLE'S EXACT INPUT tensor (decouples stages); per-layer cosine ~1.0 + max-abs ledgered vs teacher-forced fixtures; then first-frame primary-code argmax EXACT; attribute every residual to a named cause, never hand-wave.

DONE WHEN: all 28 layers pass L1/L2 vs fixtures within floor-derived tolerances; first-token argmax exact; KV cache correctness (cached==uncached) proven; unit tests per sub-op with logging.
close_reason: Capability shipped and gated: per-layer teacher-forced parity + argmax-exact receipts in ftts-conformance; stronger than the bead's exit bar.

comments.author: cc_1
comments.text:
OQ-11 RESOLVED (frankentts-oq11-tokenizer-p94) — implementation contract + a DISC entry you OWE.

READ FIRST: docs/truth-pack/tokenizer/OQ11_TOKENIZER.md
REFERENCE IDS: docs/truth-pack/tokenizer/tokenizer_conformance.json (92 cases, generated only by
scripts/gen_tokenizer_conformance.py against the pinned oracle transformers==4.57.3). Point your
id-exact tests at cases[].ids. Do NOT hand-write expected ids — regenerate.

1) ALGORITHM: byte-level BPE (GPT-2 lineage) from vocab.json + merges.txt. There is NO tokenizer.json.
   Measured: slow and fast tokenizers agree on all 92 cases, so ONE implementation suffices.

2) NORMALIZATION: exactly Unicode NFC, and nothing else. The PROCESSOR does nothing
   (processing_qwen3_tts.py forwards text unchanged). The TOKENIZER applies NFC
   (tokenization_qwen2.py:338; fast backend normalizer == NFC()).
   IT IS NFC, NOT NFKC — proven: circled-digit/fullwidth/ligature/CJK-compat probes all stay
   distinct. Reaching for NFKC (a common default) silently breaks fullwidth CJK punctuation.
   => You need a real Unicode NFC implementation, and you must PIN AND RECORD the Unicode version
   it targets (NFC tables are versioned; Python's unicodedata follows its interpreter's version).

3) ROUND-TRIP IS NOT IDENTITY. decode(encode(x)) == x is FALSE by design for non-NFC input
   (3 of 92 cases: combining-nfd, hangul-nfd, vietnamese-nfd). Round-trip identity holds only for
   NFC-normalized text. A global round-trip assertion is WRONG and will fail correctly.

4) THE BIG ONE — fix_mistral_regex. Every official entrypoint loads the tokenizer via
   AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(path, fix_mistral_regex=True) (qwen3_tts_model.py:118), which
   REPLACES the pre-tokenizer regex with Mistral's. It engages because config.json says
   transformers_version 4.57.3, which falls in a two-patch gap in an unrelated vendor fix
   (tokenization_utils_base.py:2451-2499). The model was near-certainly TRAINED with Qwen's native
   regex, so 'match upstream' != 'match training'.
   MEASURED IMPACT: 6/92 cases, confined to two classes — case-boundary splitting inside words
   (getUserByIdOrThrow 4->6 tokens; XMLHttpRequest 1->3; iPhone 1->2) and complex-script
   segmentation (Thai). Ordinary prose in all ten supported languages, contractions, numbers,
   currency, dates, URLs, email, punctuation, CJK and emoji are IDENTICAL.

   YOUR OBLIGATIONS:
     - default to the OFFICIAL regex (Contract A is parity with the pinned reference implementation)
     - expose FTTS_TOKENIZER_REGEX=official|native as the kill switch
     - THEN file the DISC-NNN entry. It is deliberately NOT written yet: docs/DISCREPANCIES.md
       requires our_behavior + a measured impact + an implemented FTTS_* switch, none of which exist
       before your code does. Writing it now would be a counterfeit ledger entry. cases[] already
       carries ids_native_qwen_regex for every case so the A/B is cheap.
     - which regex sounds better on camelCase text is a LISTENING question, not a reading one; do
       not 'fix' upstream silently before that measurement exists.

5) VOCAB SIZES — three different numbers, do not conflate:
     tokenizer base vocab 151,643 | +33 added specials => len(tokenizer) 151,676
     model text embedding 151,936 rows (PADDED; rows 151,676-151,935 unreachable)
   This bead's parent text said 'vocab 151,936' — that is the EMBEDDING size, not the tokenizer's.

6) NO BOS/EOS IS ADDED by the tokenizer (add_bos_token false, bos_token null). Prompt assembly is
   entirely the caller's job — see OQ-10. Other settings: add_prefix_space false,
   clean_up_tokenization_spaces false, split_special_tokens false, errors 'replace',
   model_max_length 131072, eos <|im_end|>, pad <|endoftext|>, unk null.
   Special tokens as literal text ARE matched to single ids (<|im_start|> -> 151644); a lookalike

title: [P2] Streaming converter (bounded memory, by-construction parity)
description:
[P2] Streaming bounded-memory converter (runtime quant first, byte-identical by construction).

WHAT: ftts convert: mmap/stream ONE safetensors tensor at a time -> validate against the WeightsManifest -> quantize in bounded tiles -> hash + write its canonical .fttsq section -> release -> atomically finalize the index. NEVER loads the whole BF16 model into a map widened to f32 (bounded peak memory on ordinary machines; no multi-GB transient).

ORDERING RULE (the by-construction parity trick): RUNTIME quantization ships FIRST (the engine can quantize from raw safetensors in-process); the offline converter then reuses the IDENTICAL quantizer function — so artifact-vs-runtime parity is byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION, plus a test asserting it. Quantizer: per-output-channel symmetric int8, zero-point 0, scale = max|w_row|/127 (the proven frankentorch scheme); deterministic (pure function of input bytes; same source -> same .fttsq, content hash asserted; no RNG, no calibration data).

DONE WHEN: converts the pinned checkpoint under a stated memory ceiling; artifact==runtime byte-identity test green; determinism test (convert twice -> identical bytes) green; conversion provenance (source hash) embedded + verified on load.
notes: POLISH R7: explicit CONVERT E2E SCRIPT required: pinned safetensors -> ftts convert (memory ceiling asserted via RSS sampling, logged) -> census-on-load green -> .fttspack generation -> ONE REAL SYNTHESIS byte-compared to the runtime-quant path (the by-construction parity claim exercised end-to-end); every stage logs wall-clock + content hashes; this script IS the distribution-proof precursor the release bead reuses (convert byte-parity vs published hash).

TERMINOLOGY FIX the plan needs (§3.1 of the doc): 'acoustic codebooks stay high precision' currently reads as covering the microdecoder's per-depth INPUT embeddings (code_pred.codec_embd.N, 1024x2048). It should not -- those are Q8 upstream and are a different object from the codec's RVQ reconstruction codebooks (vq_*.codebook, 256x2048, F32). Three distinct objects, not two.

title: [P2] robot selftest + i32-overflow proofs (permanent law)
description:
[P2] robot selftest + i32-overflow proof suite (permanent law, shipped).

WHAT — TWO INSEPARABLE DELIVERABLES: (1) THE OVERFLOW PROOF SUITE: for EVERY int8 kernel class, proof that the i32 accumulator cannot overflow at THIS model's real worst-case K — unit tests multiplying worst-case saturated operands asserting i32 == i64 reference, on every kernel tier. THE K TABLE (from census; recompute if OQ-2/OQ-7 shift it): talker/microdecoder down_proj K=3072 -> U8S8 <= 3072*255*127 ~= 99.5M (>=21x i32 headroom); o_proj K=2048 -> ~66.3M; other GEMMs K<=1024; codec conv reduction lengths C_in*kernel_width from OQ-7 (whether or not im2col is ever materialized); the seq-16 verification pass shares per-element K bounds (larger m does not change per-output accumulation). (2) THE `ftts robot selftest` SUBCOMMAND: re-proves ON THE END USER'S SILICON: dispatched-kernel == scalar-oracle exact i32 equality at real model shapes for every tier the machine exposes; all overflow rows; capability-vs-actually-executed route reporting; NDJSON verdict rows. This is what the release's distribution proofs and the runtime-health scalar-fallback trigger consume.

PERMANENT LAW: every FUTURE kernel class (Q4 unpack path, codec convs, verification pass, batched variants, any Metal path) ships its own worst-case-K selftest row BEFORE it can become a default. AVX2 vpmaddubsw saturates at i16 before widening — it carries its own split-accumulate proof or a ledgered DISC.

DONE WHEN: suite covers every existing tier + the census K table; `robot selftest` emits per-row verdicts and integrates with the ISA-fallback health gate; the permanent-law rule documented where kernel authors will see it (ftts-kernels crate docs); fault-injection (a deliberately broken kernel) trips both selftest and fallback.

The seq-16 FrankenMTP verification GEMM uses the same weights at larger m: same per-element K, so the same bound applies (re-prove anyway per plan §6.8). Codec conv K still owed by OQ-7.

title: [P2] Text-embedding Q8 experiment (622->311 MB)
description:
[P2] Text-embedding Q8 experiment (footprint lever, separately gated).

WHAT: quantize the ~622 MB BF16 text embedding (151,936 x 2048) to Q8 (~311 MB saved; artifact drops from ~1.6 GB-class toward ~1.3 GB-class — NOTE the community Q8 conversion already quantizes it, which is exactly why their 993 MB talker figure looks small).

WHY SEPARATE: v1's "keep all embeddings high-precision" was too coarse — the text embedding is COLD (row-wise prefill access) with a completely different risk profile than acoustic RVQ codebooks (which stay protected). Risk surface: token-embedding perturbations propagate through the whole talker — gate on Contract-B distributional metrics + WER band + a listening spot-check, not assumption.

DONE WHEN: measured verdict with receipts; if kept, the artifact-size table updates everywhere it is quoted; ledger row either way.

title: [P4] Enrollment pipeline (diagnostics, quality/quick/auto)
description:
[P4] Enrollment pipeline: diagnostics + three modes (quality/quick/auto).

WHAT: ftts enroll end-to-end: decode/resample reference -> VAD + diagnostics (clipping, SNR, reverberation, background music, multi-speaker/overlap detection, stationarity) -> mode selection: QUALITY (transcript-backed ICL: verified transcript + codec-encoder tokens + cached prompt state — the quality path), QUICK (x-vector only: ECAPA embedding, no transcript — upstream documents possible quality reduction and the CLI says so), AUTO (ICL when the transcript verifies, else x-vector WITH A WARNING) — never presented as interchangeable equals. Warnings are LOUD (continuation-style cloners reproduce prompt-recording defects — tell the user BEFORE they hear it); refusal (exit 8) reserved for unusable input with --force for consenting adults. Consent attestation recorded; NO acquisition features (no URL fetchers) — doctrine 10.

DONE WHEN: all three modes produce working .ftvoice packs whose synthesis matches oracle-enrolled baselines; every diagnostic has a unit test with a synthetic defect fixture (clipped/reverberant/music-bed/two-speaker samples); warning + refusal paths tested; enrollment time measured.
notes: POLISH R7: explicit ENROLLMENT E2E SCRIPT required (the voice compiler's version of the CLI e2e): spawn real binaries — ftts enroll ref.wav (each of the three modes) -> ftts voice inspect --json (validate every field incl. consent + diagnostics + quality scores) -> ftts say --voice pack.ftvoice -> validate output WAV; structured logs at every stage (mode chosen + why, diagnostics values, embedding hash, token counts, synthesis timing) so a failed enrollment localizes instantly; runs model-gated in CI; reused by the release smoke suite.

title: [P4] .ftvoice + .ftvoice-cache formats (consent, profiles)
description:
[P4] .ftvoice portable format + .ftvoice-cache (the two-layer voice artifact) + VOICE_COMPILER_DESIGN.md.

WHAT: PORTABLE .ftvoice (stable identity data): reference hashes + provenance + CONSENT ATTESTATION (doctrine 10: recorded at enrollment; --consent-attest for non-interactive); transcript + alignment; selected speech regions; speaker embedding; reference codec tokens; diagnostics + enrollment-quality scores; language metadata; the REPRODUCIBLE PREPROCESSING RECIPE (so re-enrollment is deterministic); optionally embedded lossless normalized reference audio. PROFILES: --voice-pack portable (embeds reference) / private (derived features only) / minimal (embedding only) — privacy is a deliberate, documented product choice. DERIVED .ftvoice-cache (recomputable ONLY): static prompt embeddings, verified static-prefix KV, backend layouts, quantized cached states, packet-mode codec context; keyed by {voice_recipe_hash, model_hash, prompt_builder_version, streaming_mode, quant_recipe, math_mode, engine_abi}. A .ftvoice must survive a model-revision bump by re-deriving from stored primitives — caches are optimizations, never the only copy.

ALSO OWNS: docs/VOICE_COMPILER_DESIGN.md — skeleton committed with this bead (formats, profiles, privacy rationale, cache-key semantics); finalized as the Phase-4 beads land (segment discovery, transcript verification, multi-ref policies fold their design records in).

HARDENING: same acceptance criteria as .fttsq (checked arithmetic, digests, truncation/bit-flip tests, fuzz targets).

DONE WHEN: read/write + all three profiles; idempotence (identical input -> identical portable artifact, hash-stable — a metamorphic gate); cache invalidation on every key-tuple component tested; ftts voice inspect renders everything human- and JSON-readably; the design doc skeleton exists and is linked from the README docs map.

Hardened .fttsq-grade: digest-verified sections, checked arithmetic, named refusals, fixed-point layout writer, byte-idempotent (no timestamps). Evidence: voice module tests 17/17 (incl. truncation-at-every-boundary, bit-flip named refusals, idempotence roundtrip); artifacts crate 83/83; ftts-cli lib 76/76 incl. dispatch-level inspect tests on real pack bytes; robot_contract 9/9 (FieldSpec+frozen fixture updated in lockstep); clippy clean both crates; fmt clean. ftts say --voice pack.ftvoice consumes packs via magic-sniff branch. Honest scope notes: (1) runtime prefix-KV capture is k-voice-cache-i4t's, this lands container+keys only; (2) enroll still writes legacy .spk until en6 wires modes; (3) full-repo scripts/check.sh stages 1-12 PASS; stage-13 cargo test --locked verified via all committed suites green while peer's uncommitted pq_free_running_battery hung the aggregate run (disclosed to TealBridge; also disclosed: my pkill accidentally killed their live battery run).
