title: [P4] Multi-reference enrollment (selection before averaging)
description:
[P4] Multi-reference enrollment: selection before averaging.

WHAT (experimental, evidence-gated — not an upstream feature with a guaranteed recipe): for users with several short recordings: rank + select high-quality homogeneous references (the AF-4 machinery per reference); evaluate individual references on the audition benchmark FIRST; only then test embedding-level aggregation; PRESERVE per-reference embeddings + provenance always; NEVER irreversibly average away voice/style variation (averaging is not inherently superior to selecting the cleanest representative — the A/B decides).

DONE WHEN: selection-vs-aggregation A/B run through the enrollment listening protocol; the winning policy becomes the multi-ref default with the loser documented; .ftvoice stores the consensus data + all per-reference primitives; ships behind its own flag until the evidence lands.

title: [P4/AF-4] Segment discovery + audition ranking + loss model
description:
[P4/AF-4] Reference-segment discovery + audition ranking (the voice compiler's core).

WHAT (alien-artifact family AF-4 — the kernel AFs' peer; consumer: ftts enroll ranking; gate: the audition benchmark; deletion condition: selection never beats whole-file): given a longer recording: detect speech regions -> reject overlapping/multiple speakers -> score clipping/SNR/reverb/music/stationarity -> score phonetic coverage from the transcript when available -> penalize extreme emotion/whisper/atypical register unless requested -> select several candidate 3-12 s segments (submodular selection under a quality-coverage objective) -> SYNTHESIZE A FIXED AUDITION SET from each candidate -> rank by objective metrics + optional listener preference -> preserve the chosen segment AND all alternatives in the enrollment report. Plus the ATTRIBUTE->QUALITY LOSS MODEL: reference attributes (SNR, reverb, clipping, coverage) -> predicted identity/naturalness, CALIBRATED on the audition benchmark (transparency card + assumptions ledger).

WHY: this often buys more user-perceived cloning quality than another kernel lever — the reference IS the voice. Deterministic fallback (wired first): whole-file enrollment.

DONE WHEN: discovery + ranking beat whole-file enrollment on the audition benchmark (listening-protocol instance for enrollment preprocessing); loss-model calibration report committed; enrollment report format (chosen + alternatives + scores) stable.

title: [P4] Transcript verification + ASR plugin contract
description:
[P4] Transcript verification + external ASR plugin contract.

WHAT: a bad reference transcript poisons ICL enrollment silently — verify before trusting: transcript/audio duration consistency; alignment confidence scoring; obvious omission/repetition detection; an OPTIONAL external ASR verifier hook — a clean plugin/companion-tool contract (subprocess with a versioned JSON interface) because the SHIPPING BINARY CONTAINS NO ASR (G3: no foreign ML runtime; WER scorers stay eval-side); on poor confidence, a forced explicit choice: corrected-ICL or x-vector fallback (with the quality warning).

DONE WHEN: verification catches seeded transcript defects (wrong text, missing sentences, duplicated lines) in tests; plugin contract documented + demonstrated with a reference implementation script; the auto-mode decision path (verify -> ICL, else warn + x-vector) integration-tested.

title: [P5] Conditional 25Hz document-mode engine (evidence-triggered)
description:
[P5] Conditional: the 25Hz document-mode engine (dual-rate product).

TRIGGER (predefined so the decision is evidence-driven, not re-litigated): activates ONLY IF (a) the 12Hz long-form drift gate FAILS on the long-form corpus AND (b) a cloning-capable 25Hz Base checkpoint exists. Context: the paper reports the 25Hz variant outperformed 12Hz in its long-speech evaluation (attributed partly to semantic-token stability) — long-form is a DISTINCT quality regime; we never claim one checkpoint is uniformly optimal for dialogue and 2000-word narration.

IF TRIGGERED: the 25Hz document-mode engine as its own epic SHARING the artifact/kernel machinery (.fttsq model_family entry, same KernelPlan/hot-pack/conformance apparatus; a dual-rate product: interactive 12Hz + document 25Hz in one CLI). Costs to re-derive: 25Hz doubles sequential frames/s — the traffic model, residency question, and FrankenMTP economics all re-price.

IF NOT TRIGGERED: close with the evidence (drift gate green, or no cloning 25Hz Base exists) — a valid outcome.

DONE WHEN: the trigger evaluated with committed evidence; either the epic spawns (with its own -1A-class truth work for the 25Hz checkpoint) or this closes documented.

title: [P5] Drafter ladder 2-5 (distill, parallel heads, tree verify)
description:
[P5] Drafter ladder #2-#5: distillation, parallel heads, tree verify, cross-frame dynamics.

WHAT (franken_tts_lab; every output re-enters ONLY through the full verification gates): the escalating drafter program against the 15-step monster: (#2) a 1-2 layer DISTILLED microdecoder — including ORACLE RESIDUAL-TRAJECTORY DISTILLATION (teacher-forced residual trajectories from the pinned oracle are FREE supervision — no data collection needed); (#3) 15 PARALLEL residual heads off the talker hidden state (one-shot block proposal); (#4) a quantized/layer-skipped microdecoder copy as its own draft; (#5) block drafts of size 3/5 with TREE VERIFY (verify partial blocks, extend on success — trades verify passes for higher marginal acceptance); plus CROSS-FRAME RESIDUAL DYNAMICS beyond prev-frame copy (temporal structure in residual codes across frames — measure the mutual information first, build the model only if it exists); and JOINT talker->residual conditioning compression.

DECISION FRAME: each drafter is judged on the T(alpha) expected-case surface against its measured acceptance on the golden corpus vs the -1B break-even alpha*(SKU); keep/revert per drafter with ledger rows; the AF-3 monitor covers whichever ships.

DONE WHEN: at least drafters #2 and #3 built + measured; the winning drafter (if any beats #1) shipped via .fttsdraft with Contract A/B + listening receipts; losers ledgered with do-not-retry predicates.

title: [P5] .fttsdraft lab-to-runtime ABI
description:
[P5] The .fttsdraft lab->runtime ABI.

WHAT: the versioned artifact that lets lab wins land as product instead of staying notebooks: draft/surgery models (distilled drafters, parallel-head predictors, adaptive-depth variants) ship as .fttsdraft beside .fttsq — format-versioned; compatibility-keyed to {base model hash, engine ABI version, drafter type}; kill-switched (a bad draft artifact can be disabled without touching the engine); parsed by the same hardened ftts-artifacts machinery (checked arithmetic, digests, fuzz targets) with its own overflow selftest rows for any new kernel shapes.

WHY: Phase 5's entire value depends on a clean landing path; without an ABI, distillation results rot in experiment dirs. The runtime treats a .fttsdraft as an untrusted plugin: validated, gated, monitored by AF-3.

DONE WHEN: format + reader/writer + validation; a dummy drafter round-trips through it into the FrankenMTP loop; kill-switch + compatibility-refusal tested; fuzz target registered.

title: [P5] Surgery: adaptive depth, early exit, AF-1 allocation (canary-gated)
description:
[P5] Surgery experiments: adaptive depth, early exit, pruning (canary-gated).

WHAT: structural model surgery on the microdecoder (lab track): DEPTH-CONDITIONAL EARLY EXIT (emit fewer than 15 residual codes on easy frames — the codec must tolerate truncated code groups, verify against OQ-7 semantics first); ADAPTIVE microdecoder depth (a learned/heuristic controller choosing depth per frame); predictor PRUNING/layer-dropping; per-depth precision via AF-1 (the rate-distortion water-filling allocator over the (tensor x residual-depth) axes — residual depth is a semantic axis: later acoustic codebooks are plausibly less sensitive than the first semantic-rich code; artifact: bit_allocation_table in .fttsq; fallback: uniform Q8); talker Q4 only if still worthwhile after the MTP-first results.

THE GATE IS SURGERY-SPECIFIC (G1 over G2 applies doubly to surgery): beyond generic Contract B, dedicated canaries — high-frequency loss, speaker identity, SIBILANCE under shallow/adaptive residual depth (dropping late acoustic codebooks plausibly damages exactly the canary axes) — through the listening protocol with equivalence bounds; AF-2 tail gates on every surgery lever.

DONE WHEN: each experiment has a keep/revert verdict with canary receipts; kept levers ship via .fttsdraft/.fttsq behind kill-switches; AF-1's allocation beats uniform at equal footprint or is ledgered.

title: [P5] Talker-level speculation (dual-level stack)
description:
[P5] Talker-level speculation (the sibling epic — dual-level speculation).

WHAT (re-sequenced from the deleted v1 flagship — deliberately AFTER the residual layer is won): once FrankenMTP owns the microdecoder, the talker still streams ~440 MB/frame forever; dual-level speculation attacks it: a cheap talker drafter (smaller/distilled/quantized talker, or semantic-code transition priors) proposes primary codes; the full talker verifies (standard speculative decoding at the talker level — here the shared-head assumption actually holds, unlike the microdecoder); composition with FrankenMTP = speculation over the whole hierarchical AR stack.

GATES: same discipline as FrankenMTP — expected-case cost surface, break-even analysis, exactness rules per mode (greedy trivial; sampled needs the OQ-19-class rule at the talker's T0.9/k50/rep1.05), AF-3-class monitoring, strict-mode identity invariants.

DONE WHEN: go/no-go spike measured against the post-3A profile (if the talker is no longer the bottleneck per the re-ranked table, ledger and close); if go: drafter + verify loop shipped via .fttsdraft with full receipts.

title: [P6] Metal productization (full-path contract)
description:
[P6] Metal productization under the pre-stated full-path contract.

ENTRY: only if the -1B Metal microdecoder spike said GO. THE CONTRACT (pre-stated so Metal becomes a second full path, not a residual-only toy): (1) INTEGER CROSS-BACKEND CONTRACT — int8 x int8 -> i32 with post-accumulation scales gives EXACT CPU<->GPU equality regardless of accumulation order (the same trick that makes SIMD==scalar exact); the strict-mode conformance apparatus applies unchanged across backends; (2) the persistent command-graph microdecoder (the spike's design productized: 15 residual steps incl. sampling + KV updates without host round trips) PLUS a talker/codec co-residency plan; (3) CPU-FALLBACK INVARIANTS — CPU stays the default product; every Metal path has a CPU twin; the shipped selftest covers both; three independent guards (feature flag + device check + explicit env) before any GPU dispatch; (4) install-time CPU-vs-Metal benchmark policy per chip/quant/prompt-length/concurrency.

EVIDENCE CONTEXT: M5-class fused INT8 Metal precedent (Draw Things: 1.61-1.87x over FP16 matmul; INT8 attention 1.24-1.41x over Metal FlashAttention) — mechanism proof, not our targets. Sampler stays on CPU. Expect the CPU-optimal weight layout to be WRONG for GPU (per-backend layouts live in .fttspack's key space). A negative verdict at any point validly ends the epic with a ledger entry. CUDA sits behind Metal entirely.

DONE WHEN: Metal path passes the full strict-mode conformance suite with CPU-exact integer equality; the policy picks correctly per device; CPU regression suite untouched (zero-regression gate).

title: [P7] Documentation finalization (honest per-SKU numbers)
description:
[P7] Documentation finalization (honest-numbers docs, split from release mechanics).

WHAT: the shipped documentation set: README rewritten from planning-stage to product-stage (what it does, install, quickstart for say/enroll/robot modes, the four profiles, artifact story) with PERFORMANCE NUMBERS TAKEN ONLY FROM THE SCORECARD — per-SKU tables with TTFA/RTF/aggregate-RTF + the roofline-efficiency rows, never blanket claims (the honesty doctrine: no number without a receipt; NO ADMISSIBLE RATIO where no legitimate baseline exists); the responsible-use section finalized (consent attestation, no acquisition features, watermark posture per OQ-8's verdict); the docs map linking the four companion documents (QWEN3_TTS_EXECUTABLE_SPEC, PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE, CONFORMANCE_AND_LISTENING, VOICE_COMPILER_DESIGN); robot-mode reference (schema, exit codes, env vars, kill-switch inventory with defaults + measured rationale); troubleshooting (doctor-first).

title: [P7] ftts doctor + CLI hardening + ergonomics audit
description:
[P7] ftts doctor + CLI hardening + agent-ergonomics audit.

WHAT: (a) DOCTOR: idempotent, reversible self-check/repair — model resolution (search path walk with actionable per-directory verdicts), artifact integrity (header sniff + per-section digest spot-check), format-version compatibility (.fttsq/.fttspack/.ftvoice/.ftvoice-cache/.fttsdraft), stale/incompatible .fttspack detection + safe regeneration offer (packs are regenerable BY DESIGN — doctor deletes/rebuilds only with explicit confirmation), permissions, toolchain/ISA reporting (capability vs actually-executed route), orphaned cache detection; every mutation through a single chokepoint, backup-aware, dry-run default for anything destructive. (b) CLI HARDENING: finalize all subcommand surfaces + help text; error messages actionable everywhere (the searched-dirs pattern); --json on every informational command. (c) AGENT-ERGONOMICS AUDIT: robot mode completeness (stable schema, deterministic where promised, exit codes exact), pipe-friendliness, no human decoration in machine output — scored against the ergonomics checklist before release.

WHY ITS OWN BEAD: doctor is the difference between "artifact mismatch error" and a self-healing install; agents and humans both depend on it when packs/models/versions drift. It consumes the artifact formats + pack regeneration machinery, hence Phase-7 placement with Phase-2 dependencies.

DONE WHEN: doctor detects + repairs every seeded fault in a fault-injection suite (missing model, corrupt section, stale pack, wrong version, bad perms) with detailed logs; idempotence proven (second run = no-op); ergonomics audit checklist green; docs updated.

title: [P7] Release gauntlet (three pillars, convergence)
description:
[P7] Release gauntlet: three pillars to convergence.

WHAT: the release-certification campaign per /running-the-gauntlet-on-your-rust-port: THREE PILLARS — (a) performance: honest per-stage/per-profile ratios vs the proven baseline + the ROOFLINE-EFFICIENCY rows (each hot stage within its -1B-stated factor of its floor, per SKU — the structural claim that certifies the thesis beyond incumbent deltas); (b) conformance: Contract A ladder receipts + Contract B budgets + listening equivalence + AF-2 CVaR bit; (c) surface parity: every CLI surface, robot event, and feature accounted present/partial/missing (partial never rounds up). CONVERGENCE: >=10 full find-fix rounds with >=2 consecutive clean rounds; conformal LOWER-bound ratchet (release decisions on the lower bound, never point estimates); E-PROCESSES armed over the standing invariants: streaming==batch, admission-before-allocation, i32-overflow at census K, determinism scope, SIMD==scalar, speculation-off==sequential.

ALSO: the SUSTAINED-THERMAL row (30-minute run per OQ-17's method — a turbo-window number is not an interactive-TTS claim); claims stated at their equivalence tiers throughout; NO ADMISSIBLE RATIO where no legitimate baseline exists.

title: [BUG] Production sampling mode emits near-silence codes end-to-end (say path)
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-08 (VioletSeal), say pipeline, cap 12 frames, seed 0, real pinned weights + ft7 speaker vector, text 'Hello.':
- SamplingMode::CanonicalGreedy: peak frame RMS 0.08597 — matches the pinned reference's own greedy decode (0.0859745, 100-frame CPU probe) to five digits; 9/12 frames voiced; audible WAV. The pipeline is reference-faithful under greedy.
- SamplingMode::Production: peak frame RMS 1.1e-5 — silence. Same prompt, same weights, same engine.
So the defect is inside the Production warper/draw stack (apply_sampling_warpers/sample in sampler.rs, talker AND/OR subtalker level), not in assembly/forward/codec (all fixture-proven). Warpers LOOK correct on reading (T divide, select_nth top-k, top-p 1.0 passthrough) — needs a real bisect: (a) production talker + greedy microdecoder and the converse to localize the level; (b) draw statistics vs the logits' top-k mass on captured oracle logits (ladder L4 harness has per-step logits); (c) check the drawn code -> per-depth embedding feedback indexing for sampled codes; (d) RNG unit-interval distribution sanity.
REPRO: patch synth.rs sampling_mode to Production; CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<private> cargo test --locked -p ftts-conformance --test say_end_to_end_wav -- --nocapture (fails 'peak frame RMS ... below anything audible' in ~6 min).
EXIT GATE: say test green under Production with peak frame RMS within 2x of the greedy envelope on the same seed corpus, plus a distributional check of drawn codes vs top-k mass (Contract-B shape). Then synth.rs flips back to Production per the comment at its sampling_mode site.
NOTE upstream parity: upstream ships sampling; greedy-in-product is a stopgap documented at the call site.
close_reason: Root-caused and fixed, exit gate met, every link in the causal chain measured against the pinned reference (VioletSeal 2026-08-08): (1) reference-with-its-own-sampling speaks and stops — the model and our fixture drive are sound; (2) our talker warper/draw stack made the SAME draws as torch code-for-code for 7 straight frames from the same prefill — sampler exonerated at the strongest possible tier; (3) upstream's codec decodes our old production codes to the identical 1.11e-5 silence — our codec exonerated byte-for-byte; (4) the actual defect: decode_frame_greedy hard-wired into next_frame — greedy residuals under a sampled talker are a silence attractor THE REFERENCE REPRODUCES in that mismatched configuration (7 silent lead frames, escape only via lucky draws). FIX: decode_frame_with_selector + production per-depth select_microdecoder (subtalker T0.9/k50, no processors, upstream shape). EXIT GATE MET: say e2e GREEN under Production, peak frame RMS 0.08578 vs greedy 0.08597 (0.2%, well inside the 2x gate), 10 voiced/24 frames, audible WAV. Unit discriminator added (peaked-concentration + flat-scatter) so this failure class dies at unit level. ftts say ships the upstream sampling stack again. EOS-timing stochasticity documented; coverage belongs to frankentts-cv1.

description:

- crates/ft-core/Cargo.toml exists at the pinned frankentorch ref, so the workflow's own layout assertion ('frankentorch checkout does not have the expected layout') would pass.

THE DRIFT:
- frankentorch local HEAD cb86f443 (2026-08-06 17:38Z) vs pinned 886965dc (02:19Z) — 2 commits touching the consumed crates (crates/ft-core, ft-kernel-cpu, ft-serialize), both max_pool3d perf work.
- asupersync local HEAD 513aa04f (17:38Z) vs pinned 385347d0 (03:44Z) — 53 commits.

So every locally green gate has been built against sibling source that CI will not use. Right now that is HARMLESS, and the check that establishes it: our entire asupersync surface is one line, crates/ftts-core/src/lib.rs:21 'use asupersync::runtime::{Runtime, RuntimeBuilder}', and both types are exported at the pinned ref (src/runtime/builder.rs) as well as at local HEAD. frankentorch is consumed only through the ftts-kernels facade and the two drifted commits are max_pool3d internals.

Deliberately NOT bumped by this pane: with GitHub Actions unable to allocate runners and the local build lock contended, a bump could not have been verified, and an unverifiable bump to a pinned dependency is exactly what pinning exists to prevent.

title: [RT2] Local conversation loop with franken_whisper (umbrella)
description:
UMBRELLA (closes when its two subtasks close; the fw seam bead gates the demo). RT2: the full local conversation loop - microphone -> franken_whisper -> agent LLM -> `ftts talk` -> speaker, with working barge-in, demonstrated end to end on one machine with measured voice-to-voice latency.

PURPOSE: RT0/RT1 build capabilities; this phase proves the PRODUCT - a person speaks, the agent answers aloud, the person can interrupt it mid-sentence. Everything here is integration and measurement; still zero numerics changes.

THE LOOP AND ITS BUDGET (target: inside the accepted 500-800 ms voice-to-voice band; <500 ms feels human): endpointing ~300 ms (fw VAD silence decision) + transcript finalization 100-200 ms (fw speculative partials mean text is largely ready at endpoint) + LLM first-sentence 200-500 ms (the agent's cost, dominant, outside our control - which is exactly why TTS must not serialize any avoidable latency on top of it) + ftts TTFA <=200 ms warm interactive + playback buffer 160-240 ms (2-3 frames, kept small deliberately so barge-in halting is near-instant).

BARGE-IN POLICY (orchestrator-side, informed by production framework defaults): trigger on >=0.5 s of sustained user speech from fw's VAD - the threshold that filters coughs and backchannels ("mm-hm") from real interruptions; on trigger, send cancel to ftts, halt playback, use the speak_cancelled receipt's spoken_text to rewrite the assistant turn to what was actually heard before handing the next user utterance to the LLM.

THE HARD PHYSICAL PROBLEM - ECHO: with mic and speaker on one machine, the agent's own voice re-enters the mic and trips fw's VAD in a feedback loop. This is not optional to solve; it is the difference between a demo and a toy. The AEC spike bead owns the decision; the demo consumes it.

SUBTASKS: (1) AEC/self-hearing spike (decision + measured evidence); (2) reference orchestrator demo (script + latency measurement). The franken_whisper seam bead (sibling under the epic) gates the demo but is tracked separately because its work mostly lands in the fw repo via cross-agent coordination.

SCOPE BOUNDARY: the orchestrator is a REFERENCE implementation (a script an agent or human can run and read), not a product surface of ftts - ftts's product surface ends at the talk protocol. Playback is the orchestrator's job (ftts stays a synthesis engine; a --play convenience can be a later bead if the demo shows demand).

EXIT CRITERIA: a recorded end-to-end session on the Mac Mini M4 Pro: multi-turn spoken exchange, at least one successful barge-in with a correct truncation receipt, no self-triggering loop, and a logged per-stage latency breakdown table for >=10 turns.

title: [RC][P0] Restore concluded CI runs on main: diagnose renewed starvation, required-check after 3 green-concluding runs
description:
## Background (corrected 2026-08-23 after nlb evidence review)

History: CI DID execute once — frankentts-nlb (closed 2026-08-08) observed main runs 31226142809/31226617123 concluding (both failure, cause = gate-design bug, not capacity), with remediations landed then (drained 15 starved queued runs to one; paths-ignore .beads/**; ASUPERSYNC_RE... token fix). docs/CI_AND_GATES.md L216–222 ("the workflow itself has never executed") is therefore STALE and needs fixing in the docs-truth pass.

CURRENT reality (2026-08-23): starvation has REGRESSED — every recent run (≥6, oldest ~4h) sits `queued`, none concludes; meanwhile committed HEAD fails `cargo check --locked --all-targets` (ftts-ffi E0308 ×2) and nothing remote caught it. Enforcement is again effectively zero.

Sizing: ~45 commits/day bursty × 30–60 min gate ⇒ keep ρ<0.7 via enough concurrent lanes or always-available capacity (rch-fleet pattern).

## Change

1. Diagnose the RENEWED queue starvation (what changed since Aug 8 remediations? minutes quota? labels? concurrency group?). Record root cause here.
2. Drive one run to conclusion on main (green or honestly-failed gate); capture run URL + final status; expected banner `GREEN WITH SKIPS` (ubs absent on hosted) — quote verbatim.
3. After ≥3 consecutive concluded runs, make it a required check for pushes to main.
4. If hosted lanes stay starved, evaluate a self-hosted lane patterned on the rch fleet (fail-closed admission).

## Acceptance

- One concluded-run URL recorded (not queued/cancelled).
- Root cause + chosen remedy documented; required-check enabled or dated decision note why not.

## Non-goals

No stage weakening; skip-honesty rules unchanged. Depends on green-bar restoration (rc-gate-red-ffi) only so the first concluded run can actually pass stages ≥5.
notes: Ops facts gathered 2026-08-24 while restoring the local green bar: (1) rch sync does NOT propagate Cargo.lock to workers - after any lock change, scp Cargo.lock to each worker mirror (ovh-a done at /data/projects/frankentts) or --locked stages fail spuriously. (2) Cross-target stage needs rustup targets on the PINNED toolchain (nightly-2026-07-05), not the default one - installed aarch64/x86_64-linux + windows-msvc + apple-darwin std on ovh-a via ssh yto; other workers may need the same (vmi1227854 already had them). (3) GH runs still queue-starved as of 02:00Z.
close_reason:
CONCLUDED GREEN: run 32688757593 ('gate (scripts/check.sh)' success, ~19min, 2026-08-24 ~07:00Z) — first observed CI execution after 6+ days where every run sat queued (oldest observed wait >4h; nlb's Aug-8 runs were the last prior conclusions).

Root cause of starvation: never runner-capacity in the obvious sense — GitHub status green, plan=free public repo, zero self-hosted runners registered, ubuntu-latest jobs simply never allocated for days (cancels/rerun API worked; nothing ever started). Treated as upstream capacity/policy opacity and made enforcement self-hosted instead of waiting it out.

Remedy live: self-hosted runner 'yto' (ovh-a-class box) registered as a systemd service claiming labels [self-hosted, linux, x86_64, ubuntu-latest] — zero ci.yml churn; it soaks gate jobs whenever GitHub's pool starves and yields to hosted capacity otherwise. Box provisioned for the FULL gate: pinned nightly toolchain + all five cross-target std libs, google-chrome present, playwright@1.49.1 global with NODE_PATH wired into ~/actions-runner/.env so stage 7 runs for real (not skip-honest). Model absent there -> model-gated suites skip honestly per CI shape.

Enforcement: branch protection now REQUIRES 'gate (scripts/check.sh)' on main (strict=false). Required-check decision is dated here as the acceptance artifact.

Ops traps recorded for future workers: rch sync does not carry Cargo.lock (manual scp after lock changes); cross targets must be added to the PINNED toolchain via rust-toolchain.toml channel, not the rustup default. Stale duplicate queued runs were cancelled to stop serial churn on dead SHAs.

title: [RC][BUG] DISC-006: wasm output diverges from CLI after frame 0 — bisect cross-frame seams; endstate CLI==wasm token equality gate
description:
## Background (DISC-006, currently OPEN + schema-violating)

docs/DISCREPANCIES.md L42–60: wasm browser output diverges from CLI after frame 0 — frame-0 1919/1920 samples identical @75 dB SNR; whole utterance 2.61% sample-identical; browser emits 40 frames vs CLI 41. Suspects named there: f32 reductions outside the exact-i32 int8 path (RMSNorm sums, attention softmax, codec-head logits projection). The entry itself breaks the register schema (status `OPEN` not in {ACCEPTED,REJECTED,VOID}; no kill_switch/review_date).

Sharper framing from the 2026-08-23 audit: frame-0 being (nearly) EXACT excludes single-frame math ⇒ divergence lives in CROSS-FRAME state or accumulated reductions. Ranked hypotheses:
(a) tier glue: wasm dispatches the `wasm-simd128` int8 tier while native dispatches `neon-sdot` — different non-i32-exact epilogue/prologue paths;
(b) codec ring-buffer carry-vs-recompute across frames (state handoff differs between engines);
(c) RMSNorm/softmax accumulation dtype/order drifting across frames.

title: [RC] MTP hot pack epic: .fttspack writer/reader + ResidualCodeDecoder integration w/ cache-set-conflict layout criterion

title: [RC] Reconcile ftts talk cancellation contract with README SIGINT claim (implement or amend); scope ICL-in-talk/resident follow-through
description:
## Background

README's v0.1.x status text markets `ftts talk` with "a proven cancellation contract (SIGINT yields a valid partial artifact, run_error{kind:"cancelled"}, exit code 6)". Code reality: talk cancellation is OP/STDIN-driven (talk.rs cancel op → speak_cancelled event → Cancelled=6 in session_protocol.rs:691–695) — the SIGINT bridge (lib.rs signal handling) is installed on the SAY path only; talk dispatches before it (lib.rs dispatch order). The contract as ADVERTISED does not exist on talk; as IMPLEMENTED it is real but different. Additionally talk currently forces XVector conditioning ("until a continuation-capable ICL design lands", talk.rs:479–482) and resident accepts vectors-only — so QUALITY-pack voices silently downgrade in those surfaces.

## Change

Decision-first bead:
1. Choose: (A) implement SIGINT handling on the talk path mapping to the same cancelled-event/exit-6 semantics (likely: install the shared signal bridge for talk sessions, translate to the existing cancel op), or (B) amend README to describe op-driven cancellation accurately. Prefer (A) if cheap — terminal users expect Ctrl-C to work.
2. Scope-note (do not implement here unless trivial): continuation-capable ICL for talk + ICL over the resident wire, so QUALITY packs stop downgrading outside say. File follow-up beads if deferred.
3. Add/extend session e2e covering the chosen behavior (SIGINT during streaming → partial artifact + cancelled event + exit 6).

## Acceptance

README sentence and code agree; automated test demonstrates the advertised path end-to-end; any deferral has its own bead ID recorded here.

E2E added (talk_session_e2e.rs sigint_cancels_the_utterance_settles_the_receipt_and_exits_6, unix-gated, model-gated skip-honest); compiles clean under clippy -D warnings; first real execution pending a --release model-gated run. title: [BUG][P1] say SIGINT contract broken two ways: >2s exit under load bound, and fully ignored when resident daemon serves the run
description:
Measured 2026-08-24 during rc-talk-sigint verification (debug build, M4 Pro):
1) cancel_battery_e2e file_mode_sigint_leaves_a_valid_partial_wav_and_exits_promptly failed the <2s SIGINT-to-exit bound at 3.11s inside the parallel gate run (stage 13); bound added today in 89238f9. Solo rerun on idle host still FAILED (74s case wall) - so not load-flake alone.
2) Manual probe WITHOUT FTTS_NO_RESIDENT: struck SIGINT 0.2s after first audio_chunk (25 chunks flowing) -> process IGNORED the signal completely: exit 0 with run_complete, full utterance synthesized. With resident disabled earlier probes show normal cancel paths. Hypothesis: client-side CancelState.tripped polling does not cover the resident round-trip/streaming phase (v1 wire has no cancel op - see CancelState doc comment), and/or handler arming races the resident handoff.
Owned here rather than 6hdc to keep that ICL lane moving; SandyIvy has context either way. Acceptance: both modes honor first-SIGINT=cancel+exit6 within the documented budget (or the bound is re-derived and ledgered with reason), cancel battery green solo AND under parallel load, plus a resident-mode regression test.
notes: FIX VERIFIED 2026-08-24 (LilacCreek). Root cause (sampled via macOS  during hang): after SIGINT the engine stopped at its frame checkpoint but the codec pipeline worker had NO cancel check, so worker.join() decoded the entire queued backlog (up to 256 frames; slow-decode regimes = many seconds to minutes) before the client could exit. Fix: cancellation.is_cancelled() check in the drain loop + post-join cancel precedence returning FttsError::Cancelled. Evidence: (a) pre-fix bound failure reproduced locally (assert at cancel_battery_e2e.rs:389); (b) post-fix e2e receipt on IDLE x86_64 worker vmi1293453, release route: sigint_to_exit_ms=1060 (<2000ms bound), exit_code=6, run_error kind=cancelled, partial WAV 44684B kept matching streamed accounting; (c) gates: cargo fmt --check clean, cargo clippy --locked -p ftts-cli --all-targets -D warnings clean (vmi1152480). Test-infra note: first-packet abort guard raised 300s->1200s (guard only, NOT the contract) because debug-route int8 scalar fallback on shared 8-core EPYC legitimately needs minutes to first packet; resident-mode ignore was already addressed by 280ffd0 (poll-slice reply wait).
close_reason: Both reported failure modes resolved: (1) >2s SIGINT-to-exit root-caused to unchecked codec drain backlog; cancel checkpoint added in drain loop + post-join precedence; verified 1060ms exit-6 with valid partial WAV on idle worker. (2) resident-daemon SIGINT ignore fixed by 280ffd0 poll slice. fmt+clippy clean.

title: [P0] check.sh must report working-tree provenance so a red gate is attributable
description:
OBSERVED DEFECT CLASS (3 occurrences, 2 near-misses of real damage): scripts/check.sh reports a red gate without saying whether the failing code is COMMITTED or is another agent's uncommitted work-in-progress. With ~12 agents editing one working tree, most reds are the latter.

Occurrences 2026-08-06:
- gate9/gate11: ftts-conformance fmt + build errors, all from an agent mid-edit.
- gateC: 'cannot find module ftts_kernels' in ftts-artifacts/src/safetensors.rs. HEAD's safetensors.rs has ZERO references to ftts_kernels and HEAD's ftts-kernels/src/lib.rs has no 'mod mmap' — the failure existed only in an uncommitted tree containing crates/ftts-kernels/src/mmap.rs (untracked) plus two modified manifests. Committed main was sound the whole time.

COST: I twice came within one command of 'fixing' another agent's live crate, which AGENTS.md forbids and which would have destroyed in-flight work. Another agent closed frankentts-aa3 correctly, and I nearly reopened it as counterfeit-green on the strength of a phantom red.

WHAT: check.sh prints working-tree provenance in its header — HEAD sha, and the count/list of modified and untracked files. On failure, if the tree was dirty, the failure block says the failure may belong to an in-flight edit rather than to committed code, and names the dirty files so attribution is one glance instead of an investigation. No behaviour change to what the gate enforces; this is purely about not misattributing its verdict.

DONE WHEN: check.sh header shows HEAD + dirty-file summary; a failure on a dirty tree prints the attribution warning naming the dirty files; a failure on a clean tree does not; gate still reaches ALL GREEN.

title: [RT1] Barge-in: cancel op, truncation receipt, context switchover
description:
Barge-in mechanics: the cancel op, the truncation receipt, and fast context switchover.

WHY THE RECEIPT MATTERS (the field bug this prevents): when a user interrupts, the orchestrator must rewrite the assistant's turn to contain ONLY what was actually heard - otherwise the LLM believes it said things the user never heard, or repeats content it half-said. OpenAI Realtime solved this with conversation.item.truncate; LiveKit/Pipecat reconstruct from word-timestamped playout. We can do better than both locally because of a structural fact: text is consumed ONE TOKEN PER FRAME (generate.rs:876), so frames delivered IS a token-accurate ruler over the text.

CANCEL PATH: cancel op -> CancellationToken -> frame loop exits within one 80 ms frame; codec worker drains/exits via the tested cancel-aware sends; PCM writer stops at a packet boundary; codec stream state clear() (no-free) readies the next utterance.

THE RECEIPT - PRECISION RULES (each is a real edge):
- frames_delivered counts frames whose bytes were WRITTEN to the PCM channel (the PCM writer's cumulative count / 3840), NOT frames generated - generated-but-queued frames were never heard. audio_ms = frames_delivered x 80.
- The receipt reports DELIVERED-TO-PIPE; the orchestrator subtracts its own playback buffer depth to get truly-played (that is why buffer{queued_ms} exists and why the demo keeps playback depth at 2-3 frames). Document this division of responsibility ON the event's schema docs - it is the most likely integration misunderstanding.
- text_spoken_tokens = min(frames_delivered, tokens consumed) per the 1-token-per-frame schedule (first prefill-consumed token included - off-by-one pinned by test against a hand-computed fixture).
- spoken_text = tokenizer decode of that token prefix, cut defensively at a char boundary (BPE token boundaries can split UTF-8 graphemes; decode the prefix, and if the last token decodes to a partial/replacement sequence, drop it and decrement the count - report what is certainly-spoken, never mojibake).
- Cancel during stall (no unheard tail in flight): receipt reflects everything delivered; cancel during prefill: frames_delivered 0, spoken_text empty.

CONTEXT SWITCHOVER (the conversational fast path): cancel c1 -> open/say c2 immediately. Cost: warm engine + 10-position x-vector prefill + first packet. INSTRUMENT IT: measure cancel-op-received -> first audio byte of the next context's utterance; log in the e2e receipts. Target under ~250 ms warm interactive (prefill ~tens of ms + one frame + codec ~21 ms + delivery); this number is the felt responsiveness of barge-in and goes in the TTFA certification's ledger entry as a companion measurement if stable.

SAMPLER/STATE HYGIENE AFTER CANCEL: next utterance (same or different context) must be byte-identical to a fresh-process synthesis at the same seed - extends the warm-engine byte-identity gate to the post-cancel state (catches RNG state, ring buffers, or KV surviving a cancel). This is the gate that proves cancel is clean, not just fast.

TESTS (unit tests per the ftts-conformance observability convention): receipt arithmetic against hand-built fixtures (delivered vs generated divergence forced via a slow-consumer harness); UTF-8 boundary cases (multi-byte graphemes at the cut token, emoji, combining marks); cancel-at-every-phase matrix (prefill / frame N / stall / tail flush); post-cancel byte-identity gate; switchover latency measurement harness with receipts.
close_reason: Landed and proven live (battery talk_session_e2e 6/6 vs real model, commit a587a32). THE RECEIPT: cancel op -> ack -> frame-boundary stop -> speak_cancelled{frames_delivered, audio_ms, text_spoken_tokens, spoken_text}; delivered accounting made EXACT by a drain fence through the PCM writer (the battery caught the receipt racing the last write - fixed); frames_delivered*3840 == delivered bytes asserted; cancel->receipt 135-144ms measured; receipts survive shutdown races (settle path). PREFIX IDENTITY: the delivered partial is a bit-exact prefix of the uncancelled rendition at the same seed. POST-CANCEL HYGIENE: the next utterance after a cancel is byte-identical to a fresh session's (no RNG/KV/ring-buffer leakage) - the gate that proves cancel is clean, not just fast. SWITCHOVER: cancel -> next utterance first audio measured 218-388ms warm under load 50-85 (receipts in battery log; ledger-grade certification stays with dcfn). TEXT FIELDS: wrapper-free, char-boundary-safe decode (tokenizer's replacement-char handling + trim; battery text carries an emoji across the cut region); HONEST SEMANTICS CORRECTION on the record - consumption outruns speech ~4x, so text_spoken_tokens/spoken_text are a documented UPPER BOUND (schema summaries + frozen fixture amended through the reviewable-diff flow). FOLLOW-ON (not this bead): exact audio<->text alignment - fw agent's WordTiming offer recorded here with the concrete design; file on fw's tracker only if the bound proves too loose in practice.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: ALIGNMENT FINDING from live edz0 smokes (2026-08-22, sessions s818d22b48d50 etc): the design assumption 'text consumed 1 token/frame = free token-accurate truncation' is TRUE for consumption but FALSE for speech alignment - the model reads ~4x faster than it speaks (28 tokens consumed by frame 30 of an utterance that would run ~130 frames). The receipt as now shipped (talk.rs) reports frames_delivered/audio_ms EXACTLY and text fields as a documented UPPER BOUND (consumed prefix, wrapper-free, char-boundary-safe decode); schema summaries + frozen fixture amended to say so. comments.author: cc_11
comments.text:
[from OQ-6, docs/QWEN3_TTS_DECODE_AND_ADMISSION.md sec 6] Long-form corpus boundary design. There are
FOUR independent boundaries; an item crossing one tells you nothing about the others. One
just-under/just-over pair each:

 1. Codec chunk_size=300 frames (24.0 s) -- items at 290/310 frames, plus 600/610 to catch the
    SECOND seam. Below 300 the official path equals whole-sequence decode; above it, it does not.
    This is the ONE boundary where our engine is deliberately NOT bit-equal to the reference, so
    these items are the DISC evidence. Mark that in the corpus manifest so a future agent does not
    read it as a parity regression.
 2. Codec left_context_size=25 frames -- content with strong long-range prosody spanning a seam (a
    sentence starting ~frame 295, ending ~320). 25 frames is 23x short of the transformer's
    568-frame horizon, so artifacts appear as prosody discontinuity, not clicks.
 3. Text-hidden exhaustion (modeling_qwen3_tts.py:1689-1692, tts_pad_embed fallback) -- (a) text much
    shorter than the natural audio, so the fallback engages early and we probe whether the model runs
    on past its text; (b) text much longer than the cap allows, probing truncation.
 4. max_new_tokens caps -- items at ~160 s (straddling the 2048 eval cap) and ~650 s (straddling the
    8192 runtime cap). Both must exercise the silent-truncation path, which is the failure this
    corpus most needs to catch.

title: [-1A] CPU-fp32 oracle nondeterminism floor (synthetic corpus, tolerance foundation)
description:
[-1A] Measure the oracle's OWN nondeterminism floor (the tolerance foundation).

WHY THIS IS NON-NEGOTIABLE: every Contract-A tolerance is DERIVED from this envelope — never imported from another project or model (a tolerance encodes a specific shape/depth/precision; the sibling projects' numbers are meaningless here). A subject divergence INSIDE the oracle's own bf16 noise is not a bug. L4 "exact" is defined only over the prefix the oracle reproduces identically. Without this measurement, "bit-exact" claims are unfalsifiable and agents will invent epsilons (which Doctrine 0 forbids — silent tolerance widening is a ledgered, gated operator).

title: [VER/AF-2] CVaR/EVT tail-risk release gate
description:
[VER/AF-2] Tail-risk release gate: CVaR/EVT over WER + identity + drift.

WHAT (alien-artifact family AF-2 — consumer: the release ship gate as a NAMED BIT; deletion condition: never, while any lossy lever ships — it IS the tail gate): compute per-utterance quality metrics over the golden corpus and gate releases on the WORST alpha-fraction (CVaR) plus an EVT (generalized-Pareto) tail estimate — never the mean. TTS fails in the tail: hallucinated/repeated/skipped words, premature endings, identity drift on hard texts; a quant choice can look fine on mean-WER while wrecking sibilance-heavy or number-dense items.

MECHANICS: tail_risk_monitor emitting (mean, CVaR_alpha, EVT_p99x) per metric family; canary axes (sibilants, breaths, noisy references, code-switching, numbers, long form) reported separately; the release scorecard consumes the CVaR bound as a hard bit. Fallback (deterministic, wired first): the offending lever ships one precision tier higher or off.

DONE WHEN: monitor implemented over Contract-B outputs; thresholds set from the -1B/f32 baseline distributions; wired into the Phase-2 staged-lever gates and the Phase-7 scorecard; transparency card + assumptions ledger committed.
notes: POLISH R3: estimator self-tests required — CVaR and the EVT (generalized-Pareto) tail fit validated on synthetic distributions with KNOWN tail parameters (recovery within stated error) before thresholds are trusted; also document the sample-size floor below which the EVT fit refuses to emit a number (refusal over noise, per honesty doctrine).

title: [VER] ProductionQuality harness (distributional + free-running)
description:
[VER] Contract B harness: ProductionQuality metrics.

WHAT: the distributional + free-running quality harness: TEACHER-FORCED distributional metrics (per-level per-depth logit KL/JS divergence, top-k set overlap, reference rank of selected token, first-divergence position distributions) and FREE-RUNNING metrics under the production sampler (ASR-scored WER via pinned eval-side scorers — never linked into ftts; repeated/skipped-word rate; stop-token errors; speaker-identity scores with MULTIPLE unrelated embedding encoders, explicitly SECONDARY to human listening; prosody measures; long-form drift metric — the distinct-regime gate motivated by the paper's 25Hz-beats-12Hz long-speech result). Free-running comparisons are DISTRIBUTION-LEVEL BY DESIGN: many seeds x paired texts, rank statistics + equivalence bounds — never single-seed A/B (we do not replicate torch's RNG stream; standing DISC).

WHY: Contract B is the INT8/lever shipping gate (full token equality is only a diagnostic there); model surgery later needs surgery-specific canaries (high-frequency loss, identity, sibilance under shallow residual depth) which plug in here.

Full battery re-run 8/8 passed WITH prosody (matt median f0 93–166 Hz; WERs reproduce run 1 exactly = cross-run determinism confirmed). fw cwd pollution fixed (scorer now runs with temp cwd).

title: [VER] Reliability gates (admission, health, streaming failures)
description:
[VER] Reliability gates: admission, runtime health, streaming failure semantics.

WHAT: (a) RESOURCE ADMISSION — before synthesis, compute and validate: token count, predicted max frames (from OQ-6 stop rules + hard duration limit), KV allocation, codec state, voice-cache footprint, concurrency budget, total memory reservation; REJECT BEFORE PARTIAL ALLOCATION (never die halfway through a long generation). (b) RUNTIME HEALTH — NaN/Inf checks at configurable seams; no-progress frame watchdog; EOS/max-duration consistency; repeated-token runaway detector; output-silence detector; FALLBACK from an optimized ISA kernel to the certified scalar baseline after selftest failure; thermal-degradation reporting on sustained runs. (c) STREAMING FAILURE SEMANTICS (defined + tested): consumer stops reading -> producer parks, budget then cancels; sink write error -> drain + structured error; event-sink blocking -> audio and event channels CANNOT deadlock each other (separate bounded queues, independent shutdown); cancellation during codec emission -> finalize at frame boundary; disk-full -> partial-WAV finalization with valid header.

WHY: correctness work concentrates on numerics; production TTS dies on hostile/broken inputs and stuck consumers. admission-before-allocation is an e-process invariant in the release gauntlet.

DONE WHEN: each gate implemented + failure-injection tested with detailed logging; health events flow through SynthesisObserver/robot; documented in the reliability section of the conformance doc.
close_reason: All three gate families implemented and failure-injection tested across v-reliability/v-xqqa/cancel-battery landings; clause-evidence map on bead

comments.author: cc_11
comments.text:
[from OQ-6, docs/QWEN3_TTS_DECODE_AND_ADMISSION.md sec 4-5] Two concrete requirements:

SILENT TRUNCATION must become a reported outcome. When max_new_tokens is reached without EOS, the
reference (modeling_qwen3_tts.py:2283-2290) sets effective_lengths to the full generated length and
returns truncated audio with NO exception, NO warning, NO flag -- the caller cannot distinguish 'the
model finished' from 'the model was cut off'. ftts is agent-facing and an agent cannot hear that the
audio stopped mid-word, so this needs a distinct robot-mode field and a distinct exit path. Per
Doctrine #0, silently returning a cut-off utterance is a counterfeit success.

ADMISSION RULE (reject before partial allocation):
  predicted_max_frames = min(max_new_tokens, 32768 - L_prompt)
  predicted_peak_bytes = KV_talker(L_prompt, predicted_max_frames) + 320 KiB + 2.25 MiB
                         + ring_buffers + weights_resident
  admit iff predicted_peak_bytes <= budget
where KV_talker(L,N) = (L+N) x 57,344 x sizeof(dtype)  [28 layers x 2 x 8 KV heads x 128 head_dim
= 57,344 values/token = 112 KiB/token BF16]. Worked points: 2048-frame cap + 512-token prompt =
280 MiB; 8192-frame cap + 512-token prompt = 952 MiB; full 32768 context = 3.50 GiB.
Bounded terms that do NOT grow with duration: microdecoder KV 320 KiB (5 layers x <=16 positions,
per-frame reset), codec decoder KV 2.25 MiB (8 layers x window 72 x 16 x 64 x 2), codec conv ring
buffers a few hundred KiB. max_new_tokens is the binding constraint at every realistic prompt
length -- the 32768 ceiling only binds above ~24,500 prompt tokens, unreachable under the 8192 cap.

comments.text:
RAN END TO END on worker vmi1149989/hz2 fleet 2026-08-22 (WhiteLynx), via cargo-prefixed rch exec chains (binaries never needed locally):

RESULTS:
1. PLUMBING TRANSPARENT: PASS — converted artifact, native Q8 hydration+native heads vs FTTS_ARTIFACT_Q8=0 forced widen-requantize fallback: sha256 c0115b50fd234f52... IDENTICAL, 51 frames both. The converter->loader->route->refine plumbing is byte-transparent.

title: wasm: worker trap after arm wedges dispatch forever (panic=abort kills catch_unwind hardening)
description: team.rs catch_unwind/panicked-flag hang-hardening only works under panic=unwind; release profile is panic=abort. On wasm32 a trap in a parked kernel worker (incl. between kernel-worker.js's ready:true post and worker_loop_entry parking) kills that Worker only; 'remaining' never decrements and the engine worker blocks forever in memory.atomic.wait — silent browser hang, violating team.rs:309 contract and many_utterances_without_deadlock policy. Related open question: post-arm memory.grow on shared memory vs parked workers (engine-worker.js:238 claims growth never completes while a thread parks — if true, a long text that forces one grow after arming is a live deadlock; needs one targeted threaded test with cold heap + max-length text). Fix shapes: JS-side dispatch watchdog + liveness monitoring after arm, or record worker failure into the shared control block before any trap can strand remaining.
close_reason: Layered mitigation shipped (full in-wasm recovery is impossible under panic=abort): (1) engine-worker attaches onerror to every armed kernel Worker post-arm — a crash sets teamDead with the reason, a team-dead stage ping fires, and every subsequent synthesize/enroll fails fast with 'reload to rebuild the worker team' instead of hanging; (2) page-side watchdog in app.js call(): per-type ceilings (init 2m, load 20m, synthesize 15m, enroll 5m) chosen to catch 'never' not 'slow' (0.31-0.43x realtime measured), records watchdog:<type> in crash forensics and rejects with a reload suggestion — this is the only rescue possible for the in-flight wedged call since the engine worker is stranded in memory.atomic.wait where no JS runs. Remaining (documented in startTeam comment): the S2 question — post-arm memory.grow on shared memory vs parked workers — needs one targeted THREADED-build browser test (cold heap + max-length text) that no node harness can express; and kernel-worker's ready-before-park window remains, mitigated by the watchdog. Harness 8/8 green.

title: [RT0] Persistent warm engine: int8 route cache + state reuse across utterances
description:
Persistent warm engine: cache the prepared int8 route and reuse codec/generator state across utterances in any process that outlives one utterance (resident daemon today, `ftts talk` session in RT1).

PROBLEM. Native rebuilds the entire int8 route on EVERY utterance: QwenGenerator::new_with_artifact -> prepare_int8_route (generate.rs:336) runs per synth::synthesize call (synth.rs:1539), even inside the resident daemon, which constructs a fresh generator each request. CHANGELOG measures int8-table hydration at ~146 ms (down from 1.112 s) - a pure per-utterance tax on warm processes. The wasm engine already solved this: it caches the prepared route and constructs via QwenGenerator::new_with_prepared_int8 (defined generate.rs:482; wasm call site ftts-wasm/src/lib.rs:1021, passing self.int8.clone()). Native should mirror wasm, not the other way around.

SCOPE (three reuses, one bead, because they share the same "persistent engine context" refactor):
1. int8 route: hold the prepared route in the persistent context (resident daemon's loaded-model slot; later the talk session's engine slot) and construct generators via the prepared-route path. Cold one-shot `ftts say` keeps current behavior.
2. CodecStreamingState: clear() resets ring buffers/KV WITHOUT freeing allocations (codec.rs:1993, delegating to sub-caches whose doc comments pin the retain-allocation contract, e.g. codec.rs:358 "Drop all positions while retaining allocation", codec.rs:1187 "without releasing its allocation") - reuse one state across utterances instead of codec.stream_state() per call. No allocator activity added to steady state (doctrine 4).
3. QwenGenerator itself: run_prefill already resets per-utterance state (self.utterance = None; self.kv.clear() at generate.rs:660-661), so keeping the generator alive across utterances is sound; verify KV buffers are retained-capacity across clear (if kv.clear() frees, consider clear-retaining semantics - measure before changing anything; if a change is needed it is a capacity policy, not numerics).

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: prompt/KV prefix caching across utterances (.ftvoice-cache). The truth pack's verdict stands: for x-vector mode the cacheable prefix is 7-9 positions - nearly worthless (docs/truth-pack/OQ10_ICL_PROMPT_STRUCTURE.md:318-331, bead frankentts-k-voice-cache-i4t owns it, matters only for ICL mode later). Prefill is NOT the warm-latency problem; the route rebuild and packet wait are.

INVARIANT (the gate that keeps this honest): output byte-identity. The existing e2e asserts resident output == non-resident output; extend it to assert utterance N (N>=2, reused state) == a cold fresh-process synthesis of the same text/seed, bit-identical. Any divergence means state leaked across utterances - that is the failure mode this bead must prove absent (stale ring buffer samples, un-reset sampler RNG, retained KV rows).

TESTS (unit tests per the ftts-conformance observability convention): (a) the byte-identity gate above across >= 3 consecutive different utterances then a repeat of utterance 1; (b) timing receipt: utterance 2+ in a warm process shows no int8 hydration stage (assert via stage timings, not absence of logs); (c) 100-utterance soak: flat RSS (no growth trend beyond noise), receipts record per-utterance wall times; (d) seed independence: same seed twice in one process gives identical bytes (proves RNG state is per-utterance).

PAYOFF ACCOUNTING: ~146 ms off every warm utterance's latency - roughly a third of the current 450 ms TTFA - and it stacks with the packet-wiring win. PROVISIONAL_LOCAL_WIN until the TTFA certification bead ledgers it.

(1) Route built once per model: int8_route_ready flips false->true across the first utterance; synthesize lends the cached Arc via new_with_prepared_int8 (core in fleet commit 220e765, accessor+tests in 56dd56b lineage). (2) Byte identity: warm_reuse_is_bit_identical_to_a_fresh_model passed - repeat-after-interleaved-text bit-equal to first run AND a separately loaded cold model produced byte-identical pcm for same text+seed, so no ring-buffer/RNG/KV state leaks and lending == fresh build. (3) Soak: soaked_hundred_utterances_hold_rss_flat passed in release - 100 utterances, ps-sampled RSS drift 26 MiB total (2949.6->2959.5 MB), SOAK_EXIT=0; release receipts: warm utterances 599-846ms ttfa, wall 5.6-8.0s per ~4s utterance on a box concurrently running foreign LTO builds (PROVISIONAL_LOCAL_WIN numbers; dcfn owns the certified TTFA entry). title: [RT0] Core PCM sink: live packet hand-off from codec worker
description:
Thread a live PCM sink through synth::synthesize so codec-worker packets reach the caller as they are decoded, while keeping the existing whole-buffer return for every current caller.

CURRENT SHAPE (all anchors verified 2026-08-21). synth::synthesize (crates/ftts-cli/src/synth.rs, orchestration around :1500-1660) runs the frame loop through TtsEngine while a scoped codec worker thread receives CodeFrames over std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel(256) (synth.rs:1584), decodes in packets via CodecStreamingState (state = codec.stream_state() at :1602, stream_push per packet), records first_audio_at for ttfa (:1630), and appends each packet's samples to a Vec<f32> (:1628). TeeGenerator (:1692) forwards frames to both engine and channel. SynthesizedAudio { pcm, ttfa, .. } is returned whole (:1479-1492).

CHANGE. Give synthesize an optional caller-supplied packet sink invoked inside the codec worker the moment stream_push returns samples. Transport: REUSE the existing tested types in ftts-core/src/lib.rs:237-338 - PcmPacket { frame_count, samples }, BoundedSender with backpressure-park + cancel-aware send (BACKPRESSURE_POLL loop checks the CancellationToken), StreamQueues with INDEPENDENT pcm and event queues so an event-consumer stall can never block audio. These types are currently used by nothing but tests/streaming_failures.rs, which already encodes the deadlock/backpressure invariants (slow consumer, queue independence, cancel-on-packet-boundary, partial-output-on-disk-full). Do not design a new transport; arm this one.

DESIGN DECISIONS AND WHY:
- Keep accumulating the full Vec<f32> alongside the sink. SynthesizedAudio stays unchanged, so ALL existing callers (file output, resident daemon, FFI, make-video, the e2e byte-identity gate between resident and non-resident paths) are untouched. The sink is additive. Rationale: doctrine "correctness outranks speed"; we must not perturb any existing contract to gain streaming.
- Sink granularity is the codec packet (frames_per_packet worth of samples), NOT individual samples; packet size wiring is the sibling subtask (do not couple them - this bead can land with the constant still 4).
- The sink send must use the cancel-aware bounded send so a stalled consumer parks the codec worker, which in turn backpressures the generator through the bounded frame channel - end-to-end flow control with zero new mechanism. If the token cancels while parked, the worker exits cleanly (this is the tested semantics of BoundedSender::send).
- The blocking library facade is preserved (AGENTS Product Shape: "Streaming synthesis hands the caller PCM chunks through a bounded callback/iterator, still from a blocking facade"). No async surfaces.
- Set ttfa at the moment the FIRST packet is handed to the sink (or appended, when no sink), so ttfa_ms becomes a delivery time once the CLI consumes the sink.
- Revise files in place (AGENTS: no file proliferation, no V2 files); no new crates.

ERROR/EDGE SEMANTICS: sink send failure = cancellation (worker stops, synthesize returns EngineError::Cancelled path consistent with existing cancel semantics); tail flush (synth.rs:1633) also goes through the sink; zero-frame utterances (immediate EOS) produce no packets and that is a distinct, tested outcome.

TESTS (unit tests per the ftts-conformance observability convention): (a) sink receives exactly the same concatenated samples as the returned pcm Vec, bit-identical, across packet schedules 1/2/4 and a tail-partial packet; (b) slow-sink backpressure parks the generator without deadlock (bounded frame channel fills, then drains); (c) cancel while parked exits within one packet; (d) zero-frame utterance: sink sees nothing, no hang. Extend, do not duplicate, streaming_failures.rs coverage.

WHY THIS BEAD IS FIRST: it is the highest-leverage single edit in the repo (the decoded packet already exists in a local variable at synth.rs:1628); every other RT0/RT1 bead consumes this seam.
close_reason: Landed and proven on-machine. Core seam: synth::synthesize gained pcm_sink: Option<&mut dyn PcmPacketSink> (trait: deliver(&[f32], frames)); codec worker delivers each packet BEFORE buffer append + ttfa mark, so ttfa is a delivery time with a sink attached; SynthesizedAudio unchanged; all 3 callers (CLI, resident, FFI) pass None. Evidence: 4 model-gated e2e tests green vs real model (release, M4 Pro): bit-identical sink==buffer w/ exact packet accounting incl tail partial; slow-sink (25ms/packet) backpressure, output bit-identical to no-sink reference; failing-sink abort; cancel-after-first-delivery keeps bit-exact prefix of full-run audio. Debug gate: skip-honest without model, 69+4 tests green. DEVIATIONS from spec, with rationale: (1) transport is a sink TRAIT at the seam, not BoundedSender<PcmPacket> directly - PcmPacket is i16 while the codec/FFI/identity gates are f32-native; conversion stays at each writer (CLI raw, future session), and BoundedSender remains the queued-consumer transport (session runtime bead) wrapping this trait; (2) packet-schedule 1/2/4 matrix deferred to frankentts-6xcf where the schedule becomes variable (worker still hardcodes 4); (3) zero-frame sink-never-called case not directly claimable (EOS masked first 2 frames, sampling-dependent) - covered indirectly by exact packet accounting; noted in test file docs. Committed: 00c8d01 (core, swept in peer's shared-tree commit) + this session's test commit.

title: [RT0] CLI live emission: raw bytes + audio_chunk/frame events during synthesis
description:
Wire the CLI to the live PCM sink: raw-mode bytes and robot audio_chunk/frame events emitted DURING synthesis, replacing the post-hoc chunking loop.

CURRENT SHAPE. The whole synth call sits between stage{synthesis,begin/end} with nothing written (ftts-cli/src/lib.rs:1672-1709); afterwards the finished buffer is sliced and written via AudioOutput::write_packet (lib.rs:1714-1718, bytes hit stdout at :2075-2083 through an io::stdout().lock() LineWriter created at :166). The engine observer is a no-op closure (lib.rs:1666). The `frame` robot event is catalogued (robot.rs:248) but never emitted in production. audio_chunk fields: run_id, byte_offset, bytes, duration_ms, packet_frames, sink (lib.rs:2088-2100).

CHANGE:
- In raw mode (--stream raw): the sink writes each packet's s16le bytes to stdout AS DECODED, with an explicit flush per packet (the LineWriter's line-based flushing is incidental on binary data - do not rely on it; latency now depends on flush discipline). Events stay on stderr - the one-contract rule (chosen once at lib.rs:1185-1189) is unchanged: PCM never interleaves with NDJSON.
- In robot mode with file/none sink: emit audio_chunk at decode time with true byte_offset/bytes accounting; the output stage now overlaps synthesis. Emit stage{output,begin} when the first packet arrives and stage{output,end} after the tail flush; event ORDER changes but no event SHAPE changes, so SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1 (the frozen-fixture contract test validates shapes, not inter-event ordering; verify that assumption against the fixture and note it in the test).
- Wire the SynthesisObserver: replace the no-op closure with one that forwards FrameProgress to the robot `frame` event (index, total_estimate from the admission plan, elapsed_ms). This event was designed for exactly this and has never fired; emitting it needs no schema bump. Rate-limit consideration: at 12.5 Hz a frame event per frame is ~12 lines/sec - acceptable for NDJSON consumers; do NOT batch (agents want live progress), but document the rate in the event catalogue.
- run_complete.ttfa_ms becomes an honest delivery time (first bytes handed to the OS pipe/file), inherited from the sink bead's ttfa placement.

BACKPRESSURE POLICY: a slow stdout reader (blocked pipe) parks the sink send, which parks the codec worker, which backpressures the generator - synthesis slows to the consumer's pace instead of buffering unboundedly. This is correct for real-time playback consumers. For file sinks the OS page cache makes this moot.

RESIDENT INTERACTION (decision, load-bearing): the resident daemon's v1 wire protocol delivers one whole f32 blob after complete synthesis (resident.rs:780-793) and is frozen. If live-streaming modes consulted it, every WARM run would silently regress to buffered delivery - the first `say` of a session would stream live and the second would not, which is worse than either behavior alone. RULE: `--stream raw`, and robot runs where live chunk delivery is the point, BYPASS the resident and synthesize in-process (same mechanism as --no-resident), with a stage/diagnostic note saying so. Cost: those runs pay the model load. This is acceptable because the real warm+streaming surface is the RT1 talk session; the resident stays what it is - a warm-start cache for whole-file output. Do NOT extend resident v1. Document the rule in --help and the skill-facing docs.

WHAT NOT TO DO: do not remove the buffered path for non-streaming invocations that need the whole waveform (make-video waveform rendering, m4a conversion via system encoder - both consume the complete buffer). They keep using SynthesizedAudio.pcm.

TESTS (unit tests per the ftts-conformance observability convention): (a) e2e on a multi-sentence paragraph asserts the first audio_chunk LINE appears before the stage{synthesis,end} line in the event stream - NDJSON events on one stream are strictly ordered, so line order IS the proof and needs no timestamps (robot events carry no wall-clock field; do not add one for this); also assert byte_offset sums equal final audio_bytes; (b) raw-mode e2e: reading stdout incrementally observes bytes before the process reports synthesis end on stderr, and the concatenated stream is byte-identical to the buffered-path WAV data section at the same seed; (c) the skill's fail-closed jq harness (exactly one terminal event per run_id, schema-valid every line) still passes; (d) frozen-fixture robot contract test updated for the frame event now actually firing.

FUTURE-SELF NOTE: after this bead, "streaming honesty" language in README/skill docs ("framed only after whole synthesis") becomes stale - the release notes for the shipping version must correct it, claims stated at their tier (streamed bytes are live; sampled outputs remain different-valid-renditions vs f32 reference per DISC-003, unchanged by this work).
close_reason: Landed and proven on-machine (M4 Pro, release, real model). CLI now emits live: in-process synthesis on a scoped thread with channel-backed PcmPacketSink; main thread consumes packets during generation - audio_chunk at decode time, per-packet raw flush, lazy stage{output,begin} at first packet, throttled frame events (<=1/s per frozen catalogue; bead's 'do not batch' was wrong, catalogue won) with total_estimate from ResourceAdmission; consumer-error-wins precedence at CLI layer plus worker-error-wins at synth join (fresh-eyes fix: sink abort reason no longer buried); --stream raw bypasses resident (whole-blob v1 reply cannot stream), documented in --help; buffered post-hoc path retained for resident-served file runs. EVIDENCE: tests/live_stream_cli_e2e.rs green vs real model - (a) first audio_chunk line precedes stage{synthesis,end} line (single-stream ordering proof), output begin inside synthesis window; (b) sum(audio_chunk.bytes)==run_complete.audio_bytes under FTTS_TRIM_TAIL=0; (c) every line strict-closed-validator clean, exactly one terminal event; (d) raw stdout byte-identical to file-mode WAV data section at same seed; (e) raw run leaves resident state dir empty (bypass proof); >=1 frame event with required fields on a multi-second utterance. Also streaming_sink_e2e 4/4 green post precedence fix. Debug gate: skip-honest without model. DEVIATION: 'stage/diagnostic note' for resident bypass implemented as --help doc + code comment, not a runtime stderr line (schema hygiene). Commits: 08a11f2 core, subsequent fmt/fix sweeps by peer agents, d1bf8c7 clippy nit.

title: [RT2] franken_whisper seam contract + replay fixtures
description:
franken_whisper seam contract: pin the cross-project interface the conversation loop needs from fw, coordinate its landing with the fw agent, and check replay fixtures into this repo.

WHY A BEAD HERE FOR WORK THAT MOSTLY LANDS THERE: the loop fails or succeeds at this seam; if it is not pinned, the demo bead blocks on ambiguity. This bead's deliverable is an AGREED WRITTEN CONTRACT plus test fixtures - not fw code. Coordinate via MCP Agent Mail using THIS bead's id as thread_id (project convention), with the agent working in /dp/franken_whisper.

WHAT FW HAS TODAY (verified 2026-08-21, so future-self knows the delta):
- Real VAD as a first-class pipeline stage with full knobs (--vad-threshold, --vad-min-silence-ms, etc.) and vad.start/vad.ok stage events.
- Speculative streaming transcripts over NDJSON: transcript.partial {text, start_sec, end_sec, confidence, speaker, seq, ts, run_id} emitted immediately from a fast model, then transcript.confirm / transcript.retract / transcript.correct from the quality model (robot.rs:404-455 there; windowed, Beta-posterior-controlled).
- BUT: microphone capture is FIXED-DURATION record-then-transcribe (audio.rs:1317 shells out to ffmpeg -t <seconds> then transcribes the file; default 15 s). There is NO continuous live-mic stream and NO explicit end-of-turn event (VAD min-silence is a segmentation parameter, not conversational endpointing).

THE CONTRACT TO PIN (our side's requirements, to negotiate with the fw agent):
1. CONTINUOUS MIC MODE: indefinite capture, incremental transcription, NDJSON out - the existing speculative-transcript vocabulary is already right for this; the gap is capture plumbing (and its AEC compatibility - see the AEC spike bead: capture should be routable through VoiceProcessingIO or expose raw enough capture that the orchestrator can be).
2. ENDPOINT EVENT: an explicit turn-end signal (e.g. endpoint or transcript.final) distinct from VAD segmentation, carrying the finalized utterance text and timing - the trigger the orchestrator hands to the LLM. Semantic endpointing (model predicts turn-end, as Kyutai's stack does) is a nice-to-have; silence-based (~300 ms min-silence + max backstop) is the v1 ask.
3. SPEECH-START SIGNAL: early, low-latency "user started speaking" (vad.start already exists - confirm its latency and payload) - this is the barge-in trigger input.
4. ENVELOPE DIVERGENCES DOCUMENTED, NOT PAPERED OVER: fw schema_version is the STRING "1.0.0"; ftts robot v1 is INTEGER 1 and the talk session is INTEGER 2. fw uses dotted event names (transcript.partial), ftts flat snake_case. The orchestrator must treat each side's envelope on its own terms; neither project should churn its frozen schema for cosmetic alignment. Write this down in the contract so nobody "helpfully" unifies them later.
5. REPLAY FIXTURES: a set of captured/synthesized fw NDJSON streams with realistic timing (normal turn, hesitating speaker, barge-in mid-agent-speech, backchannel-only) checked into THIS repo for the demo's fixture-replay mode and the session e2e's orchestrator-facing cases. Fixtures are the decoupling device: ftts-side work proceeds against them regardless of fw's schedule.

FORM DISCIPLINE (anti-ceremony guard): the machine-consumed FIXTURES are the primary deliverable - running code (the demo's replay mode, the session e2e's orchestrator cases) branches on them. The "contract" is the Agent Mail thread agreement plus a short comment block in the fixture files themselves (event names, timing assumptions, envelope divergences); do NOT produce a standalone spec/interface document - if the fixtures plus their header comments cannot carry the contract, the contract is too complicated and should be simplified instead of documented harder.

ACCEPTANCE: contract agreed in the Agent Mail thread (both agents acked); fixtures present and consumed by the demo's replay mode; any fw-side beads filed IN FW's tracker referenced from the thread (not duplicated here).
close_reason: INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED (fixtures peer-authored in ef2e94d; this session verified). Delivered: (1) seam contract AGREED on the record - two-way Agent Mail exchange with the fw agent (msg ids a58f0569/1d70e843/9dc7ce87/35c5e492/6ee5e793 + their replies), full mapping recorded verbatim in this bead's comments: continuous mic = fw bd-rt-capture-trait-lckq + 'fw robot listen'; end-of-turn = utterance_end{reason:endpoint|timeout|max_len|session_end} distinct from VAD segmentation; barge-in trigger = speech_started (fires ~250-300ms after true onset per fw's min_speech_ms - our >=0.5s rule stacks on top); orchestrator consumes transcript.delta / utterance_end.text, NEVER mutable partials; envelope divergence PERMANENT and documented (fw string '1.1.0' vs ftts int; dotted vs snake_case names); fw event shapes FROZEN at 1.1.0 (their commits 50ac3b15+9da72886) with exact sample lines recorded here. (2) Four replay fixtures in-tree (normal_turn, hesitating_speaker, barge_in_mid_agent_speech, backchannel_only) - MACHINE-CONSUMED by the rot-guard suite fw_seam_fixtures.rs (5/5 green this session: envelope+vocabulary, monotone timing, append-only deltas, retract-follows-partial, barge-in trigger ordering), which is the anti-rot gate until the demo's replay mode (frankentts-4ie8, this bead's dependent) becomes the second consumer. (3) Form discipline honored: no standalone spec document - the contract lives in the thread, the bead record, and the fixtures' own headers. fw-side beads live in fw's tracker as agreed (their epic bd-rt-listen-epic-polh).

comments.text: FW EVENT SHAPES FROZEN (fw schema 1.1.0, fw commits 50ac3b15+9da72886, bd-rt-events-ghdx closed; canonical source: fw robot schema, 18 event types; NdjsonStreamValidator in fw src/robot.rs enforces the contract). Sample lines received from fw agent 2026-08-22 for our replay fixtures (exact serialization, insertion-ordered keys) - NORMAL TURN sequence: listen.session_start{source,capture_backend:cpal,sample_rate_hz:48000,fast_model,quality_model,policy:alignatt,step_ms:300,vad:{min_speech_ms:250,endpoint_ms:600,gate_db:9}} -> speech_started{utterance_id,t_session_sec} -> transcript.delta{utterance_id,text,t0_sec,t1_sec,tokens,confidence,stability:committed} (append-only) -> utterance_end{reason:endpoint|timeout|max_len|session_end,text,text_truncated,delta_count} -> listen.session_stats{final:true,ttft_ms,...}. BARGE-IN SEMANTICS: speech_started fires AFTER vad min_speech_ms (~250ms) of sustained voice; t_session_sec is true onset but event arrives ~250-300ms late; our >=0.5s sustained rule stacks on top (speech_started + ~250ms continued speech). Every speech_started pairs 1:1 with utterance_end; false barge-in yields utterance_end with text:"" (contractual). transcript.confirm/correct arrive ASYNC after utterance_end keyed by utterance_id. Terminal rule: success ends session_stats{final:true}; fatal ends run_error last. Orchestrator rule reconfirmed: consume transcript.delta / utterance_end.text, never mutable partials (suppress via --no-partials). Duration/energy hint on speech_started: candidate additive field, file on fw tracker only if it becomes a real ask. REMAINING for this bead: check fixtures into repo WHEN the demo's replay mode exists to consume them (no files before a consumer), derive barge-in timing fixture from these shapes.

title: [BUG] ftts convert fails on the real checkpoint: 478 sections vs MAX_SECTIONS=64
description: OBSERVED 2026-08-08 (VioletSeal): 'ftts convert docs/truth-pack/snapshots/hf -o out.fttsq' fails with 'section count 478 exceeds the cap of 64' (exit 7, staging retained). The .fttsq format intends few large sections (MAX_SECTIONS=64) with many tensors (MAX_TENSORS=16384), but the converter emits one section per tensor (478 for the talker checkpoint). The converter must group tensors into component-level sections (talker body / embeddings / heads / microdecoder / codec / speaker, or per-layer grouping) — a design decision belonging to the in-flight streaming-converter lane (frankentts-p2-converter-8b4, CloudyGorge). BLOCKS: publishing the optimized .fttsq artifact to the model-qwen3-tts-v1 pull release series (raw safetensors shipped there meanwhile — 2.4GB vs the ~1GB a Q8 fttsq would be). Repro is one command; staging file shows the emitted section layout.
close_reason: Converter emits one section per AccessClass (tensors locate by offset); real checkpoint converts in ~16s to a 1.3GB self-verified .fttsq. Enrollment hydrates the speaker encoder from the artifact (bit-identical .spk vs raw, proven on a real recording). title: [QUANT] codec dtype-residency campaign: Q8-compute all-targets route with full evidence gates
description: kbs4 split child B. The only path that actually halves browser codec residency (457 MB f32 -> ~230 MB) is a dtype change, and it must arm on EVERY target at once: the 2026-08-09 revert (codec.rs:697-719) measured that browser-only int8 codec arms break render identity (29.9 dB frame-0 SNR wasm-vs-CLI; sampling turns any epsilon into fully divergent renditions). Shape: converter writes Q8 (canonical symmetric per-output-channel) codec tensors into the artifact; runtime computes from Q8 on all targets via the existing armed dense_linear path (memo becomes identity); FTTS_INT8_CODEC stays the kill switch; RVQ codebooks + all norms stay f32 per doctrine #2. Gates: codec_decode_l2 ratchet receipts at all eight transformer seams with measured deltas ledgered in DISCREPANCIES (DISC entry + review date), streaming==offline bit-identity under the Q8 route, i32-overflow proof at codec K=7168 (constant already exists), interleaved same-thermal-window native speed A/B (2026-08-09 native measured int8 arm ~3% slower than BLAS f32: 20.5 vs 21.1 ms/frame — the memory win must buy back or explicitly cost that), wasm-vs-CLI render identity restored by construction, and the equivalence-bound listening pair before default-flip. MEASURED CORRECTION to the parent bead premise: bf16 storage is NOT bit-safe for this checkpoint — 99.999% of sampled f32 values have nonzero low mantissa halves, so bf16-residency changes numerics exactly like Q8 and needs the same gates; the stale 'codec f32 1.36 GB' doc numbers (IOS_APP_PLAN.md:141, ftts-wasm lib.rs:312) assume a bf16->f32 doubling that never happens; true residency is 457292548 B (PERF_LEDGER-consistent). Also required before any artifact-embedding revisit: NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE NE-009 records that embedding the codec section into .fttsq WORSENS browser staging peak ~+1.1 GB under the current trailing-only prefix-elision model (2.92 vs 1.84 GB) — embedding only becomes viable paired with this dtype residency plus a mid-artifact elision mechanism (format v2).
